[[3:48|in which the Gentiles searched for the likeness of their idols|De quibus libris scrutabantur gentes similitudinem simulacrorum suorum]], that is, the Gentiles sought to justify the worship of their idols, because they proved from the books of the law that by God's command there were likenesses or images of Cherubim in the tabernacle of Moses, according to that of Exodus: [[Ex 25:18|Thou shalt make also two cherubims of beaten gold, on the two sides of the oracle|Duos Cherubim aureos et productiles facies ex utraque parte oraculi]]. But this proof was of no force, because the images were not set there to be adored or worshipped, nor in order that the things they represented, namely the angelic spirits, should be worshipped as gods, but to signify that those angelic minds stand continually before the Creator to serve him. Now the Gentiles who searched these things out of the law were learned men, and perhaps philosophers, who knew that there is one supreme God and none the less worshipped their own gods. Nay, certain philosophers, such as Porphyry, granted that the law of Moses was given by God, and that idolatry was forbidden in the law only to the Hebrews, saying that the most high God willed to be worshipped by them alone, yet did not will that the gods should not be adored by the other nations: in support of which they alleged that saying of Exodus, [[Ex 22:28|Thou shalt not speak ill of the gods|Diis non detrahes]]; and that other: [[Ex 21:5|if the servant shall say: I love my master|Si dixerit servus, Diligo dominum meum]], [[Ex 21:6|his master shall bring him to the gods|offeret eum dominus diis]] [in both places *dii*, 'gods', is commonly understood of the judges]. Against this foolish opinion Augustine argues in the book of the City of God.

paras.t: Et attulerunt ornamenta sacerdotalia, ad ostendendum quod libenter eis uterentur in templo Dei, si possent, et extra, si liceret, et primitias et decimas, quæ solebant in templo offerri; et suscitaverunt, id est, ad invocandum Deum induxerunt, Nazaræos, videlicet quosdam specialiter Deo consecratos, qui impleverant dies voti sui, quo voverant se Deo vacaturos ad certum tempus: quo expleto, debebant sacrificia quædam offerre Deo, prout in Numeris scribitur. Aliqui vero erant nazaræi per totum tempus vitæ suæ, ut Samson et Samuel. Unde in Judicum libro loquitur Samson: Nazaræus, id est, consecratus Domino sum de utero matris meæ. Idem patet de Samuele primo Regum libro.
paras.en: [[3:49|And they brought the priestly ornaments|Et attulerunt ornamenta sacerdotalia]], to show that they would gladly use them in the temple of God if they could, and outside it if it were lawful, [[3:49|and the first fruits and tithes|et primitias et decimas]], which used to be offered in the temple; [[3:49|and stirred up|et suscitaverunt]], that is, moved to call upon God, [[3:49|the Nazarites|Nazaræos]], namely certain persons specially consecrated to God, [[3:49|that had fulfilled their days|qui impleverant dies]] of their vow, by which they had vowed to give themselves to God for a set time: and when it was over they had to offer certain sacrifices to God, as is written in Numbers[[Num 6:13||]]. But some were Nazarites for the whole time of their life, like Samson and Samuel. Hence in the book of Judges Samson says: [[Judg 16:17|I am a Nazarite, that is to say, consecrated to God from my mother's womb|Nazaræus, id est, consecratus Domino sum de utero matris meæ]]. The same is clear of Samuel in the first book of Kings[[1 Kings 1:11||]].

paras.t: Et clamaverunt voce magna in cœlum, id est ad Deum cœli: cui magnitudo vocalis clamoris accepta non est, nisi in quantum procedit ex magnitudine devotionis et piæ affectionis: Quid faciemus istis, et quo eos ducemus? quasi dicant: Dolemus quod non possumus uti ornamentis sacerdotalibus aliisque prædictis, in templo, nec illuc ducere Nazaræos. Idcirco tu, Domine, subveni. Et sancta tua conculcata sunt et contaminata, id est, sacra templi loca ingressi sunt perfidi, et contaminaverunt ea vitiis gulæ atque luxuriæ ac idololatriis, prout secundo libro clarius continetur. Et sacerdotes tui facti sunt in luctum et in humilitatem, id est, propter tam abominabilia scelera ploraverunt et humiliaverunt se et sunt despecti. Quomodo poterimus subsistere ante faciem eorum, nisi tu, Deus, adjuves nos? Et tubis exclamaverunt, id est, buccinis sacerdotalibus cecinerunt ad impetrandum auxilium Dei, sicut in Josue fecisse leguntur.
paras.en: [[3:50|And they cried with a loud voice toward heaven|Et clamaverunt voce magna in cœlum]], that is, to the God of heaven, to whom the loudness of a spoken cry is not acceptable except in so far as it comes from greatness of devotion and of loving affection: [[3:50|What shall we do with these, and whither shall we carry them?|Quid faciemus istis, et quo eos ducemus?]] As if they said: We grieve that we cannot use the priestly ornaments and the other things just named in the temple, nor bring the Nazarites there. Therefore do thou, O Lord, come to our help. [[3:51|For thy holies are trodden down, and are profaned|Et sancta tua conculcata sunt et contaminata]], that is, the faithless have entered the holy places of the temple and defiled them with the vices of gluttony and lust and with idolatries, as is set out more clearly in the second book[[2 Mach 6:4||]]. And [[3:51|thy priests are in mourning, and are brought low|sacerdotes tui facti sunt in luctum et in humilitatem]], that is, because of such abominable crimes they wept and humbled themselves, and were despised. [[3:53|How shall we be able to stand before their face, unless thou, O God, help us?|Quomodo poterimus subsistere ante faciem eorum, nisi tu, Deus, adjuves nos?]] [[3:54|Then they sounded with trumpets|Et tubis exclamaverunt]], that is, they blew the priestly trumpets to obtain God's help, as they are read to have done in Josue[[Jos 6:1||]].

paras.t: Et post hæc constituit Judas duces populi, id est, exercitum suum ordinate distinxit, et quosdam quibusdam juxta legem præfecit, videlicet tribunos, et centuriones, et pentacontarchos, et decuriones. Porro tribunus præfuit bellatoribus mille; centurio, centum; pentacontarchus, id est quinquagenarius, præfuit quinquaginta; decurio, decem. De quibus in Exodo legitur: Constitue tribunos, et centuriones, et quinquagenarios, et decanos. Et dixit Judas his qui ædificabant domos, et sponsabant uxores, et plantabant vineas, et formidolosis, ut redirent unusquisque in domum suam secundum legem. Nam in Deuteronomii volumine jussum fuit, ut tales redirent ab exercitu ad propria loca, qui de novo erexerant sibi domum aut vineam, aut sponsam acceperant, seu pavidi cordis erant, ne desiderio novæ rei et timore separandi ab ea, vel ex formidine mortis fierent ad bella inepti, aliosque redderent pavidos.
paras.en: [[3:55|And after this, Judas appointed captains over the people|Et post hæc constituit Judas duces populi]], that is, he divided his army in order, and set some over others according to the law, namely [[3:55|over thousands, and over hundreds, and over fifties, and over tens|tribunos, et centuriones, et pentacontarchos, et decuriones]] [the Latin names the officers: *tribunos, centuriones, pentacontarchos, decuriones*, 'tribunes, centurions, pentacontarchs, decurions']. Now the tribune was over a thousand fighting men; the centurion, over a hundred; the pentacontarch, that is, the captain of fifty, over fifty; the decurion, over ten. Of these we read in Exodus: [[Ex 18:21|appoint of them rulers of thousands, and of hundreds, and of fifties, and of tens|Constitue tribunos, et centuriones, et quinquagenarios, et decanos]]. [[3:56|And he said to them that were building houses, or had betrothed wives, or were planting vineyards, or were fearful, that they should return every man to his house, according to the law.|Et dixit Judas his qui ædificabant domos, et sponsabant uxores, et plantabant vineas, et formidolosis, ut redirent unusquisque in domum suam secundum legem]] For in the book of Deuteronomy it was commanded that such men should go back from the army to their own homes, as had newly set up for themselves a house[[Deut 20:5||]] or a vineyard[[Deut 20:6||]], or had taken a bride[[Deut 20:7||]], or were of fearful heart[[Deut 20:8||]]: lest through desire of the new thing and fear of being parted from it, or through dread of death, they should become unfit for war and make others fearful.

paras.t: Et moverunt Judas et sui, et etiam hostes, castra, id est turmas suas. Et ait Judas bellatoribus suis: Accingimini, id est, armis accingite vos, et estote filii potentes, id est fortes corde et corpore, confidentes in Deo; quoniam melius, id est commendabilius, magisque meritorium, est nobis mori in bello justo ex parte nostri, quod inimus ex caritate et zelo justitiæ pro divini cultus et boni communis defensione: quod æquipollet martyrio; quam videre mala gentis nostræ et sanctorum, id est adversitates, mortes et profanationes populi nostri et sacrorum locorum. Sicut autem fuerit voluntas in cœlo, sic fiat.
paras.en: [[3:57|So they removed|Et moverunt]], Judas and his men, and the enemy as well, [[3:57|the camp|castra]], that is, their troops. [[3:58|And Judas said|Et ait Judas]] to his fighting men: [[3:58|Gird yourselves|Accingimini]], that is, gird yourselves with arms, [[3:58|and be valiant men|et estote filii potentes]] [*filii potentes*, literally 'mighty sons'], that is, strong in heart and body, trusting in God; [[3:59|for it is better|quoniam melius]], that is, more praiseworthy and more meritorious, [[3:59|for us to die in battle|est nobis mori in bello]], in a war that is just on our side, which we enter upon out of charity and zeal for justice in defence of the worship of God and of the common good (which is equal to martyrdom), [[3:59|than to see the evils of our nation, and of the holies|quam videre mala gentis nostræ et sanctorum]], that is, the adversities, deaths and profanations of our people and of the holy places. [[3:60|Nevertheless, as it shall be the will of God in heaven, so be it done|Sicut autem fuerit voluntas in cœlo, sic fiat]].

4.title: Explanatio capituli quarti: Et assumpsit Gorgias quinque millia virorum.
4.title_en: Explanation of the fourth chapter: Then Gorgias took five thousand men.

paras.t: Exsecutio belli, de cujus apparatu dictum est in præcedentibus, describitur hic. Et assumpsit Gorgias quinque millia virorum et mille equites electos, ut in ipsa nocte improvise superveniret exercitui Judæ, et occideret eum. Erat enim Gorgias in hujuscemodi bellorum cautelis, insidiis et circumventionibus plurimum tritus. Et filii qui erant in arce, id est quidam gentiles in arce morantes, erant illis duces, id est, itinera aptiora ostenderunt Gorgiæ ac suis. Et audivit Judas machinationem Gorgiæ: quæ fuit sibi per aliquem revelata, Deo sic ordinante; et surrexit ipse Judas, et potentes, id est fortes viri qui secum erant, percutere virtutem exercituum regis, id est ad interficiendum improvise totum reliquum agmen Antiochi missum a Lysia: ut sic ars arte illuderetur, et industria justi fraudem impii superaret. Adhuc enim dispersus erat exercitus Gorgiæ a castris, id est ab exercitu illo magno a Lysia misso: ad quem exercitum nondum reversus fuit Gorgias cum suis.
paras.en: The carrying out of the war, of whose preparation we spoke in what went before[[1 Mach 3:38||]] [the margin's verse number is only partly legible: I Mach. iii, … et seq.], is described here. [[4:1|Then Gorgias took five thousand men, and a thousand of the best horsemen|Et assumpsit Gorgias quinque millia virorum et mille equites electos]], so as to come upon the army of Judas unawares that very night and slay it. For Gorgias was very practised in the stratagems, ambushes and surprises of wars of this kind[[2 Mach 8:9||]]. And [[4:2|the men that were of the castle|filii qui erant in arce]], that is, certain Gentiles who dwelt in the castle, [[4:2|were their guides|erant illis duces]], that is, they showed Gorgias and his men the better roads. [[4:3|And Judas heard|Et audivit Judas]] of the scheme of Gorgias, which had been revealed to him by someone, God so ordering it; [[4:3|and rose up, he|et surrexit ipse]], Judas, [[4:3|and the valiant men|et potentes]], that is, the strong men who were with him, [[4:3|to attack the king's forces|percutere virtutem exercituum regis]], that is, to fall unawares upon the whole remaining host of Antiochus sent by Lysias and slay it: so that art might thus be mocked by art, and the diligence of the just man overcome the guile of the wicked. [[4:4|For as yet the army was dispersed from the camp|Adhuc enim dispersus erat exercitus Gorgiæ a castris]], that is, from that great army sent by Lysias, to which Gorgias had not yet returned with his men.

paras.t: Et venit Gorgias in castra, id est loca castrorum seu tentoria, Judæ nocte, et neminem invenit; et quærebant eos in montibus. In libro isto specialem difficultatem intelligendi textum, inducit frequens variatio nominum et verborum, quoad numerum, seu de numero singulari ad pluralem, et econverso, atque relatio ad diversa, et introductio appositivorum tertiæ personæ sine expressione suppositivorum. Ideo ad intelligentiam litteræ necessarium est, circumstantiam ejus et præcedentia ac sequentia intueri. Sic et nunc, quum singulariter dictum est, Venit Gorgias et neminem invenit, pluraliter additur, Et quærebant eos in montibus. Sensus est, quod Gorgias et sui quærebant Judam atque exercitum ejus in montibus, ad quos putavit Gorgias Judam et suos ex timore fugisse. Ideo subditur, quoniam dixit ipse Gorgias: Fugiunt hi a nobis.
paras.en: [[4:5|And Gorgias came by night into the camp|Et venit Gorgias in castra]], that is, the place of the camp, or the tents, [[4:5|of Judas|Judæ]], [[4:5|and found no man|et neminem invenit]]; [[4:5|and he sought them in the mountains|et quærebant eos in montibus]] [Denis's text has the plural *quærebant*, “they sought”; the Clementine Vulgate and the Douay-Rheims have the singular]. In this book a particular difficulty in understanding the text is caused by the frequent change of nouns and verbs in number, from the singular to the plural and the other way about, and by their reference to different persons, and by the bringing in of predicates in the third person without their subjects being expressed [in the grammar of the schools the *suppositum* is the subject and the *appositum* what is said of it]. So, to understand the letter, one must look at its context and at what goes before and after. So here too: when it has been said in the singular, [[4:5|And Gorgias came|Venit Gorgias]] [[4:5|and found no man|et neminem invenit]], there is added in the plural, [[4:5|and he sought them in the mountains|et quærebant eos in montibus]]. The sense is that Gorgias and his men sought Judas and his army in the mountains, to which Gorgias thought Judas and his men had fled for fear. Hence it is added, [[4:5|for he said|quoniam dixit]], Gorgias himself: [[4:5|These men flee from us|Fugiunt hi a nobis]].

paras.t: Et quum dies factus esset, apparuit Judas in campo cum tribus millibus virorum tantum, qui tegumenta et gladios non habebant: et hoc propter paupertatem, ut Josephus et Magister in historiis dicunt. Aliis nonnullis videtur hoc stare non posse, quia capitulo præcedenti narrantur Judas et sui in duobus præliis prævaluisse, et spolia occisorum tulisse. Ideo dicunt correctum textum hunc esse: Quoniam tegumenta et gladios non habebant. Ac si dicatur: Ideo non fuerunt cum Juda, nisi tria millia, quia non habuerunt arma et enses pro pluribus. Quamvis autem hoc dictum apparentiam habeat, securius tamen videtur sequi primam expositionem, quia et libri correcti communiter habent, Qui non: quia et Josephus ita refert, qui tamen scribit octo millia fuisse occisa de exercitu Seron, ut patuit in expositione præcedentis capituli. Itaque dici potest, quod tria millia ista non habuerunt tegumenta et gladios ad sufficientiam: sicut aliquis dicitur nudus, quia male seu parum vestitus. Denique primo Regum volumine legitur: Quumque venisset dies prælii, non est inventus ensis et lancea in manu totius populi qui erat cum Saul et Jonatha, excepto Saul et Jonatha filio ejus; et tamen ante prælium illud Saul cum suis expugnaverat Ammonitas, ut legitur primo Regum. Estque probabile quod eorum spolia abstulit, inter quas erant et arma.
paras.en: [[4:6|And when it was day, Judas shewed himself in the plain|Et quum dies factus esset, apparuit Judas in campo]] [[4:6|with three thousand men only|cum tribus millibus virorum tantum]], [[4:6|who neither had armour nor swords|qui tegumenta et gladios non habebant]]: and this because of their poverty, as Josephus and the Master in the Histories [Peter Comestor, in the *Historia Scholastica*] say. To some others it seems that this cannot stand, because in the preceding chapter Judas and his men are told to have prevailed in two battles and to have carried off the spoils of the slain. So they say that this text should be corrected to: *Because* they [[4:6|neither had armour nor swords|tegumenta et gladios non habebant]] [that is, *quoniam*, “because”, in place of *qui*, “who”]. As if it were said: There were only three thousand with Judas because they had not arms and swords for more. But although this saying has some likelihood, it seems safer nevertheless to follow the first explanation: both because the corrected books commonly have *Qui non* [“who … not”], and because Josephus too relates it so, though he writes that eight thousand of Seron's army were slain, as was seen in the explanation of the preceding chapter. And so it can be said that these three thousand had not armour and swords enough: as someone is called naked because he is poorly or scantily clothed. Lastly, in the first volume of Kings we read: [[1 Kings 13:22|And when the day of battle was come, there was neither sword nor spear found in the hand of any of the people that were with Saul and Jonathan, except Saul and Jonathan his son|Quumque venisset dies prælii, non est inventus ensis et lancea in manu totius populi qui erat cum Saul et Jonatha, excepto Saul et Jonatha filio ejus]]; and yet before that battle Saul with his men had defeated the Ammonites[[1 Kings 11:11||]], as is read in the first of Kings. And it is likely that he carried off their spoils, among which there were arms too.

paras.t: Et viderunt hi qui erant cum Juda, castra gentium valida, et loricatos esse pedites adversariorum, et equitatus, id est equestres, in circuitu eorum, pro defensione et subsidio peditum; et hi, puta equestres, erant docti ad prælium. Judæi autem non erant exercitati in bellicis rebus, nisi forsitan quidam eorum ad aliquantulum tempus. Et ait Judas viris qui secum erant: Ne timueritis multitudinem eorum. Mementote quomodo salvi facti sunt, id est a morte et occisione Ægyptiorum erepti, patres nostri in mari Rubro, id est in siccato fundo maris illius. Tanquam dicat: Non propria et humana, sed divina virtute prævalere confidite. Et nunc clamemus in cælum, id est ad Deum cæli, tam fervide, ut oratio nostra ad ipsum pertingat: qui tamen vere ubique est. Juxta quod in Ecclesiastico dicitur: Oratio justi penetrat cælos. Et miserebitur nostri Dominus, et memor erit testamenti patrum nostrorum, id est pacti quod iniit et percussit cum eis, dicens, quod pugnantes in ipso confidentes juvaret. Itaque Judas implevit illud Deuteronomii: Si exieris ad bellum, et videris equitatum et currus, et majorem quam tu habes, adversarii exercitus multitudinem, non timebis eos. Appropinquante autem prælio, stabit sacerdos ante faciem exercitus, dicens: Audi, Israel: vos hodie contra inimicos vestros pugnam committitis; nolite metuere, nolite cedere, quia Dominus in medio vestri est, et pro vobis dimicabit.
paras.en: [[4:7|And they saw|Et viderunt]], those who were with Judas, [[4:7|the camp of the Gentiles that it was strong|castra gentium valida]], [[4:7|and the men in breastplates|et loricatos]], that is, that the enemy's foot-soldiers wore breastplates, [[4:7|and the horsemen|et equitatus]], that is, mounted men, [[4:7|round about them|in circuitu eorum]], for the defence and support of the foot; [[4:7|and these|et hi]], namely the horsemen, were [[4:7|trained up to war|docti ad prælium]]. But the Jews were not practised in the things of war, except perhaps some of them for a little while. [[4:8|And Judas said to the men that were with him|Et ait Judas viris qui secum erant]]: [[4:8|Fear ye not their multitude|Ne timueritis multitudinem eorum]]. [[4:9|Remember in what manner|Mementote quomodo]] [[4:9|our fathers|patres nostri]] [[4:9|were saved|salvi facti sunt]], that is, were snatched from death and slaughter at the hands of the Egyptians, [[4:9|in the Red Sea|in mari Rubro]][[Ex 14:21||]], that is, on the dried-up bottom of that sea. As though he said: Trust that you will prevail not by your own human strength but by the power of God. [[4:10|And now let us cry to heaven|Et nunc clamemus in cælum]], that is, to the God of heaven, so fervently that our prayer may reach him: though in truth he is everywhere. According to what is said in Ecclesiasticus: The prayer of the just pierces the heavens[[Ecclus 35:21||]] [the margin gives Ecclus. xxxv, 21, where the text reads: “The prayer of him that humbleth himself, shall pierce the clouds”; Denis quotes it loosely]. And [[4:10|the Lord will have mercy on us, and will remember the covenant of our fathers|miserebitur nostri Dominus, et memor erit testamenti patrum nostrorum]], that is, of the pact which he made and struck with them, saying that he would help those who fight trusting in him. So Judas fulfilled that word of Deuteronomy: [[Deut 20:1|If thou go out to war|Si exieris ad bellum]], [[Deut 20:1|and see horsemen and chariots, and the numbers of the enemy's army greater than thine, thou shalt not fear them|et videris equitatum et currus, et majorem quam tu habes, adversarii exercitus multitudinem, non timebis eos]]. [[Deut 20:2|And when the battle is now at hand, the priest shall stand before the army|Appropinquante autem prælio, stabit sacerdos ante faciem exercitus]], saying: [[Deut 20:3|Hear, O Israel, you join battle this day against your enemies|Audi, Israel: vos hodie contra inimicos vestros pugnam committitis]]: [[Deut 20:3|be not afraid, do not give back|nolite metuere, nolite cedere]], [[Deut 20:4|Because the Lord your God is in the midst of you, and will fight for you|quia Dominus in medio vestri est, et pro vobis dimicabit]].

paras.t: Et levaverunt alienigenæ, id est exercitus Lysiæ, oculos suos, et viderunt eos, scilicet Judam et suos, venientes ex adverso. Et tuba cecinerunt qui fuerant cum Juda, in signum audaciæ et confidentiæ magnæ in Deo. Nempe, secundum Josephum, Judas inter cetera dixit ad suos: Etiam nudis corporibus pugnare debemus et Deum invocare, qui sæpius nos inermes contra plures et armatos victoriam fecit acquirere. Et persecutus est Judas alienigenas fugientes.
paras.en: [[4:12|And the strangers lifted up|Et levaverunt alienigenæ]], that is, the army of Lysias, [[4:12|their eyes, and saw them|oculos suos, et viderunt eos]], namely Judas and his men, [[4:12|coming against them|venientes ex adverso]]. And [[4:13|they that were with Judas sounded the trumpet|tuba cecinerunt qui fuerant cum Juda]], as a sign of boldness and of great confidence in God. For according to Josephus, Judas said to his men among other things: We ought to fight even with naked bodies and to call upon God, who has often made us, unarmed, win the victory against men more numerous and armed. And Judas [[4:15|pursued|persecutus est]] the strangers as they fled.

paras.t: Et apparuit pars quædam prospiciens de monte, id est pars exercitus quem Gorgias assumpsit ut Judam expugnaret: cujus exercitus pars prospexit in campum de monte, in quo Gorgias quæsierat Judam. Et vidit Gorgias quod in fugam conversi sunt sui, id est exercitus ille missus a Lysia: de quo exercitu Gorgias millia sua accepit; et succensa sunt castra, id est tentoria seu tabernacula suorum, quæ Judas succendit illis fugatis. Quibus illi, puta Gorgias et ejus exercitus, conspectis, timuerunt valde. Et fugerunt omnes in campo alienigenarum.
paras.en: And [[4:19|part of them appeared, looking forth from the mountain|apparuit pars quædam prospiciens de monte]], that is, part of the army which Gorgias took to attack Judas: part of that army looked out over the plain from the mountain on which Gorgias had sought Judas. [[4:20|And Gorgias saw that his men were put to flight|Et vidit Gorgias quod in fugam conversi sunt sui]], that is, that army sent by Lysias, from which Gorgias had taken his thousands; [[4:20|and that they had set fire to the camp|et succensa sunt castra]], that is, the tents or tabernacles of his men, which Judas set on fire when they had been put to flight. [[4:21|And when they had seen this|Quibus illi]], namely Gorgias and his army, [[4:21|they were seized with great fear|conspectis, timuerunt valde]]. [[4:22|So they all fled away into the land of the strangers|Et fugerunt omnes in campo alienigenarum]].

paras.t: Et acceperunt Judas et ejus exercitus, aurum multum et argentum et hyacinthum et purpuram marinam et opes magnas: quæ omnia a fugientibus erant relicta in campo. Hyacinthus autem interdum pro flore, quandoque pro gemma, aliquando pro genere panni accipitur. Has autem divitias pro parte attulerunt mercatores, qui venerunt ad emendum Judæos in servos, quos præsupposuerunt vincendos.
paras.en: And Judas and his army [[4:23|got much gold, and silver, and blue silk, and purple of the sea, and great riches|aurum multum et argentum et hyacinthum et purpuram marinam et opes magnas]], all of which had been left in the plain by those who fled. Now *hyacinth* [here rendered “blue silk”] is taken sometimes for a flower, sometimes for a gem, sometimes for a kind of cloth. These riches had in part been brought by the merchants who came to buy the Jews as slaves, taking it for granted that they would be conquered.

paras.t: Et conversi Judas et sui a collectione spoliorum, hymnum canebant, Deo gratias referendo, et ei, non suis viribus victoriam adscribendo, neque inaniter gloriando: ideo meruerunt majorem sortiri triumphum, sicut in textu consequenter describitur: quia et ipsum Lysiam personaliter contra eos venientem cum sexaginta millibus peditum et quinque millibus equitum superaverunt; nec est difficultas in littera. Et benedicebant Deum in cælum, erigendo corda sua cum manibus et vultu ad cælos, juxta illud Threnorum: Levemus corda nostra cum manibus ad Dominum in cælos.
paras.en: [[4:24|And returning|Et conversi]], Judas and his men, from gathering the spoils, [[4:24|they sung a hymn|hymnum canebant]], giving thanks to God and ascribing the victory to him, not to their own strength, and not boasting vainly: therefore they deserved to win a greater triumph, as the text goes on to describe: for they overcame Lysias himself too, when he came against them in person with sixty thousand foot and five thousand horse[[4:28||]]; nor is there any difficulty in the letter. And they [[4:24|blessed God in heaven|benedicebant Deum in cælum]], lifting up their hearts, with their hands and faces, to heaven, according to that of Lamentations: [[Lam 3:41|Let us lift up our hearts with our hands to the Lord in the heavens|Levemus corda nostra cum manibus ad Dominum in cælos]].

paras.t: Et viderunt, Judas et sui, exercitum fortem Lysiæ, ut tactum est; et oravit Judas: Benedictus es, Salvator Israel, id est liberator et adjutor, imo et beatificator Israeliticæ plebis in te sperantis. Incepitque Judas orationem suam a laudibus Dei, quoniam oratio laudibus Dei admixta, exaudibilior est, juxta illud Psalmi: Laudans invocabo Dominum, et ab inimicis meis salvus ero. Qui contrivisti impetum potentis, id est Goliath gigantis, in manu David: qui (ut primo Regum legitur) dixit Goliath, Dabit te Dominus in manu mea, et auferam caput tuum; et tradidisti castra alienigenarum, scilicet Philistinorum, in manu Jonathæ: quod qualiter factum sit, primo Regum diffuse narratur.
paras.en: [[4:30|And they saw|Et viderunt]], Judas and his men, [[4:30|that the army was strong|exercitum fortem]], the army of Lysias, as has been touched on; [[4:30|and he prayed|et oravit]], Judas: [[4:30|Blessed art thou, O Saviour of Israel|Benedictus es, Salvator Israel]], that is, the deliverer and helper, nay, the giver of bliss, of the Israelite people that hopes in thee. Judas began his prayer with the praises of God, since prayer mingled with God's praises is the more readily heard, according to that of the Psalm: [[Ps 17:4|Praising, I will call upon the Lord: and I shall be saved from my enemies|Laudans invocabo Dominum, et ab inimicis meis salvus ero]]. [[4:30|who didst break the violence of the mighty|Qui contrivisti impetum potentis]], that is, of the giant Goliath, [[4:30|by the hand of thy servant David|in manu David]]: who (as is read in the first of Kings) said to Goliath: [[1 Kings 17:46|the Lord will deliver thee into my hand|Dabit te Dominus in manu mea]], and I will [[1 Kings 17:46|take away thy head|auferam caput tuum]]; [[4:30|and didst deliver up the camp of the strangers|et tradidisti castra alienigenarum]], namely of the Philistines, [[4:30|into the hands of Jonathan|in manu Jonathæ]]: how this was done is told at length in the first of Kings[[1 Kings 14:6||]].

paras.t: Conclude, id est, coarcta et vince, exercitum istum in manu populi tui Israel, et confundantur in exercitu suo, id est in præsumptione et confidentia, qua de sua multitudine præsumunt et extolluntur. Vel, In exercitu suo, id est in debellatione sui exercitus, quia hoc eis confusibile erit, quod tantus eorum exercitus a nobis multo paucioribus fuerit debellatus. Da illis formidinem, et tabefac, id est, stupidam ac debilem redde, audaciam virtutis, id est potestatis seu turmæ, eorum. Sic enim ad libitum alterare hominum corda, Dei est proprium, sicut est dictum. Et commoveantur contritione sua, id est, de sua destructione ipsimet admirentur, quia omnipotentiam tuam, operationemque intimam et secretam ignorant. Dejice eos gladio diligentium te. Cognovit enim Judas, quod ipse et fideles qui erant secum, erant in caritate. Hoc in quantum cognovit, vel probabiliter per certa caritatis opera atque judicia, vel certitudinaliter ex revelatione divina seu inspiratione occulta.
paras.en: [[4:31|Shut up|Conclude]], that is, hem in and overcome, [[4:31|this army in the hands of thy people Israel|exercitum istum in manu populi tui Israel]], [[4:31|and let them be confounded in their host|et confundantur in exercitu suo]], that is, in the presumption and confidence with which they presume upon their numbers and are puffed up. Or, [[4:31|in their host|In exercitu suo]], that is, in the defeat of their army: for this will be a confusion to them, that so great an army of theirs should have been defeated by us who are far fewer. [[4:32|Strike them with fear|Da illis formidinem]], and cause to [[4:32|languish|tabefac]], that is, make dull and feeble, [[4:32|the boldness of their strength|audaciam virtutis]], that is, of their power or of their troop [Latin *virtus*, which means a host as well as might]. For so to change men's hearts at will is proper to God, as has been said[[Prov 21:1||]]. And [[4:32|let them quake at their own destruction|commoveantur contritione sua]], that is, let them wonder for themselves at their own destruction, because they do not know thy almighty power and thy inward and secret working. [[4:33|Cast them down with the sword of them that love thee|Dejice eos gladio diligentium te]]. For Judas knew that he and the faithful who were with him were in charity. This he knew, so far as he knew it, either with probability, through sure works and signs of charity, or with certainty, by divine revelation or hidden inspiration.

paras.t: Et commiserunt prælium; et ceciderunt de exercitu Lysiæ quinque millia virorum. Videns autem Lysias Judæorum audaciam, quia parati sunt aut vivere cum libertate et observantia legis, aut mori fortiter, id est virtuose, pro defensione cultus divini et boni communis, abiit Antiochiam.
paras.en: [[4:34|And they joined battle: and there fell of the army of Lysias five thousand men|Et commiserunt prælium; et ceciderunt de exercitu Lysiæ quinque millia virorum]]. [[4:35|And when Lysias saw|Videns autem Lysias]] [[4:35|how bold the Jews were|Judæorum audaciam]], [[4:35|that they were ready either to live|quia parati sunt aut vivere]] with freedom and in keeping of the law, [[4:35|or to die manfully|aut mori fortiter]], that is, virtuously, for the defence of the worship of God and of the common good, [[4:35|he went to Antioch|abiit Antiochiam]].

paras.t: Præterea Judas tot sortitus victorias, sollicitus fuit de renovatione cultus divini, ut subditur. Dixit autem Judas et fratres ejus: Ecce contriti, id est destructi, victi, dissipati, sunt inimici nostri pro magna parte; ascendamus nunc Jerosolymam in alto sitam, mundare sancta et renovare, id est ad purgandum sacra loca, templum atque altaria a gentilibus profanata, et ad renovandum cultum Dei in eis. Et congregatus est omnis exercitus, et ascenderunt in montem Sion. Et viderunt sanctificationem desertam, id est, templum quasi in solitudinem versum, et altare tam thymiamatis quam holocausti, profanatum, quia super unum illorum posuerat sceleratissimus Antiochus idolum Jovis, et in atriis templi virgulta nata, sicut in saltu, id est in nemore, et pastophoria diruta, id est destructas mansiunculas quæ erant in circuitu templi pro requie sacerdotum dum ministrabant, seu refectione offerentium hostias, quarum partem cedentem in esum eorum, inibi comederunt.
paras.en: Moreover Judas, having won so many victories, was concerned for the renewal of the worship of God, as follows. [[4:36|Then Judas, and his brethren said|Dixit autem Judas et fratres ejus]]: [[4:36|Behold our enemies are discomfited|Ecce contriti]], that is, destroyed, conquered, scattered, for the most part; [[4:36|let us go up now|ascendamus nunc]] to Jerusalem, which stands on high, [[4:36|to cleanse the holy places, and to repair them|mundare sancta et renovare]], that is, to purify the sacred places, the temple and the altars profaned by the Gentiles, and to renew the worship of God in them. [[4:37|And all the army assembled together, and they went up into Mount Sion|Et congregatus est omnis exercitus, et ascenderunt in montem Sion]]. [[4:38|And they saw the sanctuary desolate|Et viderunt sanctificationem desertam]], that is, the temple turned as it were into a wilderness, [[4:38|and the altar|et altare]], both that of incense and that of holocaust, [[4:38|profaned|profanatum]], because the most wicked Antiochus had set the idol of Jupiter upon one of them, [[4:38|and shrubs growing up in the courts as in a forest|et in atriis templi virgulta nata, sicut in saltu]], that is, in a wood, [[4:38|and the chambers joining to the temple thrown down|et pastophoria diruta]], that is, the little lodgings round about the temple, now destroyed, which served for the rest of the priests while they ministered, or for the refreshment of those who offered victims, who ate there the part of them that fell to them for food.

paras.t: Et sciderunt vestimenta sua præ dolore: in quo ostenderunt fervidum zelum quem pro divinæ majestatis honorificentia habuerunt; et exclamabant tubis signorum, id est tubis per quas multa significabantur; clanxeruntque tubis lugubri sonitu, ut sic ad ampliorem provocarentur lamentationem in casu tam tristi. Denique, per harum clangorem tubarum populus excitabatur, dum castra erant movenda; populus quoque et principes convocabantur ad tractanda consilia. In bellis quoque et festis ac epulis erat usus tubarum istarum, prout in Numerorum libro plenius scriptum est.
paras.en: [[4:39|And they rent their garments|Et sciderunt vestimenta sua]] for grief: in which they showed the fervent zeal they had for the honour of the divine majesty; [[4:40|and they sounded with the trumpets of alarm|et exclamabant tubis signorum]] [Latin *tubis signorum*, “trumpets of signals”], that is, trumpets by which many things were signified; and they blew the trumpets with a mournful sound, so as to be stirred thus to fuller lamentation in so sad a case. Further, by the blast of these trumpets the people were roused when the camp was to be moved; the people too and the princes were called together by them to take counsel. In wars also, and at feasts and banquets, these trumpets were used, as is written more fully in the book of Numbers[[Num 10:2||]][[Num 10:10||]].

paras.t: Tunc ordinavit Judas viros, id est fortes et strenuos milites, ut pugnarent adversus eos qui erant in arce: ne impii illi molestias inferrent per jacula, purgantibus templum. Et elegit sacerdotes sine macula, id est, quos putavit magis devotos, qui erant magis idonei reformare collapsa, et purgare polluta; et tulerunt, id est, extra templum portaverunt, lapides contaminationis: ex quibus constructa fuit ara Jovis circa altare Dei, super quod positum fuit Jovis simulacrum, ut patuit primo capitulo; in locum immundum, id est vilem et sordidum, in detestationem idololatriæ. Et cogitavit de altari holocaustorum, quod profanatum fuerat, per hoc quod statua Jovis superposita erat ei, quid de eo faceret. Et incidit illi ex illuminatione divina, consilium bonum, ut destrueret illud, propter abusiones sacrilegas in eo commissas, ne forte esset illis in opprobrium, id est, ne ipse Judas et sui sustinerent confusionem, si altare illud relinqueret integrum, quod sic erat per idololatras violatum. Et demoliti sunt, id est destruxerunt, illud, et posuerunt lapides ejus in monte domus, id est in monte Sion, in quo templum fuerat situm, in loco apto, id est mundo, eo quod lapides illi primo erant consecrati ad cultum et sacrificia Dei, quoadusque veniret Propheta, et responderet de eis, id est, ex divina revelatione doceret, quid esset agendum de illis lapidibus, seu cui essent usui deputandi.
paras.en: [[4:41|Then Judas appointed men|Tunc ordinavit Judas viros]], that is, strong and vigorous soldiers, [[4:41|to fight against them that were in the castle|ut pugnarent adversus eos qui erant in arce]]: lest those wicked men should harass with their darts those who were cleansing the temple. [[4:42|And he chose priests without blemish|Et elegit sacerdotes sine macula]], that is, those he thought the more devout, who were the fitter to restore what had fallen and to cleanse what was defiled; [[4:43|and took away|et tulerunt]], that is, carried out of the temple, [[4:43|the stones that had been defiled|lapides contaminationis]], of which the altar of Jupiter had been built beside the altar of God, upon which the image of Jupiter was set, as was seen in the first chapter[[1 Mach 1:57||]]; [[4:43|into an unclean place|in locum immundum]], that is, a vile and filthy one, in detestation of idolatry. [[4:44|And he considered about the altar of holocausts|Et cogitavit de altari holocaustorum]] [[4:44|that had been profaned|quod profanatum fuerat]] by the statue of Jupiter being set upon it, [[4:44|what he should do with it|quid de eo faceret]]. And [[4:45|a good counsel|consilium bonum]], by divine enlightenment, [[4:45|came into their minds|incidit illi]] [Denis's text has *illi*, “to him”, where the Vulgate has *illis*, “to them”], [[4:45|to pull it down|ut destrueret illud]], because of the sacrilegious abuses committed on it, [[4:45|lest it should be a reproach to them|ne forte esset illis in opprobrium]], that is, lest Judas himself and his men should suffer confusion if he left whole that altar which had been so violated by idolaters. And [[4:45|they threw it down|demoliti sunt]] (that is, destroyed it), and [[4:46|they laid up the stones in the mountain of the temple|posuerunt lapides ejus in monte domus]], that is, on Mount Sion, on which the temple had stood, [[4:46|in a convenient place|in loco apto]], that is, a clean one, because those stones had first been consecrated to the worship and sacrifices of God, [[4:46|till there should come a prophet, and give answer concerning them|quoadusque veniret Propheta, et responderet de eis]], that is, should teach by divine revelation what was to be done with those stones, or to what use they were to be put.

paras.t: Et acceperunt lapides integros secundum legem, id est non sectos, juxta illud Exodi: Quod si altare lapideum feceris mihi, non ædificabis illud de sectis lapidibus. Et in Deuteronomio scriptum est: Ædificabis altare Domino de lapidibus quos ferrum non tetigit, id est de saxis informibus et impolitis. Cujus præcepti ratio litteralis ac mystica ibi expressa est. Et ædificaverunt altare holocaustorum novum, secundum illud quod erat prius, id est instar altaris prioris quod destruxerunt.
paras.en: [[4:47|Then they took whole stones, according to the law|Et acceperunt lapides integros secundum legem]], that is, not cut, according to that of Exodus: [[Ex 20:25|And if thou make an altar of stone unto me, thou shalt not build it of hewn stones|Quod si altare lapideum feceris mihi, non ædificabis illud de sectis lapidibus]]. And in Deuteronomy it is written: [[Deut 27:5|thou shalt build there an altar to the Lord thy God, of stones which iron hath not touched|Ædificabis altare Domino de lapidibus quos ferrum non tetigit]], that is, [[Deut 27:6|of stones not fashioned nor polished|de saxis informibus et impolitis]]. The literal and the mystical reason of this precept are set out there. [[4:47|and built a new altar, according to the former|Et ædificaverunt altare holocaustorum novum, secundum illud quod erat prius]], that is, after the likeness of the former altar which they had destroyed.

paras.t: Et ædificaverunt Sancta, id est, exteriorem templi partem, quæ dicebatur Sanctum seu Sancta, in qua erat altare thymiamatis, reparaverunt, in quibus erat corruptum aut læsum, et quæ intra domum erant intrinsecus, id est interiorem partem templi, quæ dicebatur Sancta sanctorum; et ædem, id est ædes seu mansiones sacerdotum, quæ erant in gyro atrii templi, in quibus tempore officii morabantur, et atria sanctificaverunt, exstirpando virgulta ex eis, et aqua lustrationis cum oratione eadem adspergendo. Et fecerunt vasa sancta nova. Jam enim ex frequenti victoria, spoliis hostium, auro et argento fuerunt ditati. Et per vasa intelliguntur quæcumque instrumenta et utensilia cultus divini in templo. Antiochus namque rapuerat omnia.
paras.en: [[4:48|And they built up the holy places|Et ædificaverunt Sancta]], that is, they repaired the outer part of the temple, which was called the Holy or the Holies, in which stood the altar of incense, wherever anything was spoiled or damaged; [[4:48|and the things that were within the temple|et quæ intra domum erant intrinsecus]], that is, the inner part of the temple, which was called the Holy of holies; and [[4:48|the temple|ædem]], that is, the houses or dwellings of the priests that stood round about the court of the temple, in which they stayed during their time of service [Denis takes *ædes* here for the priests' lodgings], [[4:48|and the courts|et atria]] they [[4:48|sanctified|sanctificaverunt]], rooting the shrubs out of them, and likewise sprinkling them with the water of purification, with prayer. [[4:49|And they made new holy vessels|Et fecerunt vasa sancta nova]]. For by their many victories they had by now been enriched with the spoils of the enemy, with gold and silver. And by *vessels* are understood all the instruments and utensils of the worship of God in the temple. For Antiochus had carried everything off[[1 Mach 1:23||]][[1 Mach 2:8||]][[1 Mach 2:9||]].

paras.t: Et intulerunt candelabrum aureum, super quod erant septem lucernæ seu lampades aureæ, et altare incensorum, super quod ponebatur et cremabatur incensum boni odoris, ut esset in templo odor suavis, non afflictivus, ex crematione animalium, quæ in holocaustum comburebantur, et mensam propositionis in templum. Hæc tria stabant in prima exteriorique parte templi. Atque, ut Dominus in Exodo jussit, mensa ponebatur in parte aquilonari, candelabrum in australi, altare incensi in medio ex opposito Sancti sanctorum. Et incensum posuerunt super altare thymiamatis: quod ex aromaticis speciebus fuit confectum, et congruo tempore incendebatur, prout in Exodo legitur; et accenderunt lucernas septem quæ super candelabrum erant, tres ex uno latere, tresque ex altero, et septima in supremo candelabri, sicut in Exodo describitur plenius. Et posuerunt super mensam panes propositionis calidos sabbato. Et appenderunt vela: unum in medio templi inter Sancta et Sancta sanctorum, aliud in introitu templi: de quibus velis et eorum materiis ac formaturis, habetur in Exodo. Prædicta quoque inungebantur oleo unctionis, quemadmodum in Exodo fieri jussum est: ad quod pertinere potest quod subditur, et consummaverunt omnia opera quæ fecerant. Illa namque inunctio, fuit quasi consummatio operum prædictorum.
paras.en: And they [[4:49|brought in the candlestick|intulerunt candelabrum]] of gold, on which were seven golden lamps or lights, [[4:49|and the altar of incense|et altare incensorum]], on which incense of sweet savour was laid and burnt, so that there might be a sweet smell in the temple, and not the offensive one of the burning of the animals that were burnt in holocaust, [[4:49|and the table|et mensam]] of proposition, [[4:49|into the temple|in templum]]. These three stood in the first and outer part of the temple. And, as the Lord commanded in Exodus, the table was set on the north side, the candlestick on the south[[Ex 26:35||]], the altar of incense in the middle, over against the Holy of holies[[Ex 30:6||]]. [[4:50|And they put incense upon the altar|Et incensum posuerunt super altare]] of incense, which was made of aromatic spices and was burnt at the fitting time, as is read in Exodus[[Ex 30:34||]]; [[4:50|and lighted up the lamps that were upon the candlestick|et accenderunt lucernas septem quæ super candelabrum erant]], seven of them, three on one side, three on the other, and the seventh at the top of the candlestick, as is described more fully in Exodus[[Ex 25:31||]]. [[4:51|And they set the loaves upon the table|Et posuerunt super mensam panes]], the loaves of proposition, hot, on the sabbath. They [[4:51|hung up the veils|appenderunt vela]]: one in the middle of the temple, between the Holies and the Holy of holies, the other at the entrance of the temple: of these veils, their materials and their making, an account is given in Exodus[[Ex 26:31||]]. The things aforesaid were also anointed with the oil of unction, as was commanded to be done in Exodus[[Ex 30:26||]]: and to this may belong what follows, [[4:51|and finished all the works that they had begun to make|et consummaverunt omnia opera quæ fecerant]]. For that anointing was as it were the finishing of the works aforesaid.

paras.t: Et ante matutinum, id est ante auroram, surrexerunt quinta et vicesima die mensis noni, nomine Casleu, de quo dictum est sæpe, centesimi et quadragesimi octavi anni Græcorum. Secundum tempus, id est eodem die, evolutis tribus annis, renovatum est templum a Juda et suis, quo die in specie fuerat profanatum ab Antiocho. Anno enim centesimo quadragesimo quinto, vicesimo quinto die mensis Casleu, exstitit profanatum; anno autem centesimo quadragesimo octavo, vicesimo quinto die mensis præfati, est renovatum: quod non est casualiter, sed divina providentia factum, quæ juxta mensuram culparum, infligit mensuram pœnarum. Renovatum est, inquam, in canticis, id est psalmis et laudibus Dei, et citharis, id est musicis instrumentis ad movendum factis, et cinyris et cymbalis. Et cecidit omnis populus ibi præsens in faciem, prosternens se Deo humiliter ad regratiandum et exorandum.
paras.en: And [[4:52|before the morning|ante matutinum]], that is, before dawn, [[4:52|they arose|surrexerunt]] [[4:52|on the five and twentieth day of the ninth month|quinta et vicesima die mensis noni]], called Casleu, of which there has often been mention, [[4:52|in the hundred and forty-eighth year|centesimi et quadragesimi octavi anni]] of the Greeks. [[4:54|According to the time|Secundum tempus]], that is, on the same day, when three years had gone by, the temple was renewed by Judas and his men, on the very day on which it had been profaned by Antiochus. For in the hundred and forty-fifth year, on the twenty-fifth day of the month Casleu, it was profaned[[1 Mach 1:62||]]; but in the hundred and forty-eighth year, on the twenty-fifth day of the same month, it was renewed: which came about not by chance but by divine providence, which inflicts the measure of punishment according to the measure of the fault[[Deut 25:2||]] [the margin gives Deut. xxv, 3; the words are in Deut 25:2]. It was, I say, [[4:54|dedicated anew|Renovatum est]] [[4:54|with canticles|in canticis]], that is, with psalms and praises of God, [[4:54|and harps|et citharis]], that is, musical instruments made for stirring the soul, [[4:54|and lutes, and cymbals|et cinyris et cymbalis]]. [[4:55|And all the people fell upon their faces|Et cecidit omnis populus ibi præsens in faciem]], prostrating themselves humbly before God to give thanks and to pray.

paras.t: Et fecerunt dedicationem altaris octo diebus, id est, dedicationem seu consecrationem altaris uno die factam, celebraverunt septem diebus sequentibus. Quemadmodum in Ecclesia festa solennia habent octavam: quod inde dicitur tractum. Et obtulerunt holocausta, et salutaria laudis, id est hostias gratiarum actionis, pacificas, spontaneas, et votivas. Et ornaverunt faciem templi coronis aureis, quoniam Rege cæli juvante, regibus terræ prævaluerunt, et scutulis, id est parvis scutis, in signum triumphorum eis desuper concessorum. Et statuit Judas, quem fecerunt principem sacerdotum, et fratres ejus, ut agatur, id est celebretur, dies Dedicationis altaris, ab anno in annum per dies octo, a quinta et vicesima die mensis Casleu, cum lætitia mentis, et gaudio redundante ex corde in corpus. De cujus festivitate Dedicationis fertur a Joanne: Facta sunt Encænia in Jerosolymis; et hiems erat. Mensi etenim Casleu correspondet December, quamvis interdum November in parte.
paras.en: [[4:56|And they kept the dedication of the altar eight days|Et fecerunt dedicationem altaris octo diebus]], that is, the dedication or consecration of the altar, done on one day, they celebrated for the seven days following. Just as in the Church solemn feasts have an octave: which is said to be taken from this. And [[4:56|they offered holocausts|obtulerunt holocausta]], [[4:56|and sacrifices of salvation, and of praise|et salutaria laudis]], that is, victims of thanksgiving, peace offerings, free-will and votive offerings. [[4:57|And they adorned the front of the temple with crowns of gold|Et ornaverunt faciem templi coronis aureis]], because with the help of the King of heaven they had prevailed over the kings of the earth, [[4:57|and escutcheons|et scutulis]], that is, little shields, as a sign of the triumphs granted them from above. [[4:59|And Judas|Et statuit Judas]], whom they had made prince of the priests, [[4:59|and his brethren|et fratres ejus]] decreed that [[4:59|the day of the dedication of the altar|dies Dedicationis altaris]] [[4:59|should be kept|ut agatur]], that is, celebrated, [[4:59|from year to year for eight days|ab anno in annum per dies octo]], [[4:59|from the five and twentieth day of the month of Casleu|a quinta et vicesima die mensis Casleu]], [[4:59|with joy|cum lætitia]] of mind [[4:59|and gladness|et gaudio]] overflowing from the heart into the body. Of this feast of the Dedication John speaks: [[John 10:22|And it was the feast of the dedication at Jerusalem: and it was winter|Facta sunt Encænia in Jerosolymis; et hiems erat]]. For the month of Casleu answers to December, though sometimes in part to November.

paras.t: Et ædificaverunt in tempore illo montem Sion, id est, in monte illo pro defensione templi munimenta fecerunt. Ideo subditur, et per circuitum ejus muros altos, et turres firmas. Josephus refert: Murum in circuitu civitatis et turres altissimas ædificavit Judas. Nequando venirent gentes, et conculcarent eum et templum et ædificia ejus in monte Sion constructa. Et munivit Bethsuram, id est urbem sic dictam, quam tam fortiter muris et turribus roboravit, quod ea quasi fortalitio seu castro contra hostes poterat uti, præsertim contra Idumæos. Unde subjungitur, ut haberet populus Judæorum munitionem contra faciem Idumææ. Quemadmodum enim Esau persecutus est fratrem suum Jacob, sic Idumæi Judæos, prout etiam in Abdia propheta plenius continetur.
paras.en: [[4:60|They built up also at that time Mount Sion|Et ædificaverunt in tempore illo montem Sion]], that is, they made fortifications on that mount for the defence of the temple. Hence it is added, [[4:60|with high walls, and strong towers round about|et per circuitum ejus muros altos, et turres firmas]]. Josephus relates: Judas built a wall round about the city, and very high towers; [[4:60|lest the Gentiles should at any time come, and tread it down|Nequando venirent gentes, et conculcarent eum]], and the temple and its buildings set up on Mount Sion. And [[4:61|he fortified|munivit]] Bethsura [Denis's text reads *munivit Bethsuram*, “he fortified Bethsura”, where the Vulgate has *munivit eum ad custodiendum Bethsuram*], that is, the city of that name, which he strengthened so stoutly with walls and towers that he could use it as a fortress or castle against the enemy, especially against the Idumeans. Hence it is added, [[4:61|that the people might have a defence against Idumea|ut haberet populus Judæorum munitionem contra faciem Idumææ]]. For just as Esau persecuted his brother Jacob[[Gen 27:41||]], so did the Idumeans the Jews, as is also told more fully in the prophet Abdias[[Abd 1:10||]].

paras.t: Postremo, præter prætactam altaris Dedicationem, habuerunt Judæi festum Dedicationis templi Salomonis, ut patet tertio libro Regum: et fuit (ut dicitur) septimo mense, secundum computum Hebræorum. Habuerunt etiam festum Dedicationis templi post reditum a Babylone constructi, ut patet in Esdra. Et ut in Scholastica fertur historia, illa duo festa in dissuetudinem transierunt, ex tempore quo istud cœpit servari. De quo Josephus: Hanc, inquit, festivitatem celebramus, vocantes eam, Lumina, id est festum Luminum, eo quod præter spem hoc nobis splendidum lumen colendæ religionis apparuit.
paras.en: Lastly, besides the dedication of the altar touched on above, the Jews had the feast of the Dedication of Solomon's temple, as appears in the third book of Kings[[3 Kings 8:1||]]: and it was (as is said) in the seventh month[[3 Kings 8:2||]], by the reckoning of the Hebrews. They had also the feast of the Dedication of the temple built after the return from Babylon, as appears in Esdras[[1 Esd 6:16||]] [the margin gives I Esdr. vi, 18; the dedication is told in 1 Esd 6:16–18]. And, as is related in the Scholastic History, those two feasts fell out of use from the time when this one began to be kept. Of it Josephus says: This feast, he says, we celebrate, calling it Lights, that is, the feast of Lights, because beyond our hope this splendid light of practising our religion shone upon us.

5.title: Declaratio capituli quinti: Et factum est, ut audierunt gentes in circuitu.
5.title_en: Explanation of the fifth chapter: Now it came to pass, when the nations round about heard.

paras.t: Describuntur hic varia bella atque victoriæ Judæ contra gentes, in gyro Judææ manentes, quæ prosperitati Judæorum communiter invidebant, sicut in Esdra et Nehemia præcipue innotescit.
paras.en: Here are described the various wars and victories of Judas against the nations dwelling round about Judea, which commonly envied the prosperity of the Jews, as is made known chiefly in Esdras[[1 Esd 4:1||]][[1 Esd 5:1||]] and Nehemias[[2 Esd 2:10||]][[2 Esd 2:19||]][[2 Esd 4:1||]].

paras.t: Et factum est, ut, id est postquam, audierunt gentes in circuitu Judæorum morantes, quia ædificatum est altare templi, et sanctuarium, id est ipsum templum, renovatum est, id est instauratum in suo decore et cultu, sicut prius, id est antequam ab Antiocho profanaretur, iratæ sunt valde, ex invidia, et quia idololatræ erant; et cogitabant tollere genus Jacob, id est, decreverunt trucidare Judæos qui erant inter eos, et cœperunt occidere quosdam de populo Judæorum.
paras.en: [[5:1|Now it came to pass, when|Et factum est, ut]], that is, after, [[5:1|the nations round about heard|audierunt gentes in circuitu]] (the nations, that is, dwelling round about the Jews) [[5:1|that the altar|quia ædificatum est altare templi]] of the temple was built up, [[5:1|and the sanctuary|et sanctuarium]], that is, the temple itself, was renewed [Denis reads *renovatum est*, "was renewed", of the sanctuary], that is, restored in its beauty and worship, [[5:1|as before|sicut prius]], that is, as before it was profaned by Antiochus, [[5:1|that they were exceeding angry|iratæ sunt valde]], out of envy, and because they were idolaters; [[5:2|And they thought to destroy the generation of Jacob|et cogitabant tollere genus Jacob]], that is, they resolved to slaughter the Jews [[5:2|that were among them|qui erant inter eos]], [[5:2|and they began to kill|et cœperunt occidere]] some [[5:2|of the people|de populo]] of the Jews.

paras.t: Et debellabat Judas filios Esau, scilicet Idumæos, et eos qui erant in Acrabathane, id est urbe seu regione sic dicta, qui circumsedebant Israëlitas, id est, arctabant Judæos. Et recordatus est malitiam filiorum Bean, id est habitatorum loci sic nominati, vel natorum ex viro sic dicto, qui erant populo Judæorum in laqueum et scandalum, decipiendo, impingendoque eos. Et anathematizavit, id est maledixit eos, zelo justitiæ, tanquam adversarios Dei et populi sui, et incendit eos in turribus. Et transivit ad filios Ammon, et invenit manum fortem, id est robustum exercitum Ammonitarum, et Timotheum ducem eorum; et contriti sunt Ammonitæ in conspectu eorum, videlicet Judæ et suorum, imo ab ipso Juda et suis; et cepit Gazer, id est urbem famosam sic appellatam, et filios ejus, id est habitatores seu vicos aut oppida subjecta.
paras.en: [[5:3|Then Judas fought against the children of Esau|Et debellabat Judas filios Esau]], namely the Idumeans, [[5:3|and them that were in Acrabathane|et eos qui erant in Acrabathane]], that is, in a city or region so called, [[5:3|because they beset the Israelites round about|qui circumsedebant Israëlitas]], that is, hemmed in the Jews. [[5:4|And he remembered the malice of the children of Bean|Et recordatus est malitiam filiorum Bean]], that is, of the inhabitants of a place so named, or of those born of a man so called, [[5:4|who were a snare and a stumblingblock to the people|qui erant populo Judæorum in laqueum et scandalum]] of the Jews, by deceiving them and making them stumble. [[5:5|and devoted them to utter destruction|Et anathematizavit]], that is, he cursed them [*anathematizare* means both to curse and to devote to destruction], out of zeal for justice, as enemies of God and of his people, [[5:5|and burnt their towers|et incendit eos in turribus]] [Denis has "burnt them in the towers"]. [[5:6|Then he passed over to the children of Ammon, where he found a mighty power|Et transivit ad filios Ammon, et invenit manum fortem]], that is, a strong army of the Ammonites, [[5:6|and Timotheus was their captain|et Timotheum ducem eorum]]; [[5:7|and they were discomfited in their sight|et contriti sunt Ammonitæ in conspectu eorum]], namely of Judas and his men, nay rather by Judas himself and his men; [[5:8|And he took the city of Gazer|et cepit Gazer]], that is, a famous city so called, [[5:8|and her towns|et filios ejus]], that is, its inhabitants, or the villages or towns subject to it [the print reads *filios*, "sons", where the Vulgate has *filias*, "daughters", that is, the towns dependent on a city; Denis's gloss allows either].

paras.t: Et congregatæ sunt gentes. Describitur hic qualiter Judæi habitantes in terra Galaad, et item Judæi habitantes in Galilæa, miserunt ad Judam et ad fratres ejus pro subventione, et planus est textus.
paras.en: And the Gentiles [[5:9|assembled themselves together|Et congregatæ sunt gentes]]. Here it is described how the Jews dwelling in the land of Galaad, and likewise the Jews dwelling in Galilee, sent to Judas and to his brethren for help; and the text is plain.

paras.t: Ut audivit autem Judas et populus ejus sermones, convenit ecclesia magna, id est copiosa fidelium multitudo, cogitare, id est ad inquirendum et deliberandum, quid faceret fratribus, id est proximis suis, qui in tribulatione erant, et expugnabantur ab eis, id est ab inimicis suis, de quibus dictum est supra. Ex his elicitur, quod in arduis causis sit convocandum et celebrandum generale concilium. Dixitque Judas, post diligentem inquisitionem, Simoni fratri suo: Elige tibi viros, et vade et libera fratres tuos in Galilæa, etc. Et dati sunt Simoni viri tria millia; et assumpsit eos, puta Judæos, qui erant habitantes in Galilæa, cum omnibus quæ erant illis, id est cum omnibus rebus ad eos pertinentibus, et adduxit eos in Judæam, ne amplius infestarentur a gentibus.
paras.en: [[5:16|Now when Judas and the people heard these words|Ut audivit autem Judas et populus ejus sermones]], [[5:16|a great assembly met together|convenit ecclesia magna]], that is, a numerous multitude of the faithful, [[5:16|to consider|cogitare]], that is, to inquire and deliberate, [[5:16|what they should do for their brethren|quid faceret fratribus]], that is, their neighbours, [[5:16|that were in trouble, and were assaulted by them|qui in tribulatione erant, et expugnabantur ab eis]], that is, by their enemies, of whom mention was made above. From this it is gathered that in difficult causes a general council should be convoked and held. [[5:17|And Judas said|Dixitque Judas]], after diligent inquiry, [[5:17|to Simon, his brother: Choose thee men, and go, and deliver thy brethren in Galilee|Simoni fratri suo: Elige tibi viros, et vade et libera fratres tuos in Galilæa]], etc. [[5:20|Now three thousand men were allotted to Simon|Et dati sunt Simoni viri tria millia]]; [[5:23|And he took with him those|et assumpsit eos]], namely the Jews, [[5:23|that were in Galilee|qui erant habitantes in Galilæa]], [[5:23|and all that they had|cum omnibus quæ erant illis]], that is, with all the goods belonging to them, [[5:23|and he brought them into Judea|et adduxit eos in Judæam]], so that they should no longer be harried by the Gentiles.

paras.t: Et Judas et Jonathas... qui secum ceperunt octo millia, quia ad acriora pergebant bella. Et occurrerunt eis Nabuthæi: qui videntur fuisse quidam ex Israel sic vocati, et ipsius Judæ amici. Et factum est diluculo quum elevassent Judas et sui oculos suos, ecce populus multus, cujus non erat numerus, per hyperbolen, et erant gentiles, portantes scalas et machinas, ut comprehenderent munitionem, id est fortalitium in quod Judæi confugerant. Et vidit Judas quia cœpit bellum istorum gentilium, oppugnantium locum illum munitum, et eos qui erant in illo; et clamor belli, id est bellantium, vel sonus collisionis armorum, machinarumque bellicarum, ascendit in cælum, id est multum alte. Et venit tribus ordinibus post eos. Divisit enim exercitum suum in tres partes, et sic tribus agminibus distinctis, aggressus est impios illos a tergo. Et exclamaverunt tubis hi qui erant cum Juda, juxta illud Numerorum: Si exieritis ad bellum de terra vestra contra hostes, clangetis ululantibus tubis, et erit recordatio vestri coram Domino Deo vestro, ut eruamini de manibus inimicorum vestrorum; et clamaverunt in oratione: quæ est spiritualis et sonantissima tuba. Et cognoverunt castra, id est exercitus, Timothei, quia Machabæus est, cujus prosperitatem et fortitudinem erant experti. Et percusserunt eos plaga magna, et ceciderunt ex eis fere octo millia virorum. Et divertit Judas in Maspha, id est ad urbem gentilium sic vocatam, non in Maspha, quæ fuit urbs Juda.
paras.en: [[5:24|And Judas Machabeus, and Jonathan|Et Judas et Jonathas]]..., who took with them eight thousand, because they were going to fiercer wars. [[5:25|And the Nabutheans met them|Et occurrerunt eis Nabuthæi]]: who seem to have been certain men of Israel so called, and friends of Judas himself. [[5:30|And it came to pass that early in the morning|Et factum est diluculo]], when Judas and his men [[5:30|lifted up their eyes|elevassent Judas et sui oculos suos]], [[5:30|behold there were people without number|ecce populus multus, cujus non erat numerus]] (by hyperbole), and they were Gentiles, [[5:30|carrying ladders and engines to take the fortress|portantes scalas et machinas, ut comprehenderent munitionem]], that is, the stronghold in which the Jews had taken refuge. [[5:31|And Judas saw that the fight was begun|Et vidit Judas quia cœpit bellum]], the fight of those Gentiles attacking that fortified place and those who were in it; [[5:31|and the cry of the battle|et clamor belli]], that is, of the fighters, or the sound of the clash of arms and of the engines of war, [[5:31|went up to heaven|ascendit in cælum]], that is, very high. [[5:33|And he came with three companies behind them|Et venit tribus ordinibus post eos]]. For he divided his army into three parts, and so, with three distinct columns, attacked those wicked men from behind. [[5:33|and they sounded their trumpets|Et exclamaverunt tubis]], those who were with Judas, according to that of Numbers: [[Num 10:9|If you go forth to war out of your land against the enemies|Si exieritis ad bellum de terra vestra contra hostes]], [[Num 10:9|you shall sound aloud with the trumpets, and there shall be a remembrance of you before the Lord your God, that you may be delivered out of the hands of your enemies|clangetis ululantibus tubis, et erit recordatio vestri coram Domino Deo vestro, ut eruamini de manibus inimicorum vestrorum]]; [[5:33|and cried out in prayer|et clamaverunt in oratione]], which is a spiritual and most resounding trumpet. [[5:34|And the host of Timotheus understood that it was Machabeus|Et cognoverunt castra, id est exercitus, Timothei, quia Machabæus est]] (the host, that is, the army), whose success and strength they had experienced. [[5:34|and they made a great slaughter of them|Et percusserunt eos plaga magna]], [[5:34|and there fell of them|et ceciderunt ex eis]] [[5:34|almost eight thousand men|fere octo millia virorum]]. [[5:35|And Judas turned aside to Maspha|Et divertit Judas in Maspha]], that is, to a city of the Gentiles so called, not to the Maspha which was a city of Juda.

paras.t: Deinde describitur alia ac major debellatio Timothei a Juda. Et misit Judas speculari exercitum, id est, quosdam industriosos misit de suis ad considerandum quantitatem ac dispositionem exercitus Timothei; et renuntiaverunt ei, videlicet Judæ: Quia convenerunt ad eum, id est ad Timotheum, omnes gentes quæ in circuitu nostro sunt, etc. Et dixit Timotheus: Si transierit Judas ad nos prior, transfretando per torrentem ad nos, non poterimus sustinere eum: quia transfretatio illa fuit signum audaciæ et confidentiæ magnæ, quæ multum valet in prælio.
paras.en: Next is described another and greater defeat of Timotheus by Judas. [[5:38|And Judas sent men to view the army|Et misit Judas speculari exercitum]], that is, he sent some capable men of his own to observe the size and the disposition of Timotheus's army; [[5:38|and they brought him word|et renuntiaverunt ei]], that is, to Judas: [[5:38|All the nations, that are round about us, are assembled unto him|Quia convenerunt ad eum, id est ad Timotheum, omnes gentes quæ in circuitu nostro sunt]] (unto him, that is, to Timotheus), etc. [[5:40|And Timotheus said|Et dixit Timotheus]]: [[5:40|if he pass over unto us first|Si transierit Judas ad nos prior]], crossing the torrent to us, [[5:40|we shall not be able to withstand him|non poterimus sustinere eum]]: because that crossing was a sign of great boldness and confidence, which avails much in battle.

paras.t: Et congregavit Judas universos Israëlitas, qui erant in Galaaditide, id est in terra Galaad, quatenus secum morarentur cum securitate in terra Judæ. Et erat Judas congregans extremos, id est ultimos, ne quis hostium improvise irruens percuteret eos: quemadmodum Amalecitæ in deserto percusserunt extremos et lassos agminis filiorum Israel, prout in Exodo et in Deuteronomio legitur. Et exhortabatur populum per totam viam per se ipsum et per scribas ac sacerdotes quos habuit secum, admonendo populum ad virtutes, et grates Deo reddendas. Et ascenderunt in montem Sion, id est in templum situm in monte, et obtulerunt holocausta, pro gratiarum actione quod nemo ex eis cecidisset, donec reverterentur in pace: quod fuit non solum magnum beneficium Dei, sed et grande miraculum, quum in obsidionibus, de quibus in textu fit sermo, soleant fieri strages utrinque.
paras.en: [[5:45|And Judas gathered together all the Israelites that were in the land of Galaad|Et congregavit Judas universos Israëlitas, qui erant in Galaaditide, id est in terra Galaad]], so that they might dwell with him in safety in the land of Juda. [[5:53|And Judas gathered together the hindmost|Et erat Judas congregans extremos]], that is, the last, lest any of the enemy, falling on them unawares, should strike them: as the Amalecites in the desert struck the hindmost and weary of the column of the children of Israel, as we read in Exodus[[Ex 17:8||]] and in Deuteronomy[[Deut 25:18||]]. [[5:53|and he exhorted the people, all the way through|Et exhortabatur populum per totam viam]], by himself and by the scribes and priests whom he had with him, admonishing the people to virtue and to give thanks to God. [[5:54|And they went up to mount Sion|Et ascenderunt in montem Sion]], that is, to the temple set on the mount, [[5:54|and offered holocausts|et obtulerunt holocausta]], in thanksgiving [[5:54|because not one of them was slain, till they had returned in peace|quod nemo ex eis cecidisset, donec reverterentur in pace]]: which was not only a great benefit of God but also a great miracle, since in sieges, of which the text speaks, there is commonly slaughter on both sides.

paras.t: Et in diebus quibus Judas et fratres ejus erant absentes, audivit Josephus, et Azarias princeps virtutis, id est exercitus secum relicti: nam hi duo erant a Juda relicti pro custodia terræ Judæ; res bene gestas a Juda et fratribus ejus, et prælia quæ facta sunt. Et dicit Azarias ille ad Josephum: Faciamus et ipsi nobis nomen, id est famam præclaram. Et præcepit Azarias his qui erant in exercitu suo, ut pergerent secum ad pugnam: ad quod non fuerunt obligati, quia a superiori suo, hoc est a Juda, fuit ei prohibitum assumere bellum, ipso Juda nondum reverso; et abierunt Jamniam, id est ad provinciam sic vocatam. Et exivit Gorgias de civitate, et viri ejus obviam illis; et ceciderunt de populo Israel ad duo millia, et fugati sunt Josephus et Azarias, etc. Cujus dejectionis triplex causa assignatur ex littera. Prima, quia contra virtutem obedientiæ iverunt ad prælium. Secunda, quoniam ex vanitate moti fuerunt, hoc est desiderio famæ et laudis humanæ. Tertia, quia non erant de semine Mathathiæ, per cujus filios Deus præordinavit populo suo victoriam dare.
paras.en: [[5:55|Now in the days that Judas|Et in diebus quibus Judas]] and his brethren were absent, [[5:56|Joseph|audivit Josephus]] [[5:56|and Azarias, captain of the soldiers|et Azarias princeps virtutis]], that is, of the army left with him (for these two had been left by Judas to guard the land of Juda[[5:18||]]), heard [[5:56|of the good success|res bene gestas]] of Judas and his brethren, [[5:56|and the battles that were fought|et prælia quæ facta sunt]]. And that Azarias says to Joseph: [[5:57|Let us also get us a name|Faciamus et ipsi nobis nomen]], that is, a glorious fame. [[5:58|And he gave charge to them that were in his army|Et præcepit Azarias his qui erant in exercitu suo]] (Azarias, that is) to go with him to the fight: to which they were not bound, because he had been forbidden by his superior, that is, by Judas, to undertake war while Judas himself had not yet returned[[5:19||]]; [[5:58|and they went towards Jamnia|et abierunt Jamniam]], that is, to the province so called. [[5:59|And Gorgias and his men went out of the city|Et exivit Gorgias de civitate, et viri ejus obviam illis]] to meet them; and there fell [[5:60|of the people of Israel, about two thousand men|de populo Israel ad duo millia]], [[5:60|Joseph and Azarias were put to flight|et fugati sunt Josephus et Azarias]], etc. A threefold cause of this defeat is given from the letter. First, because they went to battle against the virtue of obedience[[5:61||]]. Second, because they were moved by vanity, that is, by the desire of fame and of human praise[[5:61||]]. Third, because they were not of the seed of Mathathias, through whose sons God had foreordained to give victory to his people[[5:62||]].

paras.t: Et viri Juda, id est ipse Judas potissimum et fratres ejus post eum, deinde propinqui et familiares auxiliarii ejus, magnificati sunt valde potestate, honore, fama, triumphis, et charismatibus gratiæ Dei. Et convenerunt ad eos fausta acclamantes: id est, quidam gentilium, visis tot victoriis et prosperitatibus Judæ ac fratrum et virorum ipsius, venerunt ad ipsos, ad componendum cum eis pacem et amicitiam; acclamabantque eis fausta, id est laudes de eufortuniis seu prosperis eorum successibus.
paras.en: [[5:63|And the men of Juda|Et viri Juda]], that is, Judas himself above all, and his brethren after him, then his kinsmen and familiar helpers, [[5:63|were magnified exceedingly|magnificati sunt valde]] in power, honour, fame, triumphs, and the gifts of the grace of God. [[5:64|And the people assembled to them with joyful acclamations|Et convenerunt ad eos fausta acclamantes]]: that is, certain of the Gentiles, seeing so many victories and successes of Judas and of his brethren and his men, came to them to make peace and friendship with them; and they acclaimed them with words of good omen, that is, praises for their good fortune, or their prosperous successes.

paras.t: In illa die ceciderunt sacerdotes in bello. Quod quidam exponunt de prædictis Josepho et Azaria, qui dicuntur fuisse de stirpe sacerdotali: qui tamen in textu leguntur fugati, non interfecti. Potest quoque exponi de sacerdotibus quibusdam profectis cum eis ad prælium. Dum voluit fortiter facere, id est, quando sacerdos ille quicumque præsumpsit se fortiter acturum, et sine consilio vere prudentis exiit in prælium. Et videtur scriptura ista quasi despective loqui de illis, et a numero plurali ad singularem descendit, sicut fit in libro isto frequenter.
paras.en: [[5:67|In that day some priests fell in battle|In illa die ceciderunt sacerdotes in bello]]. Some explain this of Joseph and Azarias, mentioned above, who are said to have been of priestly stock: yet in the text they are read to have been put to flight, not slain. It can also be explained of certain priests who set out with them to battle. [[5:67|while desiring to do manfully|Dum voluit fortiter facere]], that is, when that priest, whoever he was, presumed that he would act bravely, [[5:67|they went out unadvisedly to fight|sine consilio vere prudentis exiit in prælium]] (without the counsel, that is, of one truly prudent) [Denis's text has the singular here, *voluit … exiit*, "he wished … he went out", where the Vulgate has the plural *volunt … exeunt*; hence his remark that follows]. And this scripture seems to speak of them almost disparagingly, and it comes down from the plural number to the singular, as happens frequently in this book.

6.title: Explanatio capituli sexti: Et rex Antiochus perambulabat
6.title_en: Explanation of the sixth chapter: Now king Antiochus was going through

paras.t: Mors vitiosi Antiochi, et regnatio filii ejus, atque congressio Judæorum contra eum, hic describuntur.
paras.en: The death of the vicious Antiochus, and the reign of his son, and the encounter of the Jews with him, are described here.

paras.t: Et rex Antiochus perambulavit equitando superiores regiones, ad colligendum tributa ab eis. Specialiter autem nitebatur urbem quamdam ditissimam, Elymaidem nomine, spoliare; sed nequivit, quoniam habitatores urbis illius, agnita ejus rapacitate, fugaverunt eum. Quumque abiret cum ingenti tristitia, venit quidam annuntians ei quantas ruinas et mortes sustinuerunt duces ac subditi sui a Judæis, et quia diruerunt, id est, quod Judas ac sui destruxerunt, abominationem, id est idolum Jovis collocatum ab eo super altare templi, et sanctifi[…] muris excelsis.
paras.en: [[6:1|Now king Antiochus was going through|Et rex Antiochus perambulavit]] on horseback [[6:1|the higher countries|superiores regiones]], to collect tribute from them. In particular he strove to plunder a certain very rich city, Elymais by name; but he could not, because the inhabitants of that city, knowing his rapacity, put him to flight. And as he was departing with great sadness, someone came to tell him what great ruin and death his captains and subjects had suffered at the hands of the Jews, and [[6:7|that they had thrown down|quia diruerunt]], that is, that Judas and his men had destroyed, [[6:7|the abomination|abominationem]], that is, the idol of Jupiter set up by him upon the altar of the temple, and [[6:7|the sanctuary|sanctifi]] […] [[6:7|with high walls|muris excelsis]].

paras.t: Et factum est, ut audivit rex sermones istos, expavit Antiochus his auditis, et commotus est valde admiratione, ira et impatientia: imo sicut infra secundo libro habetur, repletus furore, jussit sine cessatione agitari currum, super quem sedit, comminans Judæis et templo ac urbi Jerusalem; moxque ex curru cum impetu cadens, læsus est usque ad mortem. Et incidit in languorem præ tristitia, et etiam ex illa ruina. Siquidem, Spiritus tristis exsiccat ossa; atque, ut iterum Salomon protestatur, Sicut vermis nocet ligno et tinea vestimento, ita tristitia nocet cordi.
paras.en: [[6:8|And it came to pass, when the king heard these words, that he was struck with fear|Et factum est, ut audivit rex sermones istos, expavit]], Antiochus, on hearing these things, [[6:8|and exceedingly moved|et commotus est valde]] with amazement, anger and impatience: nay, as is told below in the second book, being filled with fury, he ordered the chariot in which he sat to be driven without stopping[[2 Mach 9:4||]], threatening the Jews and the temple and the city of Jerusalem; and soon after, falling from the chariot with violence, he was hurt even unto death[[2 Mach 9:7||]]; [[6:8|and fell sick for grief|Et incidit in languorem præ tristitia]], and also from that fall. For indeed, [[Prov 17:22|a sorrowful spirit drieth up the bones|Spiritus tristis exsiccat ossa]]; and, as Solomon declares again, [[Prov 25:20|As a moth doth by a garment, and a worm by the wood: so the sadness of a man consumeth the heart|Sicut vermis nocet ligno et tinea vestimento, ita tristitia nocet cordi]] [Denis puts the worm before the moth].

paras.t: Et dixit amicis suis: Recessit somnus ab oculis meis, ex inquietudine phantasiæ, sollicitudine et timore. Unde et Nabuchodonosor ex visione sua perterritus, ait: Sermo recessit a me. Et dixi in corde meo: In quantam tribulationem deveni, et in quos fluctus tristitiæ, in qua nunc sum, qui jucundus eram et dilectus meis, quibus complacui, a quibus et Illustris quasi antonomastice sum vocatus! Nunc vero reminiscor et malorum quæ feci in Jerusalem. Cognovi ergo, quia propterea invenerunt me mala ista. Ecce quomodo vexatio dedit huic impio intellectum.
