paras.en: And he [[6:10|said|Et dixit]] to his friends: [[6:10|Sleep is gone from my eyes|Recessit somnus ab oculis meis]], from the restlessness of his imagination, from anxiety and fear. Hence Nabuchodonosor too, terrified by his vision, says: [[Dan 2:5|The thing is gone out of my mind|Sermo recessit a me]]. [[6:11|And I said in my heart: Into how much tribulation am I come, and into what floods of sorrow wherein now I am|Et dixi in corde meo: In quantam tribulationem deveni, et in quos fluctus tristitiæ, in qua nunc sum]], [[6:11|I that was pleasant and beloved|qui jucundus eram et dilectus]] by my own, whom I pleased, and by whom I was even called the Illustrious, as it were by antonomasia [that is, by a title used in place of a proper name]! [[6:12|But now I remember the evils that I did in Jerusalem|Nunc vero reminiscor et malorum quæ feci in Jerusalem]]. [[6:13|I know, therefore, that for this cause these evils have found me|Cognovi ergo, quia propterea invenerunt me mala ista]]. See how vexation has given this wicked man understanding[[Is 28:19||]].

paras.t: Et vocavit Philippum unum de amicis suis; cui dedit insignia regalia, committens ei administrationem totius regni sui, quousque filius suus Antiochus aptus esset ad regimen. Et mortuus est illic Antiochus sceleratissimus, anno centesimo quadragesimo nono regni Græcorum: et sic regnavit vix annis duodecim. Cœpit namque regnare anno centesimo tricesimo septimo, ut patuit supra. Sicque illud Job: […] sunt, in ipso impletum est. Unde et ait Ecclesiastes: Non sit bonum impio, nec prolongentur dies ejus; sed quasi umbra prætereant, qui non timent faciem Dei.
paras.en: [[6:14|Then he called Philip, one of his friends|Et vocavit Philippum unum de amicis suis]]; to whom he gave the royal insignia, committing to him the administration of his whole kingdom, until his son Antiochus should be fit to rule. [[6:16|So king Antiochus died there|Et mortuus est illic Antiochus]], most wicked as he was, [[6:16|in the year one hundred and forty-nine|anno centesimo quadragesimo nono]] of the kingdom of the Greeks: and so he reigned barely twelve years. For he began to reign in the hundred and thirty-seventh year, as was shown above[[1 Mach 1:11||]]. And so that saying of Job, […][[Job 22:16||]] [two lines are unreadable in the scan here and only the last word of the quotation, 'sunt', survives; the margin gives Job xxii, 16: 'Who were taken away before their time'], was fulfilled in him. Hence Ecclesiastes too says: [[Eccles 8:13|let it not be well with the wicked, neither let his days be prolonged, but as a shadow let them pass away that fear not the face of the Lord|Non sit bonum impio, nec prolongentur dies ejus; sed quasi umbra prætereant, qui non timent faciem Dei]].

paras.t: Circa hunc locum Josephus scribit: Miror Polybium, quod vir bonus exsistens, dicit ideo perisse Antiochum, quia voluit templum Dianæ in Perside devastare. Qui enim nullatenus egit peccatum, sed tantum cogitavit, nullo reatu tenetur. Ex quibus verbis eliciunt quidam Josephum æstimasse, non esse culpam in cogitatione aut appetitione, nisi procedat in actum. Auctor vero Scholasticæ historiæ sic concludit: Hic patet, secundum opinionem Josephi, quod lex cohibuit manum, non animum.
paras.en: On this passage Josephus writes: I wonder at Polybius that, good man though he is, he says Antiochus perished because he wished to lay waste the temple of Diana in Persia. For one who in no way committed the sin, but only thought of it, is bound by no guilt. From these words some gather that Josephus held that there is no fault in thought or desire unless it goes on into act. But the author of the Scholastic History concludes thus: Here it is plain that, in the opinion of Josephus, the law restrained the hand, not the mind [that is, the Old Law forbade the outward deed, not the inward desire].

paras.t: Et cognovit Lysias, quoniam mortuus est rex: quia ad talia denuntianda multi præcurrunt; et constituit ipse Lysias regnare Antiochum filium ejus regis defuncti. Hoc celeriter fecit Lysias, ne adolescens Antiochus veniret sub tutela atque regimine præfati Philippi.
paras.en: [[6:17|And Lysias understood that the king was dead|Et cognovit Lysias, quoniam mortuus est rex]]: for many run ahead to announce such things; [[6:17|and he set up|et constituit]], Lysias himself, [[6:17|Antiochus, his son, to reign|regnare Antiochum filium ejus]], the son of the dead king. Lysias did this quickly, lest the young Antiochus should come under the guardianship and rule of the aforesaid Philip.

paras.t: Et qui erant in arce, concluserant Israel in circuitu sanctorum, id est, arctaverant ipsos sacerdotes et consistentes cum eis infra septa templi, ita quod non valebant libere introire et exire sicut cultus Dei exegit. Arx quippe, Josepho teste, altitudinem templi vicit. Et convenerunt simul et obsederunt Judas ac sui eos qui erant in arce, et fecerunt balistas, id est instrumenta ad jacienda spicula contra arcem, et machinas alias bellicas, ad arcem obtinendam idoneas.
paras.en: [[6:18|Now they that were in the castle, had shut up the Israelites round about the holy places|Et qui erant in arce, concluserant Israel in circuitu sanctorum]], that is, they had hemmed in the priests themselves, and those who stood with them, within the precincts of the temple, so that they could not freely go in and out as the worship of God required. For the castle, as Josephus witnesses, overtopped the height of the temple. [[6:20|And they came together, and besieged|Et convenerunt simul et obsederunt]], that is, Judas and his men, those who were in the castle, [[6:20|and they made battering slings|et fecerunt balistas]], that is, instruments for hurling missiles against the castle, [[6:20|and engines|et machinas]], other engines of war fit for taking the castle.

paras.t: Et exierunt quidam ex ipsa arce de nocte, id est clam, et adjunxerunt se illis impii ex Israel refugæ legis, et abierunt ad regem, et dixerunt: Nos decrevimus servire patri tuo Antiocho jam defuncto. Isti fuerunt, qui et primo capitulo leguntur accessisse Antiochum pro licentia vivendi gentiliter. Et filii nostri propter hoc abalienabant se a nobis, volentes in Judaismo manere; et quicumque inveniebantur ex nobis, interficiebantur a Mathathia et filiis ac adjutoribus suis. Et ecce applicuerunt hodie, id est tempore isto, ad arcem; et munitionem, id est fortalitium in Bethsura urbe, munierunt: sicut prehabitum est.
paras.en: And [[6:21|some of the besieged got out|Et exierunt quidam]] from the castle itself by night, that is, secretly, [[6:21|and some wicked men of Israel joined themselves unto them|et adjunxerunt se illis impii ex Israel]], renegades from the law, and [[6:22|they went to the king, and said|et abierunt ad regem, et dixerunt]]: [[6:23|We determined to serve thy father|Nos decrevimus servire patri tuo]] Antiochus, now dead. These were the men who, as we read in the first chapter too, went to Antiochus for leave to live after the manner of the heathens[[1 Mach 1:14||]] [the margin gives 1 Mach. i, with the verse numbers partly unreadable; vv. 12–14 tell of it]. [[6:24|And for this they of our nation are alienated from us|Et filii nostri propter hoc abalienabant se a nobis]], wishing to remain in Judaism; [[6:24|and have slain as many of us as they could find|et quicumque inveniebantur ex nobis, interficiebantur]], by Mathathias and his sons and helpers. [[6:26|And behold they have approached this day|Et ecce applicuerunt hodie]], that is, at this time, [[6:26|to the castle|ad arcem]]; and [[6:26|the strong hold|et munitionem]], that is, the fortress in the city of Bethsura, [[6:26|they have fortified|munierunt]]: as was told above.

paras.t: His auditis, commotus est rex; et collegit grandem et fortem, sicut patet in textu, exercitum, in quo erant triginta duo elephanti docti ad prælium, id est, per exercitationem multum dirigibiles facti in bellis. Nam et teste Philosopho, elephanti sunt inter bruta præcipue disciplinabiles, tanquam de ratione multum participantes. Et applicuerunt rex ac sui ad Bethsuram expugnandam, et fecerunt machinas; et exierunt Judæi a Juda constituti in fortalitio illo, et succenderunt eas machinas regis, et pugnaverunt viriliter. Judas enim non posuit in fortalitio illo custodiendo ac defendendo, nisi fortissimos pugnatores valde audaces.
paras.en: When he heard these things the king was moved; and he gathered a great and strong army, as is clear in the text, in which there were [[6:30|thirty-two elephants trained to battle|triginta duo elephanti docti ad prælium]], that is, made by exercise very easy to direct in war. For, as the Philosopher [that is, Aristotle] witnesses, elephants are especially teachable among the brutes, as having, as it were, a large share in reason. And the king and his men [[6:31|approached to Bethsura|ad Bethsuram]] to storm it, [[6:31|and they made engines|et fecerunt machinas]]; [[6:31|but they sallied forth|et exierunt]], the Jews placed in that fortress by Judas, [[6:31|and burnt them|et succenderunt eas]], the king's engines, [[6:31|and fought manfully|et pugnaverunt viriliter]]. For Judas had put into that fortress, to guard and defend it, none but the strongest fighters, men of great boldness.

paras.t: Et Judas recessit ab arce ad succurrendum suis in Bethsura. Et surrexit rex ante lucem, quia audivit Judam venire; et comparaverunt, id est, disposuerunt, se exercitus tam regis quam Judæ, in prælium. Et elephantis ostenderunt sanguinem uvæ et mori, id est materiam illam liquidam expressam ex uvis et moris cruori consimilem, ad acuendum eos in prælium. Ex talis namque materiæ intuitione provocantur ad pugnam, sicut et equi ex buccinarum clangore, juxta illud Job: Non reputat tubæ sonare clangorem; ubi audierit buccinam, dicit, Vah.
paras.en: [[6:32|And Judas departed from the castle|Et Judas recessit ab arce]] to help his men in Bethsura. [[6:33|And the king rose before it was light|Et surrexit rex ante lucem]], because he heard that Judas was coming; [[6:33|and the armies made themselves ready|et comparaverunt]], that is, drew themselves up, both the king's army and that of Judas, for the battle. [[6:34|And they shewed the elephants the blood of grapes, and mulberries|Et elephantis ostenderunt sanguinem uvæ et mori]], that is, that liquid matter pressed out of grapes and mulberries, which is like blood, [[6:34|to provoke them to fight|ad acuendum eos in prælium]]. For by the sight of such matter they are stirred up to fight, as horses too are by the blare of trumpets, according to that saying of Job: [[Job 39:24|neither doth he make account when the noise of the trumpet soundeth|Non reputat tubæ sonare clangorem]]; [[Job 39:25|When he heareth the trumpet he saith: Ha, ha|ubi audierit buccinam, dicit, Vah]].

paras.t: Et diviserunt ministri regis bestias, id est elephantos, quæ videntur maximæ bestiarum, per legiones. Sed et turres ligneæ super eos, scilicet elephantos. Et residuum equitatum hinc et inde, id est ex utroque latere bestiarum, statuit, id est, ordinate divisit, in duas partes: sic quod una pars residui exercitus fuit a dextris bestiarum, alia a sinistris; tubis exercitum commovere, id est ex clangore buccinarum animare et excitare bellatores ad pugnam, et perurgere constipatos in legionibus, id est milites condensatos constringere seu dirigere ad processum, ut sic conjunctim progredientes, non possent ab hostibus separari ab invicem.
paras.en: [[6:35|And they distributed|Et diviserunt]], the king's ministers, [[6:35|the beasts|bestias]], that is, the elephants, which seem the greatest of the beasts, [[6:35|by the legions|per legiones]]. [[6:37|And upon the beast, there were strong wooden towers|Sed et turres ligneæ super eos]], that is, upon the elephants. [[6:38|And the rest of the horsemen|Et residuum equitatum]] [[6:38|on this side and on that side|hinc et inde]], that is, on both sides of the beasts, [[6:38|he placed|statuit]], that is, divided in order, [[6:38|at the two wings|in duas partes]]: so that one part of the rest of the army was on the right of the beasts, the other on the left; [[6:38|with trumpets to stir up the army|tubis exercitum commovere]], that is, by the blare of the trumpets to put heart into the fighters and rouse them to battle, [[6:38|and to hasten them forward that stood thick together in the legions|et perurgere constipatos in legionibus]], that is, to press the soldiers crowded together close and direct them forward, so that, advancing thus in a body, they could not be separated from one another by the enemy.

paras.t: Et ut refulsit sol in clypeos aureos et æreos exercitus regis, resplenduerunt montes ab eis, sicut lampades ignis, ex repercussione radiorum splendentium. Jussit enim rex clypeos illos nudari, ut nimium suæ claritatis fulgorem emitterent: et hoc forsan fecit ad incutiendum timorem Judæ ac suis. Et distincta, id est ordinate divisa, est pars exercitus regis per montes excelsos, per quos ivit, ne quis de exercitu Judæ effugeret per montes excelsos, et alii, hoc est, alia pars exercitus, distincta est et processit per loca humilia, id est bassa; et ibant caute et ordinate. Talis enim ordinatio valde utilis est in bellis: imo, secundum Vegetium, multitudo inordinata non est nisi hostium victima. Et commovebantur quadam admiratione seu horrore omnes inhabitantes terram illam, a qua videri poterat et audiri exercitus ille, a voce multitudinis eorum et collisione armorum. Et appropinquavit Judas et exercitus ejus in prælium, et ceciderunt de exercitu regis sexcenti viri. Porro, infra libro secundo aliqua aliter recitantur de prælio isto, quam hic: quæ ibi discutientur.
paras.en: [[6:39|Now when the sun shone upon the shields of gold, and of brass|Et ut refulsit sol in clypeos aureos et æreos]] of the king's army, [[6:39|the mountains glittered therewith|resplenduerunt montes ab eis]], [[6:39|like lamps of fire|sicut lampades ignis]], from the reflection of the shining rays. For the king had ordered those shields to be uncovered, so that they might send out the full brilliance of their brightness: and perhaps he did this to strike fear into Judas and his men. [[6:40|And part of the king's army was distinguished|Et distincta]], that is, divided in order, [[6:40|by the high mountains|est pars exercitus regis per montes excelsos]], by which it went, lest any of Judas's army should escape by the high mountains, [[6:40|and the other|et alii]], that is, the other part of the army, was distinguished and went forward [[6:40|by the low places|per loca humilia]], that is, the lowlands; [[6:40|and they marched on warily and orderly|et ibant caute et ordinate]]. For such ordering is very useful in war: nay, according to Vegetius, a disorderly multitude is nothing but a victim for the enemy. [[6:41|And all the inhabitants of the land were moved|Et commovebantur]] with a certain amazement or dread, those, that is, of the land from which that army could be seen and heard, [[6:41|at the noise of their multitude|a voce multitudinis eorum]] [[6:41|and the rattling of the armour|et collisione armorum]]. [[6:42|And Judas and his army drew near for battle|Et appropinquavit Judas et exercitus ejus in prælium]], [[6:42|and there fell of the king's army six hundred men|et ceciderunt de exercitu regis sexcenti viri]]. Below, however, in the second book, some things are told of this battle otherwise than here[[2 Mach 13:15||]] [the margin gives II Mach. xiii]: they will be discussed there.

paras.t: Et vidit Eleazar filius Saura bestiam unam loricatam loricis regis, et visum est ei quod in ea esset rex; et dedit se, ut acquireret sibi nomen æternum, periculo mortis corporalis pro bono communi. Et cucurrit ad eam audacter in medio legionis, interficiens a dextris et a sinistris. Et ivit sub pedes elephantis, id est, prope et infra pedes illius elephantis, putans quod rex esset in ea, id est in turre superposita bestiæ illi, et occidit eum, videlicet elephantem; et cecidit bestia super ipsum, et mortuus est illic, oppressus mole elephantis: sicut et Samson exspiravit sub domo quam dejecit. Sed istud factum est in publico bello, in quo pro boni communis conservatione seu procuratione, exponenda est mortis discrimini vita corporalis particularium personarum.
paras.en: [[6:43|And Eleazar, the son of Saura, saw|Et vidit Eleazar filius Saura]] [[6:43|one of the beasts harnessed with the king's harness|bestiam unam loricatam loricis regis]], [[6:43|and it seemed to him that the king was on it|et visum est ei quod in ea esset rex]]; and [[6:44|he exposed himself|dedit se]], [[6:44|to get himself an everlasting name|ut acquireret sibi nomen æternum]], to the danger of bodily death for the common good. [[6:45|And he ran up to it boldly in the midst of the legion, killing on the right hand, and on the left|Et cucurrit ad eam audacter in medio legionis, interficiens a dextris et a sinistris]]. [[6:46|And he went between the feet of the elephant|Et ivit sub pedes elephantis]], that is, close to and under the feet of that elephant, thinking that the king was in it, that is, in the tower set upon that beast, [[6:46|and slew it|et occidit eum]], namely the elephant; [[6:46|and it fell to the ground upon him|et cecidit bestia super ipsum]], [[6:46|and he died there|et mortuus est illic]], crushed by the elephant's bulk: as Samson too breathed his last under the house which he threw down[[Judg 16:30||]]. But this was done in a public war, in which, for the preserving or securing of the common good, the bodily life of particular persons is to be exposed to the hazard of death.

paras.t: Quod autem Eleazar dicitur istud fecisse, Ut acquireret sibi nomen æternum, in bono accipitur, secundum quod ait Scriptura, Curam habe de bono nomine: prout supra expositum est.
paras.en: That Eleazar is said to have done this [[6:44|to get himself an everlasting name|Ut acquireret sibi nomen æternum]] is taken in a good sense, according to what Scripture says, [[Ecclus 41:15|Take care of a good name|Curam habe de bono nomine]]: as was explained above[[1 Mach 2:51||]] [the margin's numerals are misread; it seems to point to 1 Mach 2:51, 'an everlasting name'].

paras.t: Præterea, ut Josephus refert, et Magister in historiis sequitur, Eleazar iste fuit frater carnalis Judæ Machabæi, et supra Eleazarus appellatur, eratque quartus inter filios Mathathiæ. Nec obstat quod nominatur hic, filius Saura. Nam Saura potuit esse nomen matris suæ, sicut et Joab et fratres ejus in libris Regum frequenter dicuntur filii Sarviæ. Vel Mathathias alio nomine vocatus est Saura, quemadmodum pater David vocatus fuit Isai et Jesse ac Naas. Nam legitur in Regum libro, quod Amasa fuit filius Abigail filiæ Naas: et constat, quod Abigail illa fuit soror Sarviæ. Hunc Eleazar Judas vocavit Mauronem, ut Josephus scribit.
paras.en: Moreover, as Josephus relates, and the Master [that is, Peter Comestor, author of the Scholastic History] follows him in the Histories, this Eleazar was the brother in the flesh of Judas Machabeus, and above he is called Eleazarus[[1 Mach 2:5||]], and he was the fourth among the sons of Mathathias. Nor is it any objection that here he is named [[6:43|the son of Saura|filius Saura]]. For Saura may have been the name of his mother, as Joab too and his brothers are often called in the books of Kings the sons of Sarvia[[2 Kings 2:13||]][[2 Kings 2:18||]]. Or else Mathathias was called Saura by another name, just as David's father was called Isai[[1 Kings 16:1||]] and Jesse[[Is 11:1||]][[Matt 1:5||]] and Naas. For we read in the book of Kings that Amasa was the son of Abigail the daughter of Naas[[2 Kings 17:25||]]: and it is certain that this Abigail was the sister of Sarvia. Judas called this Eleazar Mauron, as Josephus writes [a footnote in the edition, unreadable in the scan, gives the name in Greek; in 1 Mach 2:5 his surname is Abaron].

paras.t: Et videntes Judas et sui virtutem, id est potestatem, regis et impetum exercitus ejus, diverterunt ab eis. Festinabant enim ad templum redire, et illud munire ac custodire, ne præoccuparetur a rege.
paras.en: [[6:47|Then they seeing|Et videntes]], namely Judas and his men, [[6:47|the strength|virtutem]], that is, the power, [[6:47|of the king and the fierceness of his army|regis et impetum exercitus ejus]], [[6:47|turned away from them|diverterunt ab eis]]. For they were hastening to return to the temple, and to fortify and guard it, lest it be seized first by the king.

paras.t: Et fecit rex pacem cum his qui erant in Bethsura, promittendo eis securitatem, dummodo exirent fortalitium, et dimitterent illud sibi: quod et fecerunt, necessitate quadam compulsi. Et exierunt de civitate, quia non erant eis alimenta ibi conclusis, id est, ipsi custodes loci illius obsessi ibidem a rege, non habuerunt necessaria vitæ, quia sabbata erant terræ, id est septimus annus, in quo Judæi terram non seminabant, prout in Levitico habetur, quo Dominus jussit: Sex annis seres agrum tuum. Septimo anno sabbatum erit terræ; agrum non seres.
paras.en: [[6:49|And he made peace with them that were in Bethsura|Et fecit rex pacem cum his qui erant in Bethsura]], promising them safety provided they left the fortress and gave it up to him: which they did, compelled by a certain necessity; [[6:49|and they came forth out of the city, because they had no victuals, being shut up there|Et exierunt de civitate, quia non erant eis alimenta ibi conclusis]], that is, the very guards of that place, besieged there by the king, did not have the necessities of life, [[6:49|for it was the year of rest to the land|quia sabbata erant terræ]] [literally 'the sabbaths of the land'], that is, the seventh year, in which the Jews did not sow the land, as is found in Leviticus, where the Lord commanded: [[Lev 25:3|Six years thou shalt sow thy field|Sex annis seres agrum tuum]]; [[Lev 25:4|in the seventh year there shall be a sabbath to the land|Septimo anno sabbatum erit terræ]]: [[Lev 25:4|Thou shalt not sow thy field|agrum non seres]].

paras.t: Sed qualiter istud potuit esse causa penuriæ Judæorum istorum? quum Dominus eodem dicat capitulo: Quod si dixeritis, Quid comedemus anno septimo, si non severimus anno sexto? Dabo benedictionem meam vobis anno sexto, et faciet fructus trium annorum. Ad quod quidam respondent, quod beneficium istud multiplicationis fructuum sexto anno, fuit subtractum Judæis post reditum a Babylone, sicut et alia quædam. Hæc tamen responsio probationem non habet nec auctoritatem. Ideo dici potest, sicut et infra in isto capitulo tangitur, quod hi qui remanserant in Judæa de gentibus, consumpserant reliquias eorum, scilicet terræ nascentium, quæ repositæ erant. Vel ob aliquam populi culpam, fuit beneficium hoc subtractum pro tunc in parte vel toto.
paras.en: But how could this be the cause of these Jews' want, since the Lord says in the same chapter: [[Lev 25:20|But if you say: What shall we eat the seventh year, if we sow not|Quod si dixeritis, Quid comedemus anno septimo, si non severimus]] in the sixth year? [[Lev 25:21|I will give you my blessing the sixth year: and it shall yield the fruits of three years|Dabo benedictionem meam vobis anno sexto, et faciet fructus trium annorum]]. To this some answer that this benefit of the multiplying of the fruits in the sixth year was withdrawn from the Jews after the return from Babylon, as certain others were too. But this answer has neither proof nor authority. So it can be said, as is touched on below in this chapter too, that [[6:53|such as had stayed in Judea of them that came from among the nations, had eaten the residue|hi qui remanserant in Judæa de gentibus, consumpserant reliquias]] of them, namely of the produce of the land, which had been stored up. Or else, because of some fault of the people, this benefit was withdrawn at that time, in part or wholly.

paras.t: Et comprehendit rex Bethsuram egressis inde Judæis. Et applicuit castra ad Jerusalem ad locum sanctificationis, id est templi; et statuit balistas ad sagittandum contrarios, et ignis jacula ad incendendum, et tormenta, id est magna instrumenta, ad lapides jactandos, et scorpios, id est instrumenta ad emittendum venenatas sagittas, et fundibula. Fecerunt autem et ipsi Judas et sui machinas bellicas, et pugnaverunt dies multos. Escæ autem, id est sufficientia victualium pro tempore notabiliter longo, non erant in civitate Jerusalem, eo quod septimus annus esset: sicut modo expositum est. Quibus verbis pro causa subjungitur: et qui remanserant in Judæa de gentibus, consumpserant reliquias earum quæ repositæ fuerant. Et remanserunt in sanctis, id est in civitate et templo Jerusalem, viri pauci cum Juda, quoniam obtinuerat eos fames, id est, ex inopia victualium, compulsi fuerunt occulte exire. Ideo Judas cum suis cito fuisset devictus per famem ex obsidione, nisi Deus subvenisset per modum qui subditur, et sicut liberavit sanctum David a circumdatione Saulis, per adventum Philistinorum in terram Saul.
paras.en: [[6:50|And the king took Bethsura|Et comprehendit rex Bethsuram]], the Jews having gone out of it. And he pitched his camp[[6:48||]] at Jerusalem, [[6:51|against the sanctuary|ad locum sanctificationis]], that is, the temple; [[6:51|and he set up there battering slings|et statuit balistas]] to shoot at the enemy, [[6:51|and instruments to cast fire|et ignis jacula]] for burning, [[6:51|and engines to cast stones|et tormenta]], that is, great instruments for throwing stones, [[6:51|and pieces to shoot arrows|et scorpios]], that is, instruments for sending out poisoned arrows, [[6:51|and slings|et fundibula]]. [[6:52|And they also made|Fecerunt autem et ipsi]], that is, Judas and his men, engines of war, [[6:52|and they fought for many days|et pugnaverunt dies multos]]. [[6:53|But there were no victuals|Escæ autem]], that is, enough provisions for a notably long time, [[6:53|in the city|non erant in civitate]] of Jerusalem, [[6:53|because it was the seventh year|eo quod septimus annus esset]]: as was just explained. To which words the cause is added: [[6:53|and such as had stayed in Judea of them that came from among the nations, had eaten the residue of all that which had been stored up|et qui remanserant in Judæa de gentibus, consumpserant reliquias earum quæ repositæ fuerant]]. [[6:54|And there remained in the holy places|Et remanserunt in sanctis]], that is, in the city and temple of Jerusalem, [[6:54|but a few|viri pauci]] with Judas, [[6:54|for the famine had prevailed over them|quoniam obtinuerat eos fames]], that is, from want of victuals they were forced to go out secretly. So Judas with his men would soon have been overcome by famine from the siege, had not God come to their aid in the way that follows, as he delivered holy David from Saul's encircling[[1 Kings 23:26||]] through the coming of the Philistines into Saul's land[[1 Kings 23:27||]].

paras.t: Et audivit Lysias, quod Philippus reversus esset a Perside, etc. Festinavit ipse Lysias ire et dicere ad regem: Deficimus quotidie per mortem aliquorum ex nostris, etc., et incumbit nobis ordinare de regno: quasi dicat, Negligimus utiliora. Nunc itaque demus dexteras hominibus istis, et faciamus cum illis pacem; et ambulent in legitimis suis, etc. Et placuit sermo in conspectu regis; et misit ad eos facere pacem, et receperunt illam. Et juravit illis, videlicet Judæ et sociis ejus, rex, quod nihil ei noceret, nec templo: quod juramentum mox fregit, ingressus locum sanctum munitum, cujus muros dissipari præcepit, ut patet in textu.
paras.en: [[6:55|Now Lysias heard that Philip|Et audivit Lysias, quod Philippus]] [[6:56|returned from Persia|reversus esset a Perside]], etc. And [[6:57|he made haste|Festinavit]], Lysias himself, [[6:57|to go, and say to the king|ire et dicere ad regem]]: [[6:57|We decay daily|Deficimus quotidie]] through the death of some of our men, etc., [[6:57|and it lieth upon us to take order for the affairs of the kingdom|et incumbit nobis ordinare de regno]]: as if to say, We are neglecting more profitable things. [[6:58|Now, therefore, let us come to an agreement with these men|Nunc itaque demus dexteras hominibus istis]] [literally 'let us give right hands to these men'], [[6:58|and make peace with them|et faciamus cum illis pacem]]; [[6:59|that they may live according to their own laws|et ambulent in legitimis suis]], etc. [[6:60|And the proposal was acceptable in the sight of the king|Et placuit sermo in conspectu regis]]; [[6:60|and he sent to them to make peace: and they accepted of it|et misit ad eos facere pacem, et receperunt illam]]. And [[6:61|swore to them|Et juravit illis]], namely to Judas and his companions, [[6:61|the king|rex]], that nothing should harm him, nor the temple: which oath he soon broke, having entered the fortified holy place, whose walls he ordered to be thrown down, as is clear in the text.

paras.t: Verumtamen ab hac narratione videtur plurimum discrepare, quod secundo libro de ista recitatur historia, sicut ibidem Domino concedente tangetur.
paras.en: Yet what is related of this history in the second book seems to differ very much from this narration[[2 Mach 13:23||]] [the margin gives only II Mach.; the account is in 2 Mach 13], as will be touched on there, the Lord granting.

7.title: Declaratio capituli septimi: Anno centesimo quinquagesimo primo.
7.title_en: Explanation of the seventh chapter: In the hundred and fifty-first year.

paras.t: Bella Judæ habita contra successorem prædicti regis Antiochi, hic narrantur.
paras.en: The wars of Judas waged against the successor of the aforesaid King Antiochus are related here.

paras.t: Anno centesimo quinquagesimo primo, exiit Demetrius, Seleuci filius, ab urbe Roma. Sicut præhabitum est, Seleucus iste fuit frater Antiochi Epiphanis, qui mortuo Seleuco, invasit regnum ipsius, nepote suo, videlicet filio præfati Seleuci excluso: qui filius, nomine Demetrius, profectus est Romam ad agendum contra avunculum suum Antiochum. Audiensque ipsum obisse, reversus est, et ascendit in civitatem maritimam, id est juxta mare sitam, et regnavit illic. Atque, ut Josephus refert, civitas illa fuit Tyrus. Et factum est, ut ingressus est in domum regni patrum suorum, id est, in urbem atque palatium Antiochiæ, quæ fuit metropolis Syriæ, comprehendit exercitus Antiochum, filium Antiochi Epiphanis, et Lysiam: ad quos exercitus conceperat displicentiam et rancorem, præsertim illi qui cum Philippo venerunt, quem Antiochus iste (secundum Josephum) paulo ante occidit.
paras.en: [[7:1|In the hundred and fifty-first year, Demetrius, the son of Seleucus, departed from the city of Rome|Anno centesimo quinquagesimo primo, exiit Demetrius, Seleuci filius, ab urbe Roma]]. As was said before, this Seleucus was the brother of Antiochus Epiphanes, who on the death of Seleucus seized his kingdom, shutting out his nephew, namely the son of the said Seleucus; which son, Demetrius by name, set out for Rome to act against his uncle Antiochus. And hearing that he had died, he returned, [[7:1|and came up|et ascendit]] [[7:1|into a city of the sea coast|in civitatem maritimam]], that is, one situated by the sea, [[7:1|and reigned there|et regnavit illic]]. And, as Josephus relates, that city was Tyre. [[7:2|And it came to pass as he entered into the house of the kingdom of his fathers|Et factum est, ut ingressus est in domum regni patrum suorum]], that is, into the city and palace of Antioch, which was the metropolis of Syria, [[7:2|that the army seized upon Antiochus|comprehendit exercitus Antiochum]], the son of Antiochus Epiphanes, [[7:2|and Lysias|et Lysiam]]: against whom the army had conceived displeasure and rancour, especially those who had come with Philip, whom this Antiochus (according to Josephus) had slain a little before.

paras.t: Et venerunt ad eum, puta Demetrium, viri iniqui ex Israel, refugæ legis, et Alcimus dux eorum, qui volebat fieri sacerdos, id est princeps sacerdotum seu pontifex, ut post insinuatur. Et accusaverunt populum Judæorum apud regem, dicentes: Perdidit, id est occidit, Judas amicos tuos, quos reperit in Judæa seu alibi. Et misit rex Bacchidem; et Alcimum impium constituit in sacerdotium, id est in pontificatum. Qui venerunt in Judæam cum grandi exercitu, verbisque dolosis voluerunt decipere Judam ac fratres ejus: qui non crediderunt illis iniquis.
paras.en: [[7:5|And there came to him|Et venerunt ad eum]], namely to Demetrius, [[7:5|the wicked|viri iniqui]] men [[7:5|of Israel|ex Israel]], deserters of the law, [[7:5|and Alcimus was at the head of them|et Alcimus dux eorum]], [[7:5|who desired to be made high priest|qui volebat fieri sacerdos]] [*sacerdos*, "priest"], that is, chief of the priests or pontiff, as is indicated later. [[7:6|And they accused the people to the king|Et accusaverunt populum Judæorum apud regem]], [[7:6|saying|dicentes]]: Judas hath [[7:6|destroyed|Perdidit]], that is, slain, [[7:6|all thy friends|amicos tuos]], whom he found in Judea or elsewhere. And the king sent Bacchides[[7:8||]]; [[7:9|and the wicked Alcimus he made high priest|et Alcimum impium constituit in sacerdotium]], that is, put him in the pontificate. They came into Judea with a great army[[7:10||]], and with deceitful words wished to deceive Judas and his brethren, who did not believe those wicked men[[7:11||]].

paras.t: Porro alii quidam credebant illis, sicut subjungitur: Et convenerunt ad Alcimum et Bacchidem congregatio scribarum requirere quæ justa sunt, id est pertinentia ad bonum reipublicæ et ad conservationem cultus divini; et primi, Assidæi, qui erant in filiis Israel, et exquirebant ab eis, id est ab Alcimo et Bacchide, pacem. Porro Assidæi Judæi sunt dicti, qui assidue vacabant divinis. Dixerunt enim: Homo sacerdos de semine Aaron venit, non decipiet nos. Hi boni viri juxta suam sinceritatem judicaverunt de aliis, sed decepti fuerunt, et occisi ab impio illo usque ad sexaginta viros: quæ deceptio habuit in eis rationem pœnæ, non culpæ. Et incubuit timor et tremor in omnem populum Judæorum hæc considerantem: cujus timoris signum est, quia dixerunt: Non est in eis, videlicet Alcimo et societate ipsius, veritas verborum, quia nec juramenta servant neque promissa, et judicium, id est discretio veræ prudentiæ, seu judicium rectum in factis; transgressi sunt enim constitutum, id est ordinationem inter nos factam.
paras.en: But certain others believed them, as is added: [[7:12|Then there assembled to Alcimus and Bacchides a company of the scribes, to require things that are just|Et convenerunt ad Alcimum et Bacchidem congregatio scribarum requirere quæ justa sunt]], that is, things pertaining to the good of the commonwealth and to the preservation of divine worship; [[7:13|And first the Assideans, that were among the children of Israel|et primi, Assidæi, qui erant in filiis Israel]], [[7:13|and they sought|et exquirebant]] [[7:13|peace|pacem]] [[7:13|of them|ab eis]], that is, of Alcimus and Bacchides. Now those Jews were called Assideans who gave themselves assiduously to divine things [the play is on *Assidæi* and *assidue*]. [[7:14|For they said|Dixerunt enim]]: [[7:14|One that is a priest of the seed of Aaron is come, he will not deceive us|Homo sacerdos de semine Aaron venit, non decipiet nos]]. These good men judged of others by their own sincerity, but they were deceived, and slain by that wicked man, to the number of sixty men[[7:16||]]: and this deception was in them a matter of penalty, not of fault. [[7:18|Then fear and trembling fell upon all the people|Et incubuit timor et tremor in omnem populum]] of the Jews, as they considered these things: and the sign of this fear is that [[7:18|they said|dixerunt]]: [[7:18|There is no truth|Non est in eis, videlicet Alcimo et societate ipsius, veritas]] (among them, that is, in Alcimus and his company) of words, since they keep neither oaths nor promises, [[7:18|nor justice|et judicium]], that is, the discernment of true prudence, or right judgement in deeds; [[7:18|for they have broken the covenant|transgressi sunt enim constitutum]], that is, the agreement made between us.

paras.t: Et abiit Bacchides ad regem Demetrium, commissa Alcimo regione Judæ. Et satis agebat Alcimus pro principatu sacerdotii sui obtinendo et conservando. In quo notatur ejus ambitio; et Scriptura minus dicendo, plus notat, videlicet quod importune, impudenter, et per practicas vitiosas conatus sit pontificatum obtinere et possidere, prout ambitiosis est consuetudo. Numerari etenim vitia nequeunt, quot ex ambitione nascuntur: ex qua inter cetera oriuntur invidia, suspicio prava, crudelitas, simonia, simulatio, hypocrisis, falsitas, inquietudo, mendacium, perjurium, atque adulatio, prout in libro de Consideratione plenius docet S. Bernardus. Et vidit Judas omnia mala quæ fecit Alcimus, etc. Et fecit Judas vindictam in filios desertores, qui legem patrum suorum sanctam dereliquerant: qui tanquam apostatæ legis, fuerunt gentibus ferociores; et cessaverunt ultra exire in regionem, id est, adjutores Alcimi, præsertim qui erant in arce, non audebant amplius per Judæam discurrere ad prædandum et occidendum Judæos.
paras.en: [[7:20|So Bacchides went away to the king|Et abiit Bacchides ad regem]] Demetrius, having [[7:20|committed the country to Alcimus|commissa Alcimo regione]] of Juda. [[7:21|But Alcimus did what he could to maintain his chief priesthood|Et satis agebat Alcimus pro principatu sacerdotii sui]] [literally "was busy enough for the chief place of his priesthood"], to obtain and keep it. In this his ambition is marked; and Scripture, by saying less, signifies more: namely, that he strove importunately, shamelessly, and by vicious practices to obtain and possess the pontificate, as is the custom of the ambitious. For the vices that are born of ambition cannot be numbered: from it arise, among others, envy, evil suspicion, cruelty, simony, dissimulation, hypocrisy, falsehood, restlessness, lying, perjury, and flattery, as St. Bernard teaches more fully in the book *On Consideration*. [[7:23|And Judas saw all the evils that Alcimus|Et vidit Judas omnia mala quæ fecit Alcimus]] did, etc. [[7:24|and took vengeance upon the men that had revolted|Et fecit Judas vindictam in filios desertores]] [Denis reads *filios desertores*, "the deserting sons", for the Vulgate's *viros desertores*], who had forsaken the holy law of their fathers: who, as apostates from the law, were fiercer than the Gentiles; [[7:24|and they ceased to go forth any more into the country|et cessaverunt ultra exire in regionem]], that is, the helpers of Alcimus, especially those who were in the citadel, no longer dared to range through Judea to plunder and kill the Jews.

paras.t: Et misit rex Nicanorem, etc. Et hostes parati erant rapere Judam. Quum enim Alcimus vidisset Judam sibi prævaluisse, ad regem reversus, accusavit Judam et suos multis criminibus. Propter quod rex misit Nicanorem cum Alcimo, habentem secum magnum exercitum, voluitque Judam capere dolo. Et innotuit sermo Judæ. Et conterritus est Judas ab eo. Nam, ut Josephus refert, quum Judas et Nicanor pariter starent, dedit Nicanor suis militibus signum, ut raperent Judam: quod sentiens Judas, subito territus, prudenter et fortiter exsilivit ab illo nequissimo. Et amplius noluit videre faciem ejus, puta Nicanoris, cum tali circumventione et ad tempus. Postea tamen, sicut secundo habetur libro, erant multum concordes. Deinde contra se invicem pugnaverunt. Et cognovit Nicanor, quia denudatum est consilium ejus, et exivit obviam Judæ in pugnam. Et ceciderunt de Nicanoris exercitu fere quinque millia viri, et fugerunt in civitatem David, id est ad arcem, ipse Nicanor et sui, ad gentiles ibi manentes et eis confœderatos.
paras.en: [[7:26|And the king sent Nicanor|Et misit rex Nicanorem]], etc. [[7:29|and the enemies were prepared to take away Judas by force|Et hostes parati erant rapere Judam]]. For when Alcimus had seen that Judas had prevailed over him, he went back to the king [[7:25|and accused them of many crimes|accusavit Judam et suos multis criminibus]], Judas and his men. Therefore the king sent Nicanor with Alcimus, having a great army with him, and he wished to take Judas by guile[[7:27||]]. [[7:30|And the thing was known to Judas|Et innotuit sermo Judæ]]. [[7:30|and he was much afraid of him|Et conterritus est Judas ab eo]]. For, as Josephus relates, when Judas and Nicanor were standing together, Nicanor gave his soldiers a signal to seize Judas: and Judas, perceiving it, suddenly alarmed, prudently and boldly leapt away from that most wicked man. [[7:30|and would not see his face any more|Et amplius noluit videre faciem ejus]], that is, Nicanor's, with such a snare, and for a time. Afterwards, however, as is found in the second book, they were in close agreement[[2 Mach 14:18||]] [the margin gives 2 Mach. xiv, 18–25]. Then they fought against each other. [[7:31|And Nicanor knew that his counsel was discovered|Et cognovit Nicanor, quia denudatum est consilium ejus]]: [[7:31|and he went out to fight against Judas|et exivit obviam Judæ in pugnam]]. [[7:32|And there fell of Nicanor's army almost five thousand men, and they fled into the city of David|Et ceciderunt de Nicanoris exercitu fere quinque millia viri, et fugerunt in civitatem David]], that is, to the citadel: Nicanor himself and his men fled to the Gentiles dwelling there and in league with them.

paras.t: Et post hæc verba, id est, post gesta designata per verba hæc, ascendit Nicanor in montem Sion, id est ad aliqua ejus loca eminentiora; et exierunt de sacerdotibus populi, id est, aliqui sacerdotes exiere de templo, salutare eum, et demonstrare ei holocautomata quæ offerebantur pro rege. Specialiter enim orandum est pro præsidentibus et communitatibus etiam iniquis et perfidis, ut convertantur. Propter quod Jeremias mandavit Judæis in Babylonia captis, ut orarent pro pace civitatis ad quam translati fuerunt. Et irridens Nicanor, sprevit eos tanquam idololatra, et polluit, id est inhonoravit. Et locutus est superbe, et juravit cum ira, dicens: Nisi traditus fuerit Judas et exercitus ejus in manus meas, succendam domum istam, id est templum. Hanc præsumptionem sacrilegam, Deus superbis resistens plenarie refrenavit, et superbissimum illum extreme dejecit. Verumtamen inter hæc duo bella, inter Judam et Nicanorem habita, quorum unum prætactum, et aliud consequenter in littera describitur, notabile fluxit tempus, quo inter ipsos fuit concordia, prout secundo libro recitatur.
paras.en: [[7:33|And after this|Et post hæc verba]] [literally "after these words"], that is, after the deeds signified by these words, [[7:33|Nicanor went up into mount Sion|ascendit Nicanor in montem Sion]], that is, to some of its higher places; [[7:33|and some of the priests and the people came out|et exierunt de sacerdotibus populi]], that is, some priests came out of the temple, [[7:33|to salute him|salutare eum]], [[7:33|and to shew him the holocausts that were offered for the king|et demonstrare ei holocautomata quæ offerebantur pro rege]]. For prayer is to be made especially for rulers and communities, even wicked and faithless ones, that they may be converted. For this reason Jeremias commanded the Jews held captive in Babylon to pray for the peace of the city to which they had been carried away[[Jer 29:7||]]. [[7:34|But he mocked and despised them|Et irridens Nicanor, sprevit eos]], being an idolater, [[7:34|and abused them|et polluit]], that is, dishonoured them. [[7:34|and he spoke proudly|Et locutus est superbe]], [[7:35|And swore in anger, saying: Unless Judas and his army be delivered into my hands|et juravit cum ira, dicens: Nisi traditus fuerit Judas et exercitus ejus in manus meas]], [[7:35|I will burn this house|succendam domum istam]], that is, the temple. This sacrilegious presumption God, who resists the proud[[1 Pet 5:5||]][[Jas 4:6||]], fully curbed, and cast down that most proud man utterly. Nevertheless, between these two wars waged between Judas and Nicanor, of which one has been touched on already and the other is described next in the letter, a considerable time passed, during which there was concord between them, as is recounted in the second book[[2 Mach 14:18||]].

paras.t: Consequenter describitur in hoc loco, qualiter sacerdotes zelo justitiæ oraverunt pro justa dejectione obstinati Nicanoris, qui fuit tyrannus, et publicus hostis boni communis atque divini cultus. Ideo licuit contra eum sic exorare.
paras.en: Next it is described in this place how the priests, out of zeal for justice, prayed for the just overthrow of the obstinate Nicanor, who was a tyrant and a public enemy of the common good and of divine worship. Therefore it was lawful to pray thus against him.

paras.t: Et exiit Nicanor de Jerusalem, et castra applicuit ad Bethoron, et occurrit illi, puta Nicanori, exercitus Syriæ ad auxiliandum. Et Judas applicuit in Adarsa cum tribus millibus viris. Et oravit Judas: Qui missi erant a rege Assyriorum Sennacherib, Domine, quia blasphemaverunt te, percussit ex eis angelus centum octoginta quinque millia. Primo enim missi fuerunt a rege illo Rabsaces et alii quidam, qui Deum enormiter blasphemaverunt ex parte sceleratissimi regis. Propter quorum blasphemias aliaque facinora, interfectus fuit ab angelo totus pene exercitus regis illius, prout quarto Regum et secundo Paralipomenon enarratur. Sic contere exercitum istum, quia male locutus est super sancta tua, id est contra templum et sacrificia, et contra fideles tuos ministros.
paras.en: [[7:39|Then Nicanor went out from Jerusalem, and encamped near to Bethoron|Et exiit Nicanor de Jerusalem, et castra applicuit ad Bethoron]], [[7:39|and an army of Syria joined him|et occurrit illi, puta Nicanori, exercitus Syriæ]] (him, that is, Nicanor), to help him. [[7:40|But Judas pitched in Adarsa with three thousand men|Et Judas applicuit in Adarsa cum tribus millibus viris]]. [[7:40|and Judas prayed|Et oravit Judas]]: [[7:41|O Lord, when they that were sent by king Sennacherib blasphemed thee|Qui missi erant a rege Assyriorum Sennacherib, Domine, quia blasphemaverunt te]], [[7:41|an angel went out, and slew of them a hundred and eighty-five thousand|percussit ex eis angelus centum octoginta quinque millia]]. For first there were sent by that king Rabsaces and certain others[[4 Kings 18:17||]], who blasphemed God enormously[[4 Kings 18:19||]] on behalf of that most wicked king[[4 Kings 19:10||]]. For their blasphemies and other crimes almost the whole army of that king was slain by the angel[[4 Kings 19:35||]], as is related in the fourth book of Kings and the second of Paralipomenon[[2 Par 32:9||]][[2 Par 32:21||]]. [[7:42|Even so destroy this army|Sic contere exercitum istum]], [[7:42|that he hath spoken ill against thy sanctuary|quia male locutus est super sancta tua]], that is, against the temple and the sacrifices, and against thy faithful ministers.

paras.t: Et commiserunt prælium tertiadecima die mensis Adar, id est Martii, et cecidit Nicanor primus in prælio. Quo cognito, fugit ejus exercitus. Et tubis cecinerunt Judas et sui post eos sic fugientes, cum significationibus, quia sonitus tubarum ita fiebat et formabatur, quod designavit hostium fugam. Et exierunt Judæi de omnibus castellis Judææ in circuitu, et ventilabant eos cornibus: id est, insequendo impios illos, agitaverunt eos hinc inde per angulos et cornua, et per loca diversa; vel sonando post ipsos per cornua; et convertebantur iterum ad eos undique occurrendo fugientibus, ita quod omnes ceciderunt.
paras.en: [[7:43|And the armies joined battle on the thirteenth day of the month, Adar|Et commiserunt prælium tertiadecima die mensis Adar]], that is, of March, [[7:43|and he himself was first slain in the battle|et cecidit Nicanor primus in prælio]]. When this was known, his army fled[[7:44||]]. [[7:45|and they sounded the trumpets|Et tubis cecinerunt]], Judas and his men, [[7:45|after them with signals|post eos sic fugientes, cum significationibus]] (after them, that is, as they thus fled): because the sound of the trumpets was so made and shaped that it signified the flight of the enemy. [[7:46|And they went forth out of all the towns of Judea round about|Et exierunt Judæi de omnibus castellis Judææ in circuitu]], [[7:46|and they pushed them with the horns|et ventilabant eos cornibus]]: that is, pursuing those wicked men, they drove them this way and that through corners and horns [*cornua*, "horns", also means the corners or wings of a place or of an army], and through various places; or, by sounding horns behind them; [[7:46|and they turned again to them|et convertebantur iterum ad eos]], running upon the fugitives from every side, so that [[7:46|they were all slain|omnes ceciderunt]].

paras.t: Postremo, quemadmodum Nicanor præ ceteris peccavit enormius, sic eum etiam mortuum confusibilius tractaverunt: quia jam interfectum decapitaverunt, ejusque caput in arcis apice suspenderunt. Et quia specialiter peccavit per manum et linguam, manum contra templum contumaciter extendendo, et per linguam blasphemando, multaque verba scelestissima proferendo, ideo absciderunt ei manum et linguam, sicut in ultimo secundi libri capitulo, ubi ista historia plenius describitur, continetur. Et manum ejus suspenderunt contra Jerusalem. In secundo libro habetur, Contra templum. Ideo intelligendum est, quod suspenderunt manum iniqui ex opposito templi et civitatis, in cujus extremitate situm fuerat templum. Et siluit terra Juda paucos dies, hoc est, modico tempore plebs Judæa quievit a præliis, ut sequenti patet capitulo.
paras.en: Lastly, as Nicanor had sinned more enormously than the rest, so they treated him more shamefully even in death: for when he was already slain they beheaded him, and hung his head on the top of the citadel. And because he had sinned especially by hand and tongue, stretching out his hand insolently against the temple, and blaspheming with his tongue and uttering many most wicked words, they therefore cut off his hand and his tongue, as is contained in the last chapter of the second book, where this history is described more fully[[2 Mach 15:30||]][[2 Mach 15:33||]]. [[7:47|and hung it up over against Jerusalem|Et manum ejus suspenderunt contra Jerusalem]] (his hand, that is). In the second book it has: [[2 Mach 15:33|over against the temple|Contra templum]] [the margin reads "Ibid. 23"; the words are those of 2 Mach 15:33]. It is therefore to be understood that they hung up the wicked man's hand opposite the temple and the city, at the edge of which the temple was situated. [[7:50|And the land of Juda was quiet|Et siluit terra Juda]] [[7:50|for a short time|paucos dies]], that is, for a little while the Jewish people rested from battles, as appears in the next chapter.

8.title: Elucidatio capituli octavi: Et audivit Judas nomen Romanorum, quia sunt potentes viribus.
8.title_en: Explanation of the eighth chapter: Now Judas heard of the fame of the Romans, that they are powerful and strong.

paras.t: Describitur hic, qualiter Judas confugit ad humana præsidia, imo ad Romanorum idololatrarum auxilia. Propter quod videtur divini promeruisse subtractionem subsidii, quum jam dudum ante Deus per Prophetam suum dixisset ad regem Juda: O rex, ne egrediatur tecum exercitus Israel ad pugnam: non enim est Dominus cum Israel. Quod si putas in robore exercitus bella consistere, superari te faciet Dominus ab hostibus: Dei quippe est adjuvare et in fugam vertere.
paras.en: Here it is described how Judas fled for refuge to human protection, nay, to the help of the Romans, who were idolaters. For this he seems to have deserved the withdrawal of God's aid, since long before God had said through His prophet to the king of Juda: [[2 Par 25:7|O king, let not the army of Israel go out with thee|O rex, ne egrediatur tecum exercitus Israel]] to battle: [[2 Par 25:7|for the Lord is not with Israel|non enim est Dominus cum Israel]]. [[2 Par 25:8|And if thou think that battles consist in the strength of the army, God will make thee to be overcome by the enemies: for it belongeth to God both to help, and to put to flight|Quod si putas in robore exercitus bella consistere, superari te faciet Dominus ab hostibus: Dei quippe est adjuvare et in fugam vertere]].

paras.t: Et audivit Judas nomen, id est famam, Romanorum, qui tempore Judæ monarchiam pro magna parte fuerunt adepti: nondum tamen plenarie usque ad tempus imperii Julii, vel potius Octaviani; quia potentes sunt viribus, et acquiescunt ad omnia quæ postulantur ab eis rationabiliter: nam pii fuerunt; et quicumque accesserint ad eos ad faciendum cum ipsis amicitiam, annuerunt.
paras.en: [[8:1|Now Judas heard of the fame|Et audivit Judas nomen]], that is, the renown, [[8:1|of the Romans|Romanorum]], who in the time of Judas had for the most part obtained the monarchy [that is, dominion over the whole world], though not fully until the time of the empire of Julius, or rather of Octavian; [[8:1|that they are powerful and strong|quia potentes sunt viribus]], [[8:1|and willingly agree to all things that are requested of them|et acquiescunt ad omnia quæ postulantur ab eis]] in reason: for they were kindly; [[8:1|and that whosoever have come to them|et quicumque accesserint ad eos]] to make friendship with them, they consented.

paras.t: Audierunt Judas et sui prælia eorum, scilicet Romanorum, qui victoriosi fuerunt in bellis, et virtutes bonas, id est benevolos actus, quas fecerunt in Galatia: quæ est regio Græciæ; quia obtinuerunt eos, et duxerunt sub tributum: id est, Romani subjugaverunt sibi Galatas in tributarios; ipsis quoque sic subjugatis fuerunt benevoli.
paras.en: [[8:2|And they heard|Audierunt]], Judas and his men, [[8:2|of their battles|prælia eorum]], that is, of the Romans, who were victorious in war, [[8:2|and their noble acts|et virtutes bonas]] [Latin virtutes bonas, good deeds of power; Denis takes them as deeds of kindness], that is, their kindly deeds, [[8:2|which they had done in Galatia|quas fecerunt in Galatia]], which is a region of Greece; [[8:2|how they had conquered them, and brought them under tribute|quia obtinuerunt eos, et duxerunt sub tributum]]: that is, the Romans subdued the Galatians to themselves as tributaries; and to them, once so subdued, they were kindly.

paras.t: Et quanta, id est quam magna et strenua opera, fecerunt in regione Hispaniæ, et quod in potestatem suam redegerunt metalla argenti et auri, quæ ibi sunt, et possederunt omnem locum, id est quædam loca de omnibus; vel, Omnem locum, pro quo obtinendo egressi sunt: consilio suo et patientia: quia ut allegatum est sæpe, ad prævalendum in præliis plus confert prudentia, quam fortitudo. Consilium autem est actus prudentis. Patientia quoque plurimum proficit ad triumphum. Ipsos namque pugnatores oportet frequenter multa et magna pati incommoda: in quibus patientia est necessaria, ne propter hujusmodi aspera labor bellicus omittatur. Hinc libro de Re militari scribit Vegetius, quod per nullam rem Romani ita sibi subjugaverunt orbem, sicut per prudentiam bellicam, exercitiumque armorum. Græci enim, ut ait, erant eis astutiores, Gallici numero plures, Hispani ferociores, Teutonici corpore grandiores.
paras.en: [[8:3|And how great things|Et quanta]], that is, how great and vigorous works, [[8:3|they had done in the land of Spain|fecerunt in regione Hispaniæ]], [[8:3|and that they had brought under their power the mines of silver and of gold that are there|et quod in potestatem suam redegerunt metalla argenti et auri, quæ ibi sunt]], [[8:3|and had gotten possession of all the place|et possederunt omnem locum]], that is, certain places out of all; or, all the place, that is, all the place they had gone out to win: [[8:3|by their counsel and patience|consilio suo et patientia]]. For, as has often been said, to prevail in battle prudence avails more than strength; and counsel is the act of the prudent man. Patience too does very much toward the triumph: for the fighters themselves must often suffer many great hardships, in which patience is needed, lest the toil of war be given up because of such harshness. Hence Vegetius writes in his book On Military Matters that by nothing did the Romans so subdue the world to themselves as by skill in war and the practice of arms. For the Greeks, as he says, were more cunning than they, the Gauls more numerous, the Spaniards fiercer, the Germans larger of body.

paras.t: Et Philippum et Persen Cetheorum regem. Josephus dicit, Reges: et forsan ponitur hic singulare pro plurali. Et Antiochum magnum regem Asiæ contritum, id est victum, ab eis. Ille Antiochus fuit pater Antiochi Epiphanis, ut patuit in expositione primi capituli.
paras.en: And [[8:5|Philip and Perses the king of the Ceteans|Philippum et Persen Cetheorum regem]]. Josephus says kings: and perhaps the singular is put here for the plural [Philip and Perses were both kings of Macedon]. [[8:6|And how Antiochus, the great king of Asia|Et Antiochum magnum regem Asiæ]] [[8:6|was routed|contritum]], that is, conquered, [[8:6|by them|ab eis]]. This Antiochus was the father of Antiochus Epiphanes, as was shown in the exposition of the first chapter.

paras.t: Et statuerunt, id est, injunxerunt ei, ut daret eis, puta Romanis, tributum magnum, et constitutum, id est, id quod exegerunt ab eo ultra tributum. Et regionem Indorum esse victam ab eis, et Medos et Lydos de optimis regionibus eorum, supple, esse ejectos a Romanis; et acceptas eas ab illis, id est regiones Medorum atque Lydorum vi armorum obtentas ab ipsis Medis ac Lydis per Romanos, dederunt ipsi Romani Eumeni regi ipsis confœderato.
paras.en: [[8:7|and appointed to him|Et statuerunt]], that is, they enjoined upon him, that he [[8:7|should pay|ut daret]] to them, namely to the Romans, [[8:7|a great tribute|tributum magnum]], [[8:7|and that which was agreed upon|et constitutum]], that is, what they exacted from him over and above the tribute. [[8:8|And the country of the Indians|Et regionem Indorum]] was conquered by them, [[8:8|and of the Medes, and of the Lydians|et Medos et Lydos]], [[8:8|some of their best provinces|de optimis regionibus eorum]]: supply, were driven out by the Romans, that is, the Medes and Lydians out of their best provinces; [[8:8|and those which they had taken from them|et acceptas eas ab illis]], that is, the regions of the Medes and Lydians, won by force of arms from the Medes and Lydians themselves by the Romans, [[8:8|they gave|dederunt]], the Romans themselves, [[8:8|to king Eumenes|Eumeni regi]], their confederate.

paras.t: Et quia qui erant apud Helladan, id est regionem seu locum sic dictum, voluerunt ire et tollere eos, videlicet Eumenem regem ac suos de præfatis terris Medorum et Lydorum, et innotuit sermo his, id est, propositum illorum exsistentium apud Helladan fuit patefactum Romanis. Et miserunt ad eos, id est ad Eumenem ac populum ejus, ducem unum cum suo exercitu in illorum subsidium, et pugnaverunt rex ille et dux missus a Romanis, contra illos exsistentes apud Helladan, et ceciderunt ex illis Helladanis multi; et captivas duxerunt Romani uxores.
paras.en: [[8:9|And that they who were in Greece|Et quia qui erant apud Helladan]] [Latin apud Helladan, in Hellas], that is, a region or place so called, [[8:9|had a mind to go and to destroy them|voluerunt ire et tollere eos]], namely king Eumenes and his people, out of the aforesaid lands of the Medes and Lydians, [[8:9|and they had knowledge thereof|et innotuit sermo his]], that is, the purpose of those who lived in Hellas was made known to the Romans. [[8:10|And they sent|Et miserunt]] to them, that is, to Eumenes and his people, [[8:10|a general|ducem unum]] with his army to help them [the Douay-Rheims has sent a general against them; Denis takes ad eos as to them, in aid of Eumenes], [[8:10|and fought|et pugnaverunt]], that king and the general sent by the Romans, [[8:10|with them|contra illos]] who lived in Hellas, [[8:10|and many of them were slain|et ceciderunt ex illis]], of the men of Hellas, and the Romans [[8:10|carried away their wives|captivas duxerunt Romani uxores]] captive.

paras.t: Cum amicis autem suis, et qui in ipsis requiem habebant, id est, sub eorum defensione et confœderatione quiescebant, conservaverunt amicitiam.
paras.en: [[8:12|But with their friends, and such as relied upon them|Cum amicis autem suis, et qui in ipsis requiem habebant]] [literally, had rest in them], that is, rested under their protection and alliance, [[8:12|they kept amity|conservaverunt amicitiam]].

paras.t: Et in omnibus his nemo Romanorum portabat diadema, id est, nullus fuit inter eos imperator aut rex. Nempe primus rex Romanorum fuit Romulus conditor urbis cum fratre suo Remo: quo occiso a Fabio Romuli duce, Romulus factus est rex urbis. Post quem præfuerunt reges in urbe usque Tarquinium Superbum: quo cum filio suo Tarquinio feroce a Romanis expulso, cœperunt præesse et præfuerunt consules, deinde dictatores atque tribuni plebis usque ad Julium Cæsarem, qui usurpavit et invasit imperium: cui successit Octavianus, sub quo natus est Christus. Ideo tempore Machabæorum non præerant reges Romanis.
paras.en: [[8:14|And none of all these|Et in omnibus his nemo]] of the Romans [[8:14|wore a crown|portabat diadema]], that is, there was no emperor or king among them. For the first king of the Romans was Romulus, founder of the city with his brother Remus; and when Remus had been slain by Fabius, Romulus's captain, Romulus became king of the city. After him kings ruled in the city down to Tarquin the Proud; and when he had been driven out by the Romans with his fierce son Tarquin, consuls began to rule and did rule, and then dictators and tribunes of the people, down to Julius Caesar, who usurped and seized the empire; and he was succeeded by Octavian, under whom Christ was born. So in the time of the Machabees the Romans were not ruled by kings.

paras.t: Et quia curiam fecerunt sibi, et quotidie consulebant, id est, de agendis et evitandis inter se conquirebant, trecenti viginti consilium agentes semper de multitudine, id est, trecenti viginti illi erant ex multitudine Romanorum electi, tanquam prudentiores ad tractanda consilia. Vel sensus est, quod trecenti viginti consulebant de multitudine, id est de ipsa communitate, quod scilicet prodesset reipublicæ et paci omnium subditorum. Ut quæ digna sunt, gerant, id est, vere expedientia et eorum majestatem decentia agant ac prosequantur, juxta illud Isaiæ: Princeps, quæ digna sunt principe, cogitabit, et ipse super duces stabit.
paras.en: [[8:15|And that they had made themselves a senate house|Et quia curiam fecerunt sibi]], [[8:15|and consulted daily|et quotidie consulebant]], that is, inquired among themselves about what was to be done and what avoided, [[8:15|three hundred and twenty men, that sat in counsel always for the people|trecenti viginti consilium agentes semper de multitudine]] [a marginal note gives the variant trecentos, as in the Vulgate; de multitudine can mean from the people or about the people]: that is, those three hundred and twenty were chosen out of the multitude of the Romans, as the more prudent, to treat of counsels. Or the sense is that the three hundred and twenty took counsel about the multitude, that is, about the community itself: namely, what would profit the commonwealth and the peace of all the subjects; and [[8:15|that they might do the things that were right|Ut quæ digna sunt, gerant]], that is, that they might do and carry through what is truly expedient and befits their majesty [digna, worthy: the Douay-Rheims has right here and worthy in Isaias], according to that of Isaias: [[Is 32:8|the prince will devise such things as are worthy of a prince, and he shall stand above the rulers|Princeps, quæ digna sunt principe, cogitabit, et ipse super duces stabit]].

paras.t: Ecce qualiter Romani isti adhuc gentiles, agnoverunt quod in Proverbiis Salomon dixit: Qui cuncta agunt consilio, reguntur sapientia. Et rursus: Qui pacis ineunt consilia, sequetur eos gaudium. Itemque: Erit salus ubi multa consilia. Si Romani illi pagani ad temporalem prosperitatem suum regimen referentes, tam assidue atque quotidie inter se contulerunt et consuluerunt de bono communi: quanto magis Pontifex summus et curia ejus, quorum est ad æternam beatitudinem ordinare præsidentiam suam, deberent quotidie inter se perscrutari, consulere, determinare ea, quæ ad totius Ecclesiæ et universorum statuum, graduum, potestatum, et ordinum ejus pertinent reformationem, profectum atque salutem? Quod et suo modo unusquisque regum et principum, episcoporum et prælatorum deberet peragere, quatenus juxta dignitatem prælationum et officiorum eorum, esset et dignitas actionum ac gubernationum ipsorum. Verum, homo quum in honore esset, non intellexit; comparatus est jumentis insipientibus.
paras.en: See how these Romans, still Gentiles, recognised what Solomon said in the Proverbs: [[Prov 13:10|they that do all things with counsel, are ruled by wisdom|Qui cuncta agunt consilio, reguntur sapientia]]. And again: [[Prov 12:20|joy followeth them that take counsels of peace|Qui pacis ineunt consilia, sequetur eos gaudium]]. And again: [[Prov 24:6|there shall be safety where there are many counsels|Erit salus ubi multa consilia]] [the margin gives Prov. xi, 14, which says the same; Denis's words are those of Prov 24:6]. If those pagan Romans, who directed their government to temporal prosperity, conferred and took counsel among themselves so assiduously and daily about the common good, how much more ought the Supreme Pontiff and his curia, whose office it is to order their government to eternal beatitude, daily to search out among themselves, take counsel upon and determine the things that belong to the reform, progress and salvation of the whole Church and of all its states, degrees, powers and orders? And this each of the kings and princes, the bishops and prelates, ought in his own way to carry out, so that, answering to the dignity of their prelacies and offices, there might also be dignity in their actions and governance. But man, [[Ps 48:21|when he was in honour did not understand: he hath been compared to senseless beasts|quum in honore esset, non intellexit; comparatus est jumentis insipientibus]] [the margin gives Ps. xlviii, 13, 21: the words stand in both verses].

paras.t: Et committunt uni homini magistratum suum per singulos annos: qui præfuit ceteris universis tempore suo. Sicque regimen eorum fuit quodammodo monarchicum et regale: quod (teste Philosopho) optimum est, absolute loquendo, habetque admixtum aliquid, imo et multum de aristocratia et democratia. Et tale regimen in certo casu ex specialibus causis, et ad tempus potest optimum esse. Et omnes obediunt uni tempore præsidentiæ suæ. Obedientia namque est summe necessaria et saluberrima res in omni communitate: sine qua nulla politia, nulla villa, nulla domus potest subsistere, ut in regula sua sanctus scribit Hieronymus. De ista materia multiplicis regiminis, et quid sit optimum, atque de antiquo illo regimine Romanorum, magistraliter tractat S. Thomas in libro suo de Regimine regum; Ægidius quoque in libro de Regimine principum.
paras.en: [[8:16|And that they committed their government to one man every year|Et committunt uni homini magistratum suum per singulos annos]], who was over all the rest in his time. And so their government was in a manner monarchical and kingly, which (as the Philosopher witnesses) is the best, speaking absolutely; and it has some admixture, nay much, of aristocracy and democracy. And such a government, in a certain case, for special reasons and for a time, can be the best; [[8:16|and they all obey one|Et omnes obediunt uni]] during the time of his presidency. For obedience is a thing supremely necessary and most wholesome in every community: without it no state, no town, no house can stand, as St Jerome writes in his rule. Of this matter of the manifold kinds of government, and which is the best, and of that ancient government of the Romans, St Thomas treats masterfully in his book On the Government of Kings, and Giles [of Rome] also in his book On the Government of Princes.

paras.t: Et non est invidia neque zelus, id est rancor aut contentio, inter eos: sicut solet inter ambitiosos consistere. Durante autem hac bonitate regiminis Romanorum, profecerunt in multis, et in brevi venerunt ad maximum incrementum, prout de hoc Cato et Tullius multa conscribunt. Postea vero fuit hoc regimen in ipsis corruptum: unde venerunt ad miserabile decrementum. Nempe, ut ait Hieronymus, et ante eum Sallustius, sicut concordia parvæ res crescunt, sic per discordiam res maximæ dilabuntur.
paras.en: And [[8:16|there is no envy nor jealousy|non est invidia neque zelus]], that is, rancour or strife, [[8:16|amongst them|inter eos]], as there commonly is among the ambitious. And while this goodness of the Romans' government lasted, they prospered in many things, and in a short time came to the greatest increase, as Cato and Tully write at length. But afterwards this government was corrupted among them, and so they came to a wretched decline. For, as Jerome says, and before him Sallust, as by concord small things grow, so by discord the greatest things fall apart.

paras.t: Et elegit Judas Eupolemum et Jasonem, et misit eos Romam constituere cum illis, puta Romanis, amicitiam et societatem, et ut Romani auferrent ab eis, videlicet a Judæis, jugum Græcorum, id est grave dominium, quo reges Syriæ opprimebant populum Judæorum. Dicitur autem jugum illud, Græcorum, quoniam ex Græcorum imperio exstitit derivatum. Et placuit sermo legatorum Judæ, in conspectu eorum, scilicet Romanorum.
paras.en: [[8:17|So Judas chose Eupolemus|Et elegit Judas Eupolemum]] [[8:17|and Jason|et Jasonem]], [[8:17|and he sent them to Rome|et misit eos Romam]] [[8:17|to make a league|constituere]] with them, namely the Romans, [[8:17|of amity and confederacy|amicitiam et societatem]], and that the Romans [[8:18|might take off from them|auferrent ab eis]], that is, from the Jews, [[8:18|the yoke of the Grecians|jugum Græcorum]], that is, the heavy dominion with which the kings of Syria oppressed the people of the Jews. That yoke is called the Grecians' because it was derived from the empire of the Greeks. [[8:21|And the proposal was pleasing|Et placuit sermo]] of Judas's envoys [[8:21|in their sight|in conspectu eorum]], namely of the Romans.

paras.t: Et rescripserunt in tabulis æreis ad perpetuam rei memoriam: Bene sit Romanis et genti Judæorum in mari, id est bellis navalibus, negotiisque marinis, et in terra in æternum, id est per omne tempus vitæ eorum.
paras.en: And [[8:22|they wrote back again|rescripserunt]] [[8:22|in tables of brass|in tabulis æreis]] for a perpetual memorial of the matter: [[8:23|GOOD SUCCESS BE TO THE ROMANS|Bene sit Romanis]], [[8:23|and to the people of the Jews by sea|et genti Judæorum in mari]], that is, in wars at sea and the business of the sea, [[8:23|and by land, for ever|et in terra in æternum]], that is, for the whole time of their life.

paras.t: Quod si institerit bellum Romanis prius, aut omnibus sociis eorum, id est cuicumque genti Romanis confœderatæ, auxilium feret gens Judæorum, prout tempus dictaverit, id est, dispositio temporis seu casus occurrens exegerit, corde pleno, id est prompto atque omnino spontaneo.
paras.en: [[8:24|But if there come first any war upon the Romans, or any of their confederates|Quod si institerit bellum Romanis prius, aut omnibus sociis eorum]], that is, upon any nation confederate with the Romans. [[8:25|The nation of the Jews shall help them|auxilium feret gens Judæorum]], [[8:25|according as the time shall direct|prout tempus dictaverit]], that is, as the ordering of the time or a chance that arises shall require, [[8:25|with all their heart|corde pleno]], that is, readily and wholly of their own will.

paras.t: Et præliantibus, id est, Judæis Romanos juvantibus, non dabunt Romani triticum, arma, pecuniam, id est stipendium, vel naves, sicut placuit Romanis, id est, prout Romani istud instituerunt; et custodient Judæi mandata eorum, videlicet Romanorum, nihil ab eis, id est Romanis, accipientes ipsi Judæi, sed suis expensis servientes ac subvenientes Romanis.
paras.en: [[8:26|Neither shall they give them|non dabunt]], that is, the Romans shall not give, [[8:26|whilst they are fighting|Et præliantibus]], that is, to the Jews when they help the Romans, [[8:26|wheat, or arms, or money|triticum, arma, pecuniam]], that is, pay, [[8:26|or ships|vel naves]], [[8:26|as it hath seemed good to the Romans|sicut placuit Romanis]], that is, as the Romans have ordained this; [[8:26|and they shall obey their orders|et custodient Judæi mandata eorum]], namely the Jews those of the Romans, [[8:26|without taking any thing|nihil]] [[8:26|of them|ab eis]], that is, of the Romans: the Jews themselves serving and aiding the Romans at their own expense.

paras.t: Similiter succurrent Romani Judæis; adjuvabunt Romani, et adjuvantibus Romanis ipsos Judæos, non dabitur a Judæis triticum, etc., id est stipendium; sed Romani suis expensis succurrent Judæis.
paras.en: [[8:27|In like manner|Similiter]] the Romans will succour the Jews: [[8:27|the Romans shall help them|adjuvabunt Romani]]; and [[8:28|to them that come to their aid|adjuvantibus]], that is, to the Romans helping the Jews themselves, [[8:28|there shall not be given|non dabitur]] by the Jews [[8:28|wheat|triticum]], etc., that is, pay; but the Romans will succour the Jews at their own expense.

paras.t: Quod si post hæc verba, hi aut illi, id est Romani sive Judæi, addere vel demere ad hæc vel ab his aliquid voluerint, facient ex proposito suo, id est concordi deliberatione, seu communi utriusque partis consensu.
paras.en: And [[8:30|if after this, one party or the other|Quod si post hæc verba, hi aut illi]], that is, the Romans or the Jews, [[8:30|shall have a mind to add to these articles, or take away any thing|addere vel demere ad hæc vel ab his aliquid voluerint]], [[8:30|they may do it at their pleasure|facient ex proposito suo]], that is, by agreed deliberation, or by the common consent of both parties.

paras.t: Sed et scripsimus ei, id est Demetrio, dicentes: Quare gravasti jugum tuum, id est potestatis tuæ tyrannidem et abusum, super amicos nostros et socios Judæos? Si ergo iterum adierint, id est accesserint, nos, adversum te conquerendo, atque subsidium postulando, faciemus illis judicium, id est judicialem vindictam, et pugnabimus tecum, id est contra te, mari, id est bello navali, terraque.
paras.en: Moreover [[8:31|we have written to him|scripsimus ei]], that is, to Demetrius, [[8:31|saying|dicentes]]: [[8:31|Why hast thou made thy yoke heavy|Quare gravasti jugum tuum]], that is, the tyranny and abuse of thy power, [[8:31|upon our friends and allies, the Jews|super amicos nostros et socios Judæos]]? [[8:32|If, therefore, they come again|Si ergo iterum adierint]], that is, approach, [[8:32|to us complaining of thee|nos, adversum te conquerendo]], and asking for help, [[8:32|we will do them justice|faciemus illis judicium]], that is, judicial vengeance, [[8:32|and will make war against thee|et pugnabimus tecum]] [the Latin tecum, with thee, here means against thee], [[8:32|by sea|mari]], that is, in naval war, [[8:32|and land|terraque]].

9.title: Explanatio capituli noni: Interea, ut audivit Demetrius quia cecidit Nicanor.
9.title_en: Explanation of the ninth chapter: In the mean time, when Demetrius heard that Nicanor was fallen.

paras.t: Mors Judæ et institutio fratris sui Jonathæ, ac aliqua ejus bella hic describuntur.
paras.en: The death of Judas, and the appointment of his brother Jonathan, and some of his wars, are described here.

paras.t: Interea, id est, inter ea quæ dicta sunt, hoc est infra tempus quo legati Judæ et populi sui fuerunt in expeditione commissi eis negotii occupati, ut audivit Demetrius quia cecidit Nicanor et exercitus ejus in prælio, apposuit Bacchidem et Alcimum rursus mittere in Judæam, et dextrum cornu cum illis, id est fortiores et constantiores de suo exercitu, qui solent poni in dextera parte, et regi a dextris adsistere. Et abierunt, et castra posuerunt in Masaloth, et occupaverunt eam, et peremerunt animas hominum multas, intelligendo per animas ipsos homines, qui quantum ad corpus, occidebantur. Per partem etenim totum exprimitur, juxta præhabita.
paras.en: [[9:1|In the mean time|Interea]], that is, amid the things that have been told, that is, within the time in which the envoys of Judas and of his people were taken up with carrying out the business entrusted to them, [[9:1|when Demetrius heard that Nicanor and his army were fallen in battle|ut audivit Demetrius quia cecidit Nicanor et exercitus ejus in prælio]], [[9:1|he sent again Bacchides and Alcimus into Judea|apposuit Bacchidem et Alcimum rursus mittere in Judæam]]; [[9:1|and the right wing of his army with them|et dextrum cornu cum illis]], that is, the stronger and steadier men of his army, who are usually placed on the right side, and stand at the king's right hand. And they went off, [[9:2|and they camped in Masaloth|et castra posuerunt in Masaloth]], [[9:2|and they made themselves masters of it|et occupaverunt eam]], [[9:2|and slew many people|et peremerunt animas hominum multas]] [literally "slew many souls of men"], understanding by *souls* the men themselves, who were slain as to the body. For the whole is expressed by the part, as was said before.

paras.t: Et Judas posuerat castra in Laisa, et tria millia viri electi cum eo, id est cum Juda. Et viderunt qui erant cum Juda multitudinem exercitus Bacchidis, qui multi sunt, scilicet viginti millia peditum et duo millia equitum, et timuerunt valde: quum tamen frequenter prævaluissent in bellis, in quibus comparative loquendo, pauciores erant respectu adversariorum, quam in isto occursu; sed ad Romanos idololatras confugiendo, meruerunt privari confortatione animationis ac confidentiæ Dei: et non remanserunt nisi octingenti viri cum Juda. Et vidit quod defluxit, id est, minoratus sic fuit, exercitus ejus, et bellum perurgebat eum, id est, valde arctabat eum, ita quod sine suorum periculo non poterant declinare; et confractus est corde, id est, solitam confidentiam in Deo amisit pro parte, quia non habebat tempus congregandi eos, qui defluxerunt de suo exercitu; et dissolutus est formidine quadam, subtracta sibi solita magnanimitate et spe plena in Deo, quia ad hominum infidelium confugerat opem. Unde nec in isto congressu legitur suos more solito ad confidendum in Domino admonuisse, aut precem fudisse ad Deum, sed potius cum ambiguitate quadam dixisse: Eamus ad adversarios nostros, si poterimus pugnare adversus eos.
paras.en: [[9:5|Now Judas had pitched his tents in Laisa, and three thousand chosen men with him|Et Judas posuerat castra in Laisa, et tria millia viri electi cum eo]], that is, with Judas. [[9:6|And they saw|Et viderunt]], those who were with Judas, [[9:6|the multitude of the army|multitudinem exercitus]] of Bacchides, [[9:6|that they were many|qui multi sunt]], namely twenty thousand foot and two thousand horse[[9:4||]], [[9:6|and they were seized with great fear|et timuerunt valde]]: though they had often prevailed in wars in which, comparatively speaking, they were fewer in respect of their adversaries than in this encounter; but by fleeing for refuge to the idolatrous Romans they deserved to be deprived of the strengthening of courage and of confidence in God: [[9:6|and there remained of them no more than eight hundred men|et non remanserunt nisi octingenti viri]] with Judas.
