[[9:7|And Judas saw that his army slipped away|Et vidit quod defluxit, id est, minoratus sic fuit, exercitus ejus]] (that is, was thus diminished), [[9:7|and the battle pressed upon him|et bellum perurgebat eum]], that is, hemmed him in closely, so that they could not turn aside without danger to his men; [[9:7|and his heart was cast down|et confractus est corde]], that is, he lost in part his wonted confidence in God, [[9:7|because he had not time to gather them together|quia non habebat tempus congregandi eos]], who had slipped away from his army; [[9:7|and he was discouraged|et dissolutus est]] by a certain fear, his wonted magnanimity and full hope in God being withdrawn from him, because he had fled for refuge to the help of unbelieving men. Hence we do not read that in this encounter he exhorted his men, as was his custom, to trust in the Lord, or poured out prayer to God, but rather that he said with a certain doubtfulness: Let us [[9:8|go against our enemies, if we may be able to fight against them|Eamus ad adversarios nostros, si poterimus pugnare adversus eos]].

paras.t: Verumtamen, quia habitum magnanimitatis aliarumque virtutum in magna excellentia habuit, non fuit totaliter mente dejectus, nec fugere acquievit; imo ad moriendum pro bono communi exhibuit se paratum, dicendo: Si appropiavit, id est, si nunc instat, tempus nostrum, id est finis curriculi vitæ nostræ, moriamur in virtute, id est in exercitio virtuoso fortitudinis, justitiæ, imo et caritatis fraternæ. Ideo subditur, propter fratres nostros, id est pro communi pace et salute proximorum nostrorum, quatenus liberati ab hostibus, Deo secundum legem deserviant. Et non inferamus crimen gloriæ nostræ, id est maculam famæ nostræ, vel opprobrium eminentiæ nostræ, neque excessum meritis nostris, pro quibus nobis debetur gloria æternalis.
paras.en: Yet because he possessed the habit of magnanimity and of the other virtues in great excellence, he was not altogether cast down in mind, nor would he consent to flee; nay, he showed himself ready to die for the common good, saying: [[9:10|but if our time be come|Si appropiavit, id est, si nunc instat, tempus nostrum]] (*be come*, that is, if it is now at hand; *our time*, that is, the end of the course of our life), [[9:10|let us die manfully|moriamur in virtute]] [literally "in virtue", which Denis takes in its full sense], that is, in the virtuous exercise of fortitude, of justice, and indeed of brotherly charity. Therefore it is added, [[9:10|for our brethren|propter fratres nostros]], that is, for the common peace and safety of our neighbours, so that, freed from their enemies, they may serve God according to the law. [[9:10|and let us not stain our glory|Et non inferamus crimen gloriæ nostræ]] [literally "let us not bring a charge upon our glory"], that is, a blot upon our fame, or disgrace upon our eminence, nor a fault upon our merits, for which eternal glory is owed us.

paras.t: Et movit exercitus Judæ de castris, id est tentoriis suis: in quo patet adhuc Judæ audacia, quod sic magnanimiter ivit obviam tanto exercitui inimicorum suorum; et divisi sunt equites Bacchidis in duas partes; et fundibularii et sagittarii præibant exercitum Bacchidis; et primi certaminis omnes potentes, id est, viri exsistentes in dextro cornu cum Bacchide, qui erant primo pugnaturi, fuerunt validi pugnatores. Et proximavit legio militum Bacchidis ex duabus partibus. Et commota est terra a voce exercituum, id est, habitantes in terra sunt admirati et quodam horrore concussi. Vel ipsa terra quasi timere videbatur ex buccinarum et tubarum clangore, congredientiumque clamore et collisione armorum atque strepitibus ictuum.
paras.en: [[9:11|And the army removed out of the camp|Et movit exercitus Judæ de castris]] (the army of Judas), that is, from its tents: in which the boldness of Judas still appears, that he went so magnanimously to meet so great an army of his enemies; [[9:11|and the horsemen were divided into two troops|et divisi sunt equites Bacchidis in duas partes]] (the horsemen of Bacchides); [[9:11|and the slingers, and the archers, went before the army|et fundibularii et sagittarii præibant exercitum]] of Bacchides; [[9:11|and they that were in the front were all men of valour|et primi certaminis omnes potentes]] [literally "those of the first fight were all mighty"], that is, the men stationed in the right wing with Bacchides, who were to fight first, were strong fighters. [[9:12|and the legion drew near on two sides|Et proximavit legio militum Bacchidis ex duabus partibus]]. [[9:13|and the earth shook at the noise of the armies|Et commota est terra a voce exercituum]], that is, the dwellers in the land were astonished and shaken with a kind of horror. Or the earth itself seemed as it were to fear, at the blare of horns and trumpets, the shouting of those joining battle, the clash of arms and the din of blows.

paras.t: Et vidit Judas quia firmior, id est robustior, est pars exercitus Bacchidis in dextris, id est in dextero cornu seu latere, et convenerunt cum ipso Bacchide omnes constantes corde, videlicet fortes et imperterriti; et contrita est dextera pars ab eis, id est, dexterum cornu illud a Juda et suis est dissipatum et victum, atque in fugam conversum, sicut subjungitur; et persecutus est eos usque ad montem Azoti. In quo patet mira fortitudo, strenuitas et elegantia Judæ et virorum suorum, et quod Deus omnipotens illum pusillum gregem suum in extremo illo conflictu non reliquit, sed mirabiliter confortavit, quamvis eos pro magna parte permisit occidi, quia feliciter obierunt, et virilissime suas compleverunt ac concluserunt congressiones et expeditiones. Unde et Josephus circa hoc refert: Videns Judas Bacchidem cum suis electis in dextero cornu ordinatum, congregans animosissimos viros, invasit illam partem exercitus, et confligens ibi, ordinem eorum dirupit, et medios ad fugam convertit.
paras.en: [[9:14|And Judas perceived that the stronger part of the army of Bacchides was on the right side|Et vidit Judas quia firmior, id est robustior, est pars exercitus Bacchidis in dextris]] (*stronger*, that is, sturdier; *on the right side*, that is, in the right wing or flank), [[9:14|and all the stout of heart came together with him|et convenerunt cum ipso Bacchide omnes constantes corde]] (with Bacchides himself) [Denis takes *with him* of Bacchides; the Douay-Rheims understands it of Judas], namely the strong and undaunted; [[9:15|And the right wing was discomfited by them|et contrita est dextera pars ab eis]], that is, that right wing was scattered and beaten by Judas and his men, and turned to flight, as is added: [[9:15|and he pursued them even to the mount Azotus|et persecutus est eos usque ad montem Azoti]]. In this appear the wonderful fortitude, vigour and excellence of Judas and his men, and that almighty God did not forsake that little flock of his in that last conflict, but wonderfully strengthened it, although he allowed them for the most part to be slain: for they died happily, and most manfully completed and concluded their encounters and campaigns. Hence Josephus too relates of this: Judas, seeing Bacchides drawn up with his picked men in the right wing, gathered the most spirited men, attacked that part of the army, and fighting there broke their ranks and put those in the middle to flight.

paras.t: Et qui in sinistro cornu erant, viderunt quod contritum est dexterum cornu, et secuti sunt post Judam et eos qui cum ipso erant, a tergo. Et ingravatum est prælium contra Judam et suos, qui stabant in medio hostium adversariis circumsepti, jamque lassati, quia a mane usque ad vesperam pugnaverunt; et ceciderunt multi ex his et illis; plures tamen ex exercitu Bacchidis. Et Judas cecidit, et ceteri fugerunt, tali ac tanto capitaneo suo prostrato. Qui (ut Josephus scribit) fugere nolens, stans hostibus circumseptus et fortiter pugnans cum suis, multos interfecit adversariorum, et tandem percussus occubuit. Talis finis Judam invenit, virum fortem, magnum et bellicosum, mandatorum patris sui memorem, omnia pro libertate civium facere et pati paratum. Tali ergo virtute plenus, magnam sibi gloriam et monumenta servavit, liberans gentem suam a Macedonum servitute: qui quum principatum sacerdotii tribus annis habuisset, defunctus est. Hæc Josephus. Et Jonathas et Simon tulerunt Judam fratrem suum, id est, corpus ejus abstulerunt, non die eodem, sed paulo post: quod et ab hostibus redemerunt pecunia, ut in Scholastica (ex Josepho) fertur historia.
paras.en: [[9:16|And they that were in the left wing saw that the right wing was discomfited, and they followed after Judas, and them that were with him, at their back|Et qui in sinistro cornu erant, viderunt quod contritum est dexterum cornu, et secuti sunt post Judam et eos qui cum ipso erant, a tergo]]. [[9:17|And the battle was hard fought|Et ingravatum est prælium]] against Judas and his men, who stood in the midst of the enemy, hemmed in by their adversaries and already weary, because they had fought [[9:13|from morning even unto the evening|a mane usque ad vesperam]]; [[9:17|and there fell many|et ceciderunt multi]] [[9:17|of the one side and of the other|ex his et illis]], yet more from the army of Bacchides. [[9:18|And Judas was slain, and the rest fled away|Et Judas cecidit, et ceteri fugerunt]], such and so great a captain of theirs being laid low. He (as Josephus writes), refusing to flee, standing surrounded by the enemy and fighting bravely with his men, slew many of the adversaries, and at last fell stricken. Such was the end that found Judas, a brave man, great and warlike, mindful of his father's commands, ready to do and to suffer all things for the liberty of his fellow citizens. Full, then, of such virtue, he won for himself great glory and memorials, freeing his nation from slavery to the Macedonians; and when he had held the chief priesthood for three years, he died. So far Josephus. [[9:19|And Jonathan and Simon took Judas, their brother|Et Jonathas et Simon tulerunt Judam fratrem suum]], that is, they carried away his body, not on the same day but a little after; and they ransomed it from the enemy with money, as is related in the *Scholastic History* (from Josephus).

paras.t: Et cetera verba, id est gesta, bellorum Judæ et virtutum, id est virtuosorum strenuorumque operum ejus, non sunt descripta. Multa enim erant valde, ita quod singula describi vix poterant.
paras.en: [[9:22|But the rest of the words|Et cetera verba]], that is, deeds, [[9:22|of the wars of Judas, and of the noble acts|bellorum Judæ et virtutum]] [literally "of the virtues"], that is, of his virtuous and vigorous works, [[9:22|are not written|non sunt descripta]]. [[9:22|for they were very many|Multa enim erant valde]], so that they could hardly be described one by one.

paras.t: Et factum est, post mortem Judæ emerserunt, id est, de profundo malitiæ suæ diu abscondita exierunt aut proruperunt manifeste in medium, exstincto eo cujus timore non audebant hoc facere, viri iniqui in omnibus finibus Israel, etc. In diebus illis facta est fames, id est caristia, magna valde in terra Juda, et tradidit se Bacchidi omnis regio eorum cum ipsis, id est, Judæi communiter subjecerunt se Bacchidi sub tributo, seu etiam aliis modis, pro necessariis vitæ adipiscendis. Et facta est tribulatio magna in Israel: quoniam Bacchides amicos Judæ confusibiliter crudeliterque peremit.
paras.en: [[9:23|And it came to pass, after the death of Judas|Et factum est, post mortem Judæ]], [[9:23|began to put forth their heads|emerserunt]] [literally "emerged"], that is, came out, or broke forth openly into the midst, from the depth of their long-hidden malice, now that he was dead for fear of whom they did not dare to do this, [[9:23|the wicked|viri iniqui]] [[9:23|in all the confines of Israel|in omnibus finibus Israel]], etc. [[9:24|In those days there was a very great famine|In diebus illis facta est fames, id est caristia, magna valde]] (a famine, that is, a dearth) in the land of Juda, [[9:24|and they and all their country yielded to Bacchides|et tradidit se Bacchidi omnis regio eorum cum ipsis]], that is, the Jews in general submitted to Bacchides under tribute, or in other ways too, to obtain the necessaries of life. [[9:27|And there was a great tribulation in Israel|Et facta est tribulatio magna in Israel]]: because Bacchides put the friends of Judas to death shamefully and cruelly[[9:26||]].

paras.t: Et congregati sunt omnes amici Judæ, et dixerunt Jonathæ: Ex quo frater tuus Judas defunctus est, vir similis ei non est qui exeat contra inimicos nostros. Nunc itaque hodie te elegimus esse pro eo in principem et ducem. Et suscepit Jonathas tempore illo principatum ducatus et pontificatus, non ambitiose, sed ex communi et concordi populi sui electione, et tempore tantæ angustiæ, ut esset primus in omni congressu et acie. Et fugerunt Jonathas ac sui, eo quod Bacchides vellet eos occidere: et fugerunt caute, non vituperabiliter timide, in desertum, quousque adunarent se invicem, et exercitum congregarent, et consederunt ad aquam lacus Asphar, id est Mortui maris, per quod transit Jordanis, juxta illud Josue: Aquæ Jordanis inferiores, in mare Solitudinis, quod nunc vocatur Mortuum, descenderunt. Et die sabbatorum venit Bacchides ad impugnandum Jonathan; venitque sabbati die, vel in contemptum religionis Judæorum sabbato libenter quiescentium; vel putans Jonathan die illa non pugnaturum, aut saltem invite.
paras.en: [[9:28|And all the friends of Judas came together, and said to Jonathan|Et congregati sunt omnes amici Judæ, et dixerunt Jonathæ]]: [[9:29|Since thy brother Judas died there is not a man like him to go forth against our enemies|Ex quo frater tuus Judas defunctus est, vir similis ei non est qui exeat contra inimicos nostros]]. [[9:30|Now, therefore, we have chosen thee this day to be our prince, and captain, in his stead|Nunc itaque hodie te elegimus esse pro eo in principem et ducem]]. [[9:31|So Jonathan took upon him the government at that time|Et suscepit Jonathas tempore illo principatum]], the government of command and of the pontificate, not ambitiously, but by the common and harmonious election of his people, and in a time of such distress, that he might be first in every encounter and battle line. [[9:33|and they fled|Et fugerunt]], Jonathan and his men, because Bacchides wished to kill them[[9:32||]]: and they fled warily, not with blameworthy timidity, [[9:33|into the desert|in desertum]], until they could unite together and gather an army, [[9:33|and they pitched by the water of the lake Asphar|et consederunt ad aquam lacus Asphar]], that is, of the Dead Sea, through which the Jordan passes, according to that of Josue: The waters of the Jordan [[Jos 3:16|that were beneath, ran down into the sea of the wilderness, (which now is called the Dead Sea)|inferiores, in mare Solitudinis, quod nunc vocatur Mortuum, descenderunt]]. And [[9:34|on the sabbath day|die sabbatorum]] Bacchides came to attack Jonathan; and he came on the sabbath day either in contempt of the religion of the Jews, who gladly rest on the sabbath, or thinking that Jonathan would not fight on that day, or at least only unwillingly.

paras.t: Et Jonathas misit fratrem suum ducem populi, id est, Jonathas fratrem suum Joannem misit cum aliquibus quibus eum præfecit, et rogavit Nabuthæos amicos suos: qui secundum Josephum, Nabuthæi dicuntur ab urbe nomine Nabath; ut commendaret illis apparatum suum, id est, supellectilem suam apud illos deponeret, quousque contra Bacchidem ipse Jonathas dimicaret. Aliqui tamen habent, Ut commodarent illis apparatum suum, id est, quatenus Nabuthæi concederent Jonathæ ac suis arma sua atque tentoria. Et exierunt filii Jambri ex Madaba, id est urbe sic dicta, et comprehenderunt Joannem præfatum Jonathæ fratrem, etc. Et recordati sunt sanguinis fratris sui: id est, Jonathas et Simon recolentes injustam fratris sui Joannis occisionem a filiis Jambri, fecerunt ultionem, quæ in textu qui planus est, recitatur. Et vindicaverunt, id est, vindicando exercuerunt, vindictam sanguinis, id est effusionis sanguinis, fratris sui, zelo justitiæ.
paras.en: [[9:35|And Jonathan sent his brother, a captain of the people|Et Jonathas misit fratrem suum ducem populi]], that is, Jonathan sent his brother John with some men over whom he set him, [[9:35|to desire the Nabutheans his friends|et rogavit Nabuthæos amicos suos]] (who, according to Josephus, are called Nabutheans from a city named Nabath), that he might commit to them [[9:35|their equipage|apparatum suum]] [Denis's text reads *ut commendaret*, "that he might entrust"; the Vulgate has *ut commodarent*, "that they would lend", the reading he gives next], that is, deposit his goods with them, until Jonathan himself should fight against Bacchides. Some, however, have: [[9:35|that they would lend them their equipage|Ut commodarent illis apparatum suum]], that is, that the Nabutheans should let Jonathan and his men have their arms and tents. [[9:36|And the children of Jambri came forth out of Madaba|Et exierunt filii Jambri ex Madaba]], that is, a city so called, [[9:36|and took John|et comprehenderunt Joannem]], the aforesaid brother of Jonathan, etc. [[9:38|And they remembered the blood|Et recordati sunt sanguinis]] of [[9:38|their brother|fratris sui]]: that is, Jonathan and Simon, recalling the unjust slaying of their brother John by the children of Jambri, took the vengeance which is recounted in the text, which is plain. [[9:42|And they took revenge|Et vindicaverunt]], that is, by avenging they exacted it, [[9:42|for the blood of their brother|vindictam sanguinis, id est effusionis sanguinis, fratris sui]] (the blood, that is, its shedding), out of zeal for justice.

paras.t: Et dixit ad suos Jonathas: Surgamus et pugnemus contra inimicos nostros, videlicet Bacchidem et ejus exercitum. Non est enim hodie, sicut heri et nudiustertius, id est sicut præteritis diebus, in quibus fuit nobis libertas eundi ac divertendi hinc inde. Nunc autem oportet nos pugnando prævalere, aut infeliciter subdi seu trucidari. Nunc ergo clamate in cælum, Deum cæli invocando. Et commissum est bellum. Et extendit Jonathas manum suam percutere Bacchidem, quatenus principe impiorum hostium interempto, celerius prævaleret. Estque probabile, quod Bacchides vir valde audax, animosus et fortis, appropinquavit ad Jonathan ut eum occideret. Et divertit Bacchides ab eo retro: alioquin fuisset occisus a Jonatha. Et ceciderunt de parte Bacchidis mille viri; et reversi sunt in Jerusalem ipse Bacchides et sui, occisis de eorum exercitu mille viris.
paras.en: [[9:44|And Jonathan said to his company: Let us arise, and fight against our enemies|Et dixit ad suos Jonathas: Surgamus et pugnemus contra inimicos nostros]], namely Bacchides and his army. [[9:44|for it is not now as yesterday, and the day before|Non est enim hodie, sicut heri et nudiustertius]], that is, as in the past days, in which we were free to go and to turn aside hither and thither[[9:45||]]. But now we must prevail by fighting, or be miserably subdued or slaughtered. [[9:46|Now, therefore, cry ye to heaven|Nunc ergo clamate in cælum]], calling upon the God of heaven. [[9:46|And they joined battle|Et commissum est bellum]]. [[9:47|And Jonathan stretched forth his hand to strike Bacchides|Et extendit Jonathas manum suam percutere Bacchidem]], so that, the leader of the wicked enemy being slain, he might prevail the more quickly. And it is probable that Bacchides, a very bold, spirited and strong man, had come near to Jonathan to kill him. [[9:47|but he turned away from him backwards|Et divertit Bacchides ab eo retro]]: otherwise he would have been slain by Jonathan. [[9:49|And there fell of Bacchides' side|Et ceciderunt de parte Bacchidis]] [[9:49|a thousand men|mille viri]]; [[9:49|and they returned to Jerusalem|et reversi sunt in Jerusalem]], Bacchides himself and his men, a thousand men of their army having been slain.

paras.t: Et ædificaverunt, id est, captas munierunt, et in aliquibus exstruxerunt, civitates munitas in Judæa; et posuit custodias in eis, id est custodes et raptores de populo suo, ut inimicitias exercerent in Israel, id est, populum Judæorum spoliarent ac molestarent. Et accepit filios principum regionis, id est, filios principalium Judæorum sumpsit, in obsides, ne vel ipsi vel patres eorum contra se rebellarent, Jonathan adjuvando. Et præcepit Alcimus destrui muros, id est parietes seu munimenta muralia, domus sanctæ interioris, id est Sancti sanctorum, et opera Prophetarum, id est ædificia templi facta ex instigatione Zachariæ et Aggæi prophetarum sanctorum, ut patet in Esdra et Aggæo. In illo tempore percussus est Alcimus, id est plagatus a Deo, et occisus propter facinora sua.
paras.en: [[9:50|And they built|Et ædificaverunt]], that is, fortified those they had taken, and in some places built anew, [[9:50|strong cities in Judea|civitates munitas in Judæa]]; [[9:51|And he placed garrisons in them|et posuit custodias in eis]], that is, guards and plunderers from his own people, [[9:51|that they might wage war against Israel|ut inimicitias exercerent in Israel]], that is, might plunder and harass the people of the Jews. [[9:53|And he took the sons of the chief men of the country|Et accepit filios principum regionis]], that is, he took the sons of the leading Jews, [[9:53|for hostages|in obsides]], lest either they or their fathers should rebel against him by helping Jonathan. [[9:54|Alcimus commanded the walls|Et præcepit Alcimus destrui muros]] to be thrown down, that is, the partitions or the defences of the walls, [[9:54|of the inner court of the sanctuary|domus sanctæ interioris]] [literally "of the inner holy house"], that is, of the Holy of holies, [[9:54|and the works of the prophets|et opera Prophetarum]], that is, the buildings of the temple made at the urging of the holy prophets Zacharias and Aggeus, as appears in Esdras[[1 Esd 5:1||]][[1 Esd 6:14||]] and Aggeus[[Agg 1:14||]][[Zach 4:9||]] [the margin is partly unreadable: it seems to give 1 Esd. v, 1; vi, 14; Agg. i, 14; Zach. iv, 9]. [[9:55|At that time Alcimus was struck|In illo tempore percussus est Alcimus]], that is, smitten by God, and slain for his crimes[[9:56||]].

paras.t: Et apprehendit de viris regionis, qui principes erant militiæ ipsius Bacchidis, seu principales in ejus exercitu, quinquaginta viros, et occidit eos. Hoc Jonathas fecit, quum post mortem Alcimi Bacchides redisset ad regem, et rursus expletis duobus annis ad Judæam fuisset reversus. Et contritus, id est victus, non occisus, est Bacchides ab eis, hoc est a Jonatha et Simone. Et misit ad eum, puta ad Bacchidem volentem ad propria remeare, Jonathas legatos componere cum ipso Bacchide pacem, et reddere ei captivitatem: hoc est, ut Bacchides redderet Jonathæ eos quos de populo Jonathæ captivavit. Jonathas quoque præbuit se paratum reddere Bacchidi, quos captivos habuit de populo Bacchidis, ut Josephus refert. Et in hoc uterque consensit. Et cessavit gladius ex Israel, id est, populus Israel a solita hostium impugnatione est liberatus. Nihilo minus post hæc habuerunt et alia prælia, ut infra habetur, sed non tam dura neque ita assidua, sicut ante. Et habitavit Jonathas in Machmas, id est urbe Judææ sic nominata: de qua exponitur illud primi Regum libri, Erant cum Saul duo millia in Machmas.
paras.en: [[9:61|And he apprehended of the men of the country|Et apprehendit de viris regionis]], [[9:61|that were the principal authors of the mischief|qui principes erant militiæ]] [Denis reads *militiæ*, "of the army", for the Vulgate's *malitiæ*, "of the mischief", and explains accordingly] of Bacchides himself, that is, the leading men in his army, [[9:61|fifty men, and he slew them|quinquaginta viros, et occidit eos]]. This Jonathan did, when after the death of Alcimus Bacchides had gone back to the king[[9:57||]], and after two full years had returned again to Judea. [[9:68|and he was discomfited by them|Et contritus, id est victus, non occisus, est Bacchides ab eis]] (*discomfited*, that is, beaten, not slain), that is, by Jonathan and Simon. Jonathan [[9:70|sent ambassadors to him to make peace with him, and to restore to him the prisoners|et misit ad eum legatos componere pacem cum ipso, et reddere ei captivitatem]] (to him, that is, to Bacchides, who wished to go back to his own country): that is, that Bacchides should restore to Jonathan those of Jonathan's people whom he had taken captive. Jonathan, for his part, offered to restore to Bacchides those of Bacchides' people whom he held captive, as Josephus relates. And to this both agreed[[9:71||]]. [[9:73|So the sword ceased from Israel|Et cessavit gladius ex Israel]], that is, the people of Israel was freed from the wonted assaults of the enemy. Nevertheless after this they had other battles too, as is found below, but not so hard nor so continual as before. [[9:73|and Jonathan dwelt in Machmas|Et habitavit Jonathas in Machmas]], that is, a city of Judea so named: of which that passage of the first book of Kings is explained, [[1 Kings 13:2|two thousand were with Saul in Machmas|Erant cum Saul duo millia in Machmas]].

10.title: Expositio capituli decimi: Et anno centesimo sexagesimo ascendit Alexander.
10.title_en: Exposition of the tenth chapter: Now in the hundred and sixtieth year, Alexander came up.

paras.t: Gesta Jonathæ, bella ac prosperitas ejus sub multis regibus habita, hic narrantur.
paras.en: The deeds of Jonathan, and his wars and the prosperity he had under many kings, are related here.

paras.t: Et anno centesimo sexagesimo ascendit Alexander Antiochi filius, qui Alexander cognominatus est Nobilis, sicut avus ejus Epiphanes est cognominatus, sive Illustris. Aliqui autem accipiunt hoc loco Nobilem et Illustrem pro eodem; et addunt quod Alexander iste fuit filius Antiochi Nobilis seu Illustris, et frater Antiochi, qui Eupator vocatus est. Et occupavit Ptolemaidam; et receperunt illum, et regnavit illic, id est in urbe illa Syriæ. Atque, ut Josephus refert, ex proditione militum in Ptolemaida commorantium, Alexander fuit receptus: quia militibus illis displicuit Demetrius propter suam superbiam, quia dum se clausisset in quadam turre regali, quam non longe ab Antiochia construxerat, a nemine videbatur; sed et rem publicam ut desidiosus neglexit, ideo subditi oderant eum.
paras.en: [[10:1|Now in the hundred and sixtieth year|Et anno centesimo sexagesimo]] [[10:1|came up|ascendit]] [[10:1|Alexander, the son of Antiochus|Alexander Antiochi filius]], [[10:1|surnamed the Illustrious|qui Alexander cognominatus est Nobilis]] [Denis's text has *Nobilis*, "the Noble", which the Douay-Rheims renders "the Illustrious"; he distinguishes it here from *Illustris*], as his grandfather Epiphanes was surnamed, that is, the Illustrious[[1 Mach 1:11||]] [the margin gives I Mach. i, 14; the surname stands at 1 Mach 1:11]. Some, however, take *Noble* and *Illustrious* in this place for the same thing; and they add that this Alexander was the son of Antiochus the Noble or Illustrious, and the brother of the Antiochus who was called Eupator. [[10:1|and took Ptolemais|Et occupavit Ptolemaidam]]; [[10:1|and they received him|et receperunt illum]], [[10:1|and he reigned there|et regnavit illic]], that is, in that city of Syria. And, as Josephus relates, Alexander was received through the treachery of the soldiers stationed in Ptolemais: because Demetrius displeased those soldiers by his pride, for having shut himself up in a royal tower which he had built not far from Antioch, he was seen by no one; and he neglected the commonwealth like a sluggard, and therefore his subjects hated him.

paras.t: Et misit Demetrius rex epistolam ad Jonathan verbis pacificis, ex timore, ne Jonathas auxiliaretur Alexandro, memor molestiarum et injuriarum quas a Demetrio toleravit. Et dedit ei potestatem congregandi exercitum, et fabricare arma. Unde elicitur, quod Judæi vehementer premebantur jugo regum illorum. Et habitavit Jonathas in Jerusalem, et cœpit ædificare, id est meliorare in structuris, et innovare civitatem. Et fugerunt alienigenæ, id est gentiles, qui erant in munitionibus, id est locis munitis, quas ædificaverat Bacchides prope arcem, vel secundum quosdam, extra et prope Jerusalem. Tantum in Bethsura remanserant aliqui ex his qui reliquerant legem, id est apostatæ legis; in arce quoque, ut infra et in Josepho patet.
paras.en: [[10:3|And Demetrius sent a letter to Jonathan, with peaceable words|Et misit Demetrius rex epistolam ad Jonathan verbis pacificis]], out of fear that Jonathan would help Alexander[[10:4||]], remembering the troubles and wrongs he had suffered from Demetrius[[10:5||]]. [[10:6|And he gave him authority to gather together a army, and to make arms|Et dedit ei potestatem congregandi exercitum, et fabricare arma]]. From this it is gathered that the Jews were heavily oppressed by the yoke of those kings. [[10:10|And Jonathan dwelt in Jerusalem, and began to build|Et habitavit Jonathas in Jerusalem, et cœpit ædificare]], that is, to improve its buildings, [[10:10|and to repair the city|et innovare civitatem]]. [[10:12|Then the strangers|Et fugerunt alienigenæ]] fled, that is, the Gentiles, [[10:12|that were in the strong holds|qui erant in munitionibus]], that is, the fortified places, [[10:12|which Bacchides had built|quas ædificaverat Bacchides]] near the citadel, or, according to some, outside and near Jerusalem. [[10:14|Only in Bethsura there remained some of them, that had forsaken the law|Tantum in Bethsura remanserant aliqui ex his qui reliquerant legem]], that is, apostates from the law; and in the citadel too, as appears below and in Josephus.

paras.t: Et audivit Alexander rex, qualiter Demetrius scripserat Jonathæ: idcirco et ipse scripsit ei amorosam epistolam ex affectu non ficto, misitque ei munera pretiosa, ut patet in littera, in qua non est difficultas. Et induit se Jonathas stolam sanctam, id est vestem pontificalem. Nam Alexander non solum constituit eum summum sacerdotem, sed etiam misit ei stolam, ut Josephus narrat, quamvis hoc textus non dicat. In die solenni Scenopegiæ, id est dedicationis templi primi a Salomone constructi, ut quidam exponit: quæ expositio probatur inepta, quia in lege communiter per festum Scenopegiæ intelligitur festum Tabernaculorum. Josephus quoque refert: Suscipiens epistolam Alexandri Jonathas, induitur stola sacerdotali, festo Tabernaculorum instante. Festum quoque Scenopegiæ occurrebat septimo mense, ut patet in Levitico; de quo mense loquitur hic Scriptura, dicendo, Et induit se Jonathas stolam sanctam septimo mense. Verumtamen stolam illam a rege missam ipse consecravit, antequam utebatur ea in Dei obsequio.
paras.en: [[10:15|And king Alexander heard|Et audivit Alexander rex]] how Demetrius had written to Jonathan: therefore he too wrote him a loving letter[[10:17||]] out of unfeigned affection, and sent him precious gifts, as appears in the letter of the text, in which there is no difficulty. [[10:21|Then Jonathan put on the holy vestment|Et induit se Jonathas stolam sanctam]], that is, the pontifical vesture. For Alexander not only made him high priest[[10:20||]], but also sent him the vestment, as Josephus narrates, although the text does not say so. [[10:21|at the feast day of the tabernacles|In die solenni Scenopegiæ]] [*Scenopegia*, "the pitching of tents", is the Greek name of the feast of Tabernacles]: that is, of the dedication of the first temple, built by Solomon, as one expounds it; which explanation is shown to be unfit, because in the law the feast of Scenopegia is commonly understood as the feast of Tabernacles. Josephus too relates: Jonathan, receiving Alexander's letter, put on the priestly vestment, as the feast of Tabernacles was at hand. The feast of Scenopegia, moreover, fell in the seventh month, as appears in Leviticus[[Lev 23:34||]]; and of this month Scripture speaks here, saying, [[10:21|Then Jonathan put on the holy vestment in the seventh month|Et induit se Jonathas stolam sanctam septimo mense]]. Yet he himself consecrated that vestment sent by the king before he used it in the service of God.

paras.t: Et audivit Demetrius verba ista, quod scilicet Alexander scripsit et munera contulit Jonathæ, et ait consiliariis suis: Quid hoc fecimus, id est, cur ita habuimus nos, quod hæc fieri permisimus, quod præoccupavit nos Alexander apprehendere amicitiam Judæorum ad munimen sui, id est ad suam protectionem et opem? Scribam et ego illis verba deprecatoria et dignitates et dona, ut sint mecum in adjutorium. Et scripsit Demetrius eis, Jonathæ ac populo ejus, in hæc verba: Quoniam servastis ad nos pactum, et mansistis in amicitia nostra, et non accessistis ad inimicos nostros per confœderationem, gavisi sumus, etc. Hæc falsa erant et ficta, ut Jonathas erubesceret non adhærere Demetrio. Et remittemus vobis præstationes multas, id est multa quæ nobis dare solebatis certis temporibus: imo dabimus vobis donationes, id est munera.
paras.en: [[10:22|And Demetrius heard these words|Et audivit Demetrius verba ista]], namely that Alexander had written and given gifts to Jonathan, [[10:22|and said|et ait]] to his counsellors: [[10:23|What is this that we have done|Quid hoc fecimus]], that is, why have we behaved so as to let this happen, [[10:23|that Alexander hath prevented us to gain the friendship of the Jews to strengthen himself|quod præoccupavit nos Alexander apprehendere amicitiam Judæorum ad munimen sui]], that is, for his protection and help? [[10:24|I also will write to them words of request, and offer dignities, and gifts: that they may be with me to aid me|Scribam et ego illis verba deprecatoria et dignitates et dona, ut sint mecum in adjutorium]]. [[10:25|And he wrote to them in these words|Et scripsit Demetrius eis, Jonathæ ac populo ejus, in hæc verba]] (to them, that is, to Jonathan and his people): [[10:26|Whereas you have kept covenant with us, and have continued in our friendship, and have not joined with our enemies|Quoniam servastis ad nos pactum, et mansistis in amicitia nostra, et non accessistis ad inimicos nostros]] by alliance, [[10:26|and are glad|gavisi sumus]], etc. These things were false and feigned, so that Jonathan should be ashamed not to cleave to Demetrius. [[10:28|And we will remit to you many charges|Et remittemus vobis præstationes multas]], that is, many things that you used to give us at fixed times: nay, [[10:28|and will give you gifts|dabimus vobis donationes]], that is, presents.

paras.t: Et nunc absolvo vos et omnes Judæos in meo dominio commorantes, a tributis, et pretia salis indulgeo, id est pecunias quas solvistis pro sale, quod confecistis in terra nostra ex aqua maris, super quod pro parte sita est terra Judææ. Sicque aquæ de mari eductæ per alveos, super terram vertebantur in sal per solis calorem. Et coronas remitto, quas solvere consuevistis, et tertias seminis, id est tertias frugum partes. Merito ergo Esdras locutus est: Fructus ejus multiplicantur regibus, quos posuisti super nos. Et dimidiam partem fructus ligni, id est arborum, in totum tempus præsidentiæ meæ.
paras.en: [[10:29|And now I free you, and all the Jews|Et nunc absolvo vos et omnes Judæos]] dwelling in my dominion, [[10:29|from tributes|a tributis]], [[10:29|and I release you from the customs of salt|et pretia salis indulgeo]], that is, the money you paid for the salt which you made in our land from the water of the sea, on which the land of Judea partly lies. And so the waters drawn from the sea through channels were turned into salt on the land by the heat of the sun. [[10:29|and remit the crowns|Et coronas remitto]], which you were accustomed to pay, [[10:29|and the thirds of the seed|et tertias seminis]], that is, the third parts of the crops. Rightly, then, did Esdras say: [[2 Esd 9:37|the fruits thereof grow up for the kings, whom thou hast set over us|Fructus ejus multiplicantur regibus, quos posuisti super nos]]. [[10:30|And the half of the fruit of trees|Et dimidiam partem fructus ligni]], that is, of the trees, [[10:30|for ever|in totum tempus præsidentiæ meæ]] [literally "for the whole time of my rule"].

paras.t: Et Jerusalem sit sancta, id est, Dei cultus exerceatur in ea et in templo ipsius, et libera a tributis; et decimæ et tributa, quæ nobis solvere solent, ipsius sint, id est, ei remaneant pro bono ejus communi. Remitto etiam potestatem arcis, ita ut nullus in ea moretur contra Jonathæ voluntatem. Ideo additur, et do eam summo sacerdoti, non simpliciter, sed ut constituat in ea viros quoscumque ipse voluerit, qui molestiam non ingerant intrantibus templum; qui custodiant eam pro rege, ut Josephus addit: quod et verbis sequentis concordat capituli. Et omnem animam, id est personam, Judæorum captivam in omni regno meo, relinquo liberam gratis.
paras.en: [[10:31|And let Jerusalem be holy|Et Jerusalem sit sancta]], that is, let the worship of God be exercised in it and in its temple, [[10:31|and free|et libera]] from tributes; [[10:31|and let the tenths, and tributes|et decimæ et tributa]], which they are accustomed to pay us, [[10:31|be for itself|ipsius sint]], that is, remain to it for its common good. [[10:32|I yield up also the power of the castle|Remitto etiam potestatem arcis]], so that no one may stay in it against Jonathan's will. Therefore it is added, [[10:32|and I give it to the high priest|et do eam summo sacerdoti]], not absolutely, but [[10:32|to place therein such men as he shall choose|ut constituat in ea viros quoscumque ipse voluerit]], who may not trouble those entering the temple; [[10:32|to keep it|qui custodiant eam]] for the king, as Josephus adds: which also agrees with the words of the following chapter. [[10:33|And every soul|Et omnem animam]], that is, person, [[10:33|of the Jews|Judæorum]] held captive [[10:33|in all my kingdom, I set at liberty freely|in omni regno meo, relinquo liberam gratis]].

paras.t: Et omnes dies solennes, id est majora festa, ut Paschæ, Pentecostes, Tabernaculorum et Tubarum, quæ semel venerunt in anno, et sabbata in omni hebdomada venientia, et neomeniæ, id est festa in exordiis mensium celebranda, et dies decreti, id est, pro celebrandis festivitatibus ex certis casibus instituti seu ordinati, quemadmodum dies Sortium pro interfectione Aman liberationeque Judæorum, et dies victoriæ Judith, et tres dies ante diem solennem, id est præcipuam legis solennitatem, et tres dies post eam. Josephus vero ait pluraliter, Ante eos, et, Post eos: et sic per diem solennem forsitan designantur solennes dies semel in anno venientes. Solennitas autem Paschæ et Tabernaculorum duravit septem diebus, prout in Levitico habetur. Sint omnes dies immunitatis ab exactione, et remissionis a vectigalibus, omnibus Judæis qui sunt in regno meo; et nemo habebit potestatem agere aliquid contra Judæos in foro contentioso, et movere negotia adversus aliquem eorum in omni causa, id est quacumque, in prætactis diebus.
paras.en: [[10:34|And I will that all the feasts|Et omnes dies solennes]], that is, the greater feasts, such as those of the Pasch, of Pentecost, of Tabernacles and of Trumpets, which come once in the year, [[10:34|and the sabbaths|et sabbata]] that come every week, [[10:34|and the new moons|et neomeniæ]], that is, the feasts to be kept at the beginnings of the months, [[10:34|and the days appointed|et dies decreti]], that is, those instituted or ordained for keeping feasts on account of particular events, such as the days of Lots for the slaying of Aman and the deliverance of the Jews[[Esth 9:21||]], and the day of the victory of Judith[[Jdt 16:31||]], [[10:34|and three days before the solemn day|et tres dies ante diem solennem]], that is, the chief solemnity of the law, [[10:34|and three days after|et tres dies post]] it. Josephus, however, says in the plural, *before them* and *after them*: and so perhaps by *the solemn day* are meant the solemn days that come once in the year. Now the solemnity of the Pasch and of Tabernacles lasted seven days, as is had in Leviticus[[Lev 23:6||]][[Lev 23:8||]][[Lev 23:34||]]. [[10:34|be all days of immunity and freedom, for all the Jews that are in my kingdom|sint omnes immunitatis et remissionis omnibus Judæis, qui sunt in regno meo]] (immunity, that is, from exaction, and freedom from customs); [[10:35|And no man shall have power to do any thing|et nemo habebit potestatem agere aliquid]] against the Jews in the contentious court [that is, by a lawsuit], [[10:35|or to molest any of them, in any cause|et movere negotia adversus aliquem eorum in omni causa]] (*any*, that is, whatsoever), on the days aforesaid.

paras.t: Et ascribantur ex Judæis in exercitu regis ad negotia bellica, pro defensione reipublicæ, qui sint quasi milites et stipendiarii regis, et præcipui defensores Judæorum in regno meo manentium, usque ad triginta millia virorum. Et dabuntur illis copiæ, id est necessaria ad sua officia peragenda, ut arma, stipendia aut consimilia, ut oportet dari omnibus exercitibus regis; et ex ipsis triginta millibus Judæorum, ordinabuntur aliqui per principes meos, qui sint custodes et propugnatores in munitionibus regis magnis, id est fortalitiis. Et ex his constituentur qui sint super negotia regni, id est aliqui officiati ad expediendum negotia, quæ aguntur ex fide, id est, qui tantæ sint reputationis, quod eis credatur, et ambulent in legitimis suis, sicut præcepit rex in terra Juda, id est, ubique in regno meo permittantur vivere secundum legem patrum suorum, sicut præcepi eos permitti sic vivere in Judæa.
paras.en: [[10:36|And let there be enrolled in the king's army|Et ascribantur ex Judæis in exercitu regis]] men of the Jews for warlike affairs, for the defence of the commonwealth, who are to be as it were the king's soldiers and paid men, and the chief defenders of the Jews dwelling in my kingdom, [[10:36|to the number of thirty thousand|usque ad triginta millia virorum]]. [[10:36|and allowance shall be made them|Et dabuntur illis copiæ]], that is, what they need to carry out their duties, such as arms, pay and the like, [[10:36|as is due to all the king's forces|ut oportet dari omnibus exercitibus regis]]; and of these thirty thousand Jews [[10:36|certain of them shall be appointed|ordinabuntur aliqui]] by my princes, to be guards and defenders [[10:36|in the fortresses of the great king|in munitionibus regis magnis]] [Denis's text has *regis magnis*, "in the king's great fortresses"], that is, in the strongholds. [[10:37|And some of them shall be set over the affairs of the kingdom|Et ex his constituentur qui sint super negotia regni]], that is, certain officers to dispatch business, [[10:37|that are of trust|quæ aguntur ex fide]], that is, men of such repute that they are believed; [[10:37|and let them walk in their own laws, as the king hath commanded in the land of Juda|et ambulent in legitimis suis, sicut præcepit rex in terra Juda]], that is, let them be allowed everywhere in my kingdom to live according to the law of their fathers, as I have commanded that they be allowed so to live in Judea.

paras.t: Et tres civitates quæ additæ sunt Judææ ex regione Samariæ, cum Judæa reputentur, tanquam de jure pertinentes ad eam, ut sint sub uno, scilicet principe sacerdotum. Ideo subditur, et non obediant alienæ potestati, nisi summo sacerdoti. Judæi namque post reditum a Babylone per pontifices regebantur. Ptolemaida et confines urbes ejus, quas dedi donum sanctis qui sunt in Jerusalem, id est ministris templi, sacerdotibus ac Levitis, ad necessarios sumptus sanctorum, id est ministrorum illorum divinis consecratorum.
paras.en: [[10:38|And the three cities that are added to Judea, out of the country of Samaria, let them be accounted with Judea|Et tres civitates quæ additæ sunt Judææ ex regione Samariæ, cum Judæa reputentur]], as belonging to it by right, [[10:38|that they may be under one|ut sint sub uno]], namely the chief of the priests. Therefore it is added, [[10:38|and obey no other authority but that of the high priest|et non obediant alienæ potestati, nisi summo sacerdoti]]. For the Jews, after the return from Babylon, were ruled by pontiffs. [[10:39|Ptolemais and the confines thereof, I give as a free gift to the holy places that are in Jerusalem|Ptolemaida et confines urbes ejus, quas dedi donum sanctis qui sunt in Jerusalem]], that is, to the ministers of the temple, the priests and Levites, [[10:39|for the necessary charges of the holy things|ad necessarios sumptus sanctorum]], that is, of those ministers consecrated to divine things [the Latin *sancti*, "holy ones", can mean holy places or things, or holy persons; Denis takes it of the ministers].

paras.t: Et ego singulis annis dabo ad sacrificia aut consimilia, quindecim millia siclorum argenti, id est tantam pecuniam. Siclus autem, ut in lege habetur, viginti obolos habet. Sed sicli erant diversi. De rationibus regis, id est de rebus et bonis ad me de jure spectantibus. Et omne quod reliquum fuerit, dabunt qui præsunt negotiis in opera domus, id est ad ea quæ necessaria sunt in templo. Et super, id est ultra hæc quinque millia siclorum quæ accipiebant officiati mei pro me, vel alii reges, de sanctorum ratione, id est de pertinentibus ad templi ministros, vel ad templum, ad sacerdotes pertineant, qui ministerio sacerdotali funguntur. Et quicumque confugerint in templum, et in omnibus finibus ejus, id est infra septa ipsius, obnoxii regi in omni negotio, id est adstricti ad satisfaciendum mihi pro culpa quacumque, dimittantur; et universa quæ sunt, id est attinent, eis, libera habeant. Et ad ædificanda vel restauranda opera sanctorum, id est ædificia templi et appendicias ejus, sumptus dabuntur de ratione, id est reditibus, regis.
paras.en: [[10:40|And I give every year|Et ego singulis annis dabo]] for sacrifices or the like [[10:40|fifteen thousand sickles of silver|quindecim millia siclorum argenti]], that is, so much money. Now, as is had in the law, [[Ex 30:13|A sicle hath twenty obols|Siclus autem, ut in lege habetur, viginti obolos habet]]. But sicles were of different kinds. [[10:40|out of the king's accounts|De rationibus regis]], that is, from the things and goods belonging to me by right. [[10:41|And all that is above|Et omne quod reliquum fuerit]], let those [[10:41|that were over the affairs|qui præsunt negotiis]] give [[10:41|to the works of the house|in opera domus]], that is, for the things that are needed in the temple. [[10:42|Moreover|Et super]], that is, beyond these, [[10:42|the five thousand sickles|quinque millia siclorum]] which my officers, or other kings, used to receive for me [[10:42|from the account of the holy places|de sanctorum ratione]], that is, from what belongs to the ministers of the temple, or to the temple, [[10:42|shall also belong to the priests that execute the ministry|ad sacerdotes pertineant, qui ministerio sacerdotali funguntur]]. [[10:43|And whosoever shall flee into the temple|Et quicumque confugerint in templum]], [[10:43|and in all the borders thereof|et in omnibus finibus ejus]], that is, within its precincts, [[10:43|being indebted to the king for any matter|obnoxii regi in omni negotio]], that is, bound to give me satisfaction for any fault whatever, [[10:43|let them be set at liberty|dimittantur]]; [[10:43|and all that they have|et universa quæ sunt, id est attinent, eis]] (that is, all that belongs to them), [[10:43|let them have it free|libera habeant]]. [[10:44|For the building also, or repairing the works of the holy places|Et ad ædificanda vel restauranda opera sanctorum]], that is, the buildings of the temple and its appurtenances, [[10:44|the charges shall be given out of the king's revenues|sumptus dabuntur de ratione, id est reditibus, regis]] [literally "out of the king's account", which Denis explains as his revenues].

paras.t: Ut autem audivit Jonathas et populus ejus sermones istos, non crediderunt eis: nam ficti erant et blandi, ex timore prolati. Et complacuit eis in Alexandrum, qui ex sinceritate quadam scripsit et contulit eis; quia ipse fuerat eis princeps sermonum pacis, id est præcipuus repromissor atque exhibitor verborum pacificorum, non loquens nec scribens eis dolose, et ipsi Alexandro auxilium ferebant omnibus diebus opportunis. Circa hoc quæritur, an in hoc bene egerunt. Et apparet quod non: quoniam Alexander iste non habuit jus ad possidendum hoc regnum Demetrii. Fuit enim ex semine Antiochi Illustris qui regnum invasit, expulso filio fratris sui senioris Seleuci, cui regnum competebat de jure, ratione primogenituræ. Quid ad hanc respondendum sit quæstionem, non video, nisi forsan quod Demetrius ob suam in Judæos tyrannidem, et ob alia crimina meruerit regno privari.
paras.en: [[10:46|Now when Jonathan and the people heard these words, they gave no credit to them|Ut autem audivit Jonathas et populus ejus sermones istos, non crediderunt eis]]: for they were feigned and flattering, uttered out of fear. [[10:47|And their inclinations were towards Alexander|Et complacuit eis in Alexandrum]], who had written and given to them with a certain sincerity; [[10:47|because he had been the chief promoter of peace in their regard|quia ipse fuerat eis princeps sermonum pacis]] [literally "the prince of the words of peace"], that is, the foremost promiser and offerer of peaceable words, not speaking or writing to them deceitfully, [[10:47|and him they always helped|et ipsi Alexandro auxilium ferebant omnibus diebus]], whenever occasion served. On this it is asked whether they did well in this. And it seems that they did not: since this Alexander had no right to possess this kingdom of Demetrius. For he was of the seed of Antiochus the Illustrious, who seized the kingdom, driving out the son of his elder brother Seleucus, to whom the kingdom belonged by right of primogeniture. What answer is to be made to this question I do not see, unless perhaps that Demetrius, for his tyranny against the Jews and for other crimes, had deserved to be deprived of the kingdom.

paras.t: Et congregavit Alexander rex exercitum magnum, et admovit castra contra Demetrium. Et commiserunt prælium duo reges, et fugit exercitus Demetrii, etc. Et cecidit, id est occisus est, Demetrius in die illa. Circa hoc Josephus scribit: Demetrius fortiter pugnans, non paucos hostium prostravit. Quumque fugans alios equus ejus cœni barathro, id est profundi luto, inhæsisset, minime fugere valens occiditur. Videntes etenim hostes quod ei accidisset, reversi circumdederunt eum: et omnibus in eum jacula destinantibus, quum ipse pedestris fortiter resisteret, postea perfossus vulneribus lapsus est.
paras.en: [[10:48|And king Alexander gathered together a great army, and moved his camp near to Demetrius|Et congregavit Alexander rex exercitum magnum, et admovit castra contra Demetrium]]. [[10:49|And the two kings joined battle, and the army of Demetrius fled away|Et commiserunt prælium duo reges, et fugit exercitus Demetrii]], etc. [[10:50|and Demetrius was slain that day|Et cecidit, id est occisus est, Demetrius in die illa]] [literally "fell", which Denis explains as "was slain"]. On this Josephus writes: Demetrius, fighting bravely, laid low not a few of the enemy. And as he was pursuing others, his horse stuck in a pit of mire, that is, in deep mud, and being unable to flee he was slain. For the enemy, seeing what had befallen him, turned back and surrounded him; and as all were aiming their darts at him, while he on foot resisted bravely, at length, pierced with wounds, he fell.

paras.t: Et misit Alexander ad Ptolemæum regem Ægypti legatos, dicens: Quoniam regressus sum ad regnum meum, etc. Et nunc statuamus ad invicem amicitiam, et da mihi filiam tuam uxorem: quod Ptolemæus libenter fecit. Et scripsit Alexander Jonathæ, ut veniret sibi obviam in Ptolemaida civitate. Quo quum Jonathas pervenisset, dedit Alexandro ac Ptolemæo munera pretiosa et magna; et honoraverunt eum, præcipue Alexander, qui jussit eum purpura mox vestiri ac secum sedere, et primum esse amicorum suorum, ac ducem atque participem principatus. Denique, sicut in Scholastica fertur historia, quatuor sunt insignia regalia, scilicet purpura, fibula aurea, diadema, et sceptrum.
paras.en: [[10:51|And Alexander sent ambassadors to Ptolemee king of Egypt|Et misit Alexander ad Ptolemæum regem Ægypti legatos]], [[10:51|saying|dicens]]: [[10:52|Forasmuch as I am returned into my kingdom|Quoniam regressus sum ad regnum meum]], etc. [[10:54|Now, therefore, let us make friendship one with another: and give me now thy daughter to wife|Et nunc statuamus ad invicem amicitiam, et da mihi filiam tuam uxorem]]: which Ptolemee willingly did[[10:58||]]. [[10:59|And king Alexander wrote to Jonathan, that he should come and meet him|Et scripsit Alexander Jonathæ, ut veniret sibi obviam]] at the city of Ptolemais. When Jonathan had come there, he gave Alexander and Ptolemee precious and great gifts[[10:60||]]; and they honoured him, especially Alexander, who ordered him at once to be clothed in purple and to sit with him[[10:62||]], and to be first among his friends, and made him [[10:65|governor, and partaker of his dominion|ducem atque participem principatus]]. Lastly, as is related in the *Scholastic History*, there are four royal insignia, namely the purple, the golden buckle, the diadem, and the sceptre.

paras.t: Consequenter describitur bellum Jonathæ contra Demetrium prætacti Demetrii filium. In anno centesimo sexagesimo quinto venit Demetrius filius Demetrii a Creta civitate: de qua ex parte matris fuerat oriundus; ideo patre suo occiso, illuc confugit. In urbe illa postea fuit archiepiscopus ipse Titus apostoli Pauli discipulus. Jupiter quoque fuit rex Cretæ. De Cretensibus vero allegat Apostolus illud poetæ: Cretenses semper mendaces, malæ bestiæ, ventres pigri. Et audivit Alexander adventum Demetrii, et contristatus est valde, timens ab illo vastari, quia Demetrius ille fuit de linea regalis prosapiæ, ex semine primogeniti magni Antiochi, et reversus est Alexander Antiochiam regni sui metropolim. Et constituit Demetrius Apollonium ducem, et congregavit exercitum magnum, ut in primis expugnaret Jonathan, quem scivit Alexandro fortiter confœderatum; et accessit ad Jamniam in Judæa prope mare sitam, et misit ad Jonathan ipse Demetrius rex, vel Apollonius ex parte ipsius, [dicens]:
paras.en: Next is described the war of Jonathan against Demetrius, the son of the Demetrius already mentioned. [[10:67|In the year one hundred and sixty-five, Demetrius, the son of Demetrius, came from Crete|In anno centesimo sexagesimo quinto venit Demetrius filius Demetrii a Creta]], the city, from which he was descended on his mother's side; and so, when his father was slain, he fled there. In that city Titus himself, the disciple of the apostle Paul, was afterwards archbishop[[Tit 1:5||]] [the margin reads Tit. i, 9 (?); Titus is left in Crete at Tit 1:5]. Jupiter too was king of Crete. And of the Cretans the Apostle cites that saying of the poet: [[Tit 1:12|The Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, slothful bellies|Cretenses semper mendaces, malæ bestiæ, ventres pigri]]. [[10:68|And king Alexander heard of it|Et audivit Alexander adventum Demetrii]] (of the coming of Demetrius), [[10:68|and was much troubled|et contristatus est valde]], fearing to be laid waste by him, because that Demetrius was of the line of the royal stock, of the seed of the firstborn of Antiochus the Great, [[10:68|and returned to Antioch|et reversus est Alexander Antiochiam]], the metropolis of his kingdom. [[10:69|And king Demetrius made Apollonius his general|Et constituit Demetrius Apollonium ducem]], [[10:69|and he gathered together a great army|et congregavit exercitum magnum]], to attack first of all Jonathan, whom he knew to be firmly allied to Alexander; [[10:69|and came to Jamnia|et accessit ad Jamniam]] in Judea, which lies near the sea, [[10:69|and he sent to Jonathan|et misit ad Jonathan]], King Demetrius himself, or Apollonius on his behalf, saying:

paras.t: Tu solus resistis nobis, id est, præcipue impedis nos, roborando audaciam Alexandri. Ego autem factus sum in derisum et in opprobrium ab Alexandro et suis, qui occupant terram patrum meorum, nec me volunt recipere, et etiam a te et tuis, propterea quia tu potestatem exerces adversus nos in montibus, id est quod in locis montanis, et in urbibus fortalitiisque hujusmodi confidis, ad quæ difficile est ascendere, præsertim equitibus. Nunc ergo si confidis in virtutibus tuis, id est robore tui exercitus, seu corporalibus viribus, aut justitiis, quibus facta tua coloras, descende ad nos in campum, ut in loco plano præliis apto pugnemus; quia mecum est virtus bellorum, id est fortitudo exercitus atque industria præliandi. Interroga, et disce quis sum ego: quasi dicat, Si excellentiam meam perpenderes, te mihi opponere non auderes. Loquitur autem comminatorie, præsumptuose, superbe, tanquam volens Jonathan perterrere: qui confidens in Domino magis quam in virtutibus suis, ex verbis tantæ improbitatis fuit magis ad magnanimitatem et confidentiam provocatus, sicut subjungitur.
paras.en: [[10:70|Thou alone standest against us|Tu solus resistis nobis]], that is, thou above all hinderest us, by strengthening the boldness of Alexander. [[10:70|and I am laughed at and reproached|Ego autem factus sum in derisum et in opprobrium]] by Alexander and his men, who occupy the land of my fathers and will not receive me, and also by thee and thine, [[10:70|because thou shewest thy power against us in the mountains|propterea quia tu potestatem exerces adversus nos in montibus]], that is, because thou trustest in mountainous places, and in cities and strongholds of that kind, which are hard to climb, especially for horsemen. [[10:71|Now, therefore, if thou trustest in thy forces|Nunc ergo si confidis in virtutibus tuis]], that is, in the strength of thy army, or in bodily powers, or in the just claims with which thou colourest thy deeds, [[10:71|come down to us into the plain|descende ad nos in campum]], that we may fight in a level place fit for battle; [[10:71|for with me is the strength of war|quia mecum est virtus bellorum]], that is, the strength of an army and skill in fighting. [[10:72|Ask, and learn who I am|Interroga, et disce quis sum ego]]: as if to say, If thou didst weigh my excellence, thou wouldst not dare to set thyself against me. He speaks threateningly, presumptuously, proudly, as one wishing to terrify Jonathan: who, trusting in the Lord more than in his own forces, was rather roused by words of such insolence to magnanimity and confidence, as is added.

paras.t: Ut audivit autem Jonathas sermones Apollonii ex ore nuntii seu ex epistola, motus est animo ad justam indignationem, et ad iram per zelum atque audaciam, quemadmodum David ex verbis Goliath. Erant namque devoti cultores veri Dei: in quo confidentes, verba idololatrarum spernebant. Et elegit Jonathas decem millia virorum, etc. Et applicuerunt Jonathas et Simon frater ejus cum exercitu suo, in Joppen, id est extra et prope Joppen: nam subditur, et exclusit eum a civitate, id est, populus in Joppe exsistens, portas clausit, ne Jonathas introiret cum suis; quia custodia Apollonii Joppe erat, id est, milites ab Apollonio constituti in urbe illa, ad succurrendum sibi tempore opportuno; et oppugnavit Jonathas eam. Et exterriti qui erant in civitate, ne caperet eam et ipsos occideret, aperuerunt ei. Et prælium commiserunt contra se invicem Jonathas et Apollonius, non statim tunc, sed paulo post.
paras.en: [[10:74|Now when Jonathan heard the words of Apollonius|Ut audivit autem Jonathas sermones Apollonii]], from the mouth of a messenger or from a letter, [[10:74|he was moved in his mind|motus est animo]] to just indignation, and to anger through zeal and boldness, as David was by the words of Goliath[[1 Kings 17:26||]][[1 Kings 17:36||]][[1 Kings 17:45||]]. For they were devout worshippers of the true God, and trusting in him they despised the words of idolaters. [[10:74|and he chose ten thousand men|Et elegit Jonathas decem millia virorum]], etc. [[10:75|And they pitched their tents near Joppe|et applicuerunt castra in Joppen]] (Jonathan, that is, and Simon his brother with their army), that is, outside and near Joppe: for it is added, [[10:75|but they shut him out of the city|et exclusit eum a civitate]], that is, the people in Joppe shut the gates, so that Jonathan should not enter with his men; [[10:75|because a garrison of Apollonius was in Joppe|quia custodia Apollonii Joppe erat]], that is, soldiers placed by Apollonius in that city to help him at a fitting time; [[10:75|and he laid siege to it|et oppugnavit Jonathas eam]]. [[10:76|And they that were in the city being affrighted|Et exterriti qui erant in civitate]], lest he should take it and kill them, [[10:76|opened the gates to him|aperuerunt ei]]. [[10:78|and they joined battle|Et prælium commiserunt]], Jonathan and Apollonius, against each other, not at once then, but a little after.

paras.t: Et cognovit Jonathas, quoniam sunt insidiæ post se, id est, quod Apollonius aliquos dimisisset occulte, qui a tergo invaderent Jonathan et suos tempore prælii. Et circuierunt Jonathas et sui castra ejus, puta Apollonii, antequam pugnaverunt, ne includerentur a viris Apollonii, et jecerunt milites et sagittarii Apollonii jacula in populum Jonathæ, a mane usque ad vesperam. Populus autem stabat sicut præcepit Jonathas; et laboraverunt equi eorum, videlicet militum Apollonii. Circa hoc Josephus scribit: Jonathas suis præcepit, sagittas equitum testudine facta excipere. Quod quum fecissent, nihil lædebantur, quamvis hostes super eos frequentia tela vibrarent, usquequo suas evacuassent sagittas: nam sagittæ corpora clypeis septa minime contingebant, quum constipatione testudinis tela venientia refugarentur. Et ejecit, id est, ad bellandum repente direxit, Simon exercitum suum, videns adversarios jam lassatos, et commisit contra legionem pedestrem, quibus equites non valebant multum succurrere. Propter quod subditur: Equites enim fatigati erant sagittando. Et contriti sunt ab eo, id est a Simone, hi qui erant in legione, et fugerunt. Et intraverunt in Bethdagon idolum suum, id est in domum seu templum Dagon dei vel idoli sui, ut se, id est eos, liberaret. Et accendit Jonathas Azotum, et templum illud cum exsistentibus in se. Et fuerunt qui ceciderunt gladio, fere octo millia virorum.
paras.en: [[10:80|And Jonathan knew that there was an ambush behind him|Et cognovit Jonathas, quoniam sunt insidiæ post se]], that is, that Apollonius had secretly left some men to attack Jonathan and his men from behind at the time of the battle. [[10:80|and they surrounded his army|Et circuierunt Jonathas et sui castra ejus]] (Jonathan, that is, and his men surrounded the camp of Apollonius) before they fought, so as not to be shut in by the men of Apollonius; [[10:80|and cast darts at the people|et jecerunt jacula in populum]] (the soldiers and archers of Apollonius, at Jonathan's people), [[10:80|from morning till evening|a mane usque ad vesperam]]. [[10:81|But the people stood still, as Jonathan had commanded them|Populus autem stabat sicut præcepit Jonathas]]: [[10:81|and so their horses were fatigued|et laboraverunt equi eorum]], namely those of the soldiers of Apollonius. On this Josephus writes: Jonathan ordered his men to form a tortoise and receive the arrows of the horsemen. And when they had done so, they took no hurt, though the enemy hurled weapons thick upon them, until they had used up their arrows: for the arrows did not reach their bodies, fenced as they were with shields, since the weapons that came were beaten back by the close-packed tortoise. [[10:82|Then Simon drew forth his army|Et ejecit, id est, ad bellandum repente direxit, Simon exercitum suum]] (*drew forth*, that is, suddenly led it to battle), seeing the adversaries already weary, [[10:82|and attacked the legion|et commisit contra legionem]] of foot, which the horsemen could not much help. Therefore it is added: [[10:82|for the horsemen were wearied|Equites enim fatigati erant]] with shooting. [[10:82|and they were discomfited by him|Et contriti sunt ab eo]], that is, by Simon, those who were in the legion, [[10:82|and fled|et fugerunt]]. [[10:83|and went into Bethdagon, their idol's temple|Et intraverunt in Bethdagon idolum suum]], that is, into the house or temple of Dagon, their god or idol, [[10:83|there to save themselves|ut se, id est eos, liberaret]] [Denis's text has *ut se liberaret*, which he takes with the idol as subject: "that it might save them"]. [[10:84|But Jonathan set fire to Azotus|Et accendit Jonathas Azotum]], and that temple with those who were in it. [[10:85|So they that were slain by the sword|Et fuerunt qui ceciderunt gladio]] were [[10:85|almost eight thousand men|fere octo millia virorum]].

paras.t: Et movit inde Jonathas castra, et applicuit ea Ascalonem, quæ fuit una de quinque principalibus urbibus Philistinorum; et exierunt obviam illi, videlicet Jonathæ, in magna gloria, non audentes se ei opponere.
paras.en: [[10:86|And Jonathan, removed his army from thence|Et movit inde Jonathas castra]] [[10:86|and camped against Ascalon|et applicuit ea Ascalonem]], which was one of the five chief cities of the Philistines; [[10:86|and they went out|et exierunt]] [[10:86|to meet him with great honour|obviam illi, videlicet Jonathæ, in magna gloria]], not daring to set themselves against him.

paras.t: Et ut audivit Alexander rex sermones istos, addidit adhuc glorificare Jonathan ad regratiandum ei, quia expugnavit adversarios Alexandri. Et misit ei fibulam auream, sicut est consuetudo dari cognatis regum. Josephus dicit, Torquem auream. Porro jam supra in isto capitulo dictum est, quod misit Jonathæ purpuram, aureamque coronam. Quumque juxta præhabita, sint quatuor insignia regalia, patet quod misit Jonathæ tria, quartum (scilicet sceptrum) sibi reservans. Et dedit ei Accaron, unam quinque principalium civitatum Philistiim, et omnes fines ejus, id est urbes et villas Accaroni confines, in possessionem.
paras.en: And it came to pass, [[10:88|when Alexander, the king heard these words|ut audivit Alexander rex sermones istos]], [[10:88|that he honoured Jonathan yet more|addidit adhuc glorificare Jonathan]] [literally "he added yet to glorify Jonathan"], to thank him, because he had overcome the adversaries of Alexander. [[10:89|And he sent him a buckle of gold, as the custom is, to be given to such as are of the royal blood|Et misit ei fibulam auream, sicut est consuetudo dari cognatis regum]]. Josephus says, *a golden collar*. Moreover it was said above in this chapter that he sent Jonathan the purple and a golden crown[[10:20||]]. And since, as was said before, there are four royal insignia, it is plain that he sent Jonathan three, keeping the fourth (namely the sceptre) for himself. [[10:89|And he gave him Accaron|Et dedit ei Accaron]], one of the five chief cities of the Philistines, [[10:89|and all the borders thereof|et omnes fines ejus]], that is, the cities and towns bordering on Accaron, [[10:89|in possession|in possessionem]].
